title: Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal: Scaffolding, Harness, Context Engineering, and Lessons Learned
finding: OPENDEV is a Rust terminal coding agent with model routing, planning split, lazy tool discovery and adaptive context compaction; the abstract reports no measurements.

title: Safety Under Scaffolding: How Evaluation Conditions Shape Measured Safety
finding: Benchmark choice explains 15.1% of outcome variation, scaffold architecture 0.5%; answer format shifts measured safety 5-20 percentage points; composite reliability G = 0.251.

title: Test-Driven AI Agent Definition (TDAD): Compiling Tool-Using Agents from Behavioral Specifications
finding: TDAD compiles agent prompts from behavioral specifications into executable tests; across 24 trials it reaches 92% compilation success, 97% mean hidden pass rate, and 86-100% mutation scores.

title: Quantifying the Accuracy and Cost Impact of Design Decisions in Budget-Constrained Agentic LLM Search
finding: Across six models and three question-answering benchmarks, extra searches help only up to a small cap, and hybrid retrieval with re-ranking gave the largest average gains.

title: Exploring the Agentic Frontier of Verilog Code Generation
finding: Naive agent wrapping degraded frontier models' Verilog generation, while structured harnesses matched or beat non-agentic baselines; open-source models lagged on crash rates and tool output reading.

title: Agentic Harness for Real-World Compilers
finding: llvm-harness lifts five frontier models on compiler bug repair by 62%; a tailored mini agent beats the enhanced state-of-the-art agent by 22% on a 334-bug benchmark.

title: Herding CATs: ALARA for Agent Harness Engineering in Portable Composable Multi-Agent Teams
finding: Plain-text files declare each agent's tool access; 22 local models from 0.6B to 35B parameters ran 115 tasks across roughly 2500 executions, with failures varying by model family.

title: Efficient Benchmarking of AI Agents
finding: Evaluating agents only on tasks with 30-70% historical pass rates cuts task count by 44-70% and keeps rankings accurate; random task sampling showed high variance across seeds.

title: Coherence Collapse: Diagnosing Why Code Agents Fail After Reaching the Right Code
finding: Trajectory decomposition across 16,758 runs shows 60-69% of capable-model failures reach and edit correct functions yet produce wrong patches; agents often overwrite correct code.

title: Natural-Language Agent Harnesses
finding: Harness policies written as editable natural-language documents run on a shared runtime reach outcomes comparable to code-based harnesses, with much shorter static policies.

title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
finding: An outer-loop search over harness code improves text classification by 7.7 points over a leading context manager while using 4x fewer context tokens.

title: GEMS: Agent-Native Multimodal Generation with Memory and Skills
finding: Agent loop, persistent memory and on-demand skills let a lightweight 6B model surpass Nano Banana 2 on GenEval2.

title: AEC-Bench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Agentic Systems in Architecture, Engineering, and Construction
finding: A multimodal benchmark for agent systems in architecture, engineering and construction; harness design techniques improved performance across foundation models in base harnesses like Claude Code and Codex.

title: View-oriented Conversation Compiler for Agent Trace Analysis
finding: Compiles raw agent logs into three views; on AppWorld it adds 1.1 to 4.2 points of goal pass rate and cuts reflector tokens by one half to two thirds.

title: In harmony with gpt-oss
finding: A native harness reproduced gpt-oss-20b scores: 60.4% on SWE Verified HIGH (published 60.7%), 53.3% MEDIUM (53.2%), 91.7% on AIME25 with tools (90.4%).

title: REAP: Automatic Curation of Coding Agent Benchmarks from Interactive Production Usage
finding: Pipeline builds a coding benchmark from real developer sessions with multi-run stability checks; across five frontier models solve rates range 42.9% to 58.2%.

title: SkVM: Revisiting Language VM for Skills across Heterogenous LLMs and Harnesses
finding: Compiles skills per model-harness pair using capability profiles; across eight models and three harnesses it raises task completion, cuts tokens up to 40% and speeds up to 3.2 times.

title: FermiLink: An Agent Harness for Multidomain Scientific Simulations
finding: Open-source harness for high performance computing simulations reproduced 74 of 132 published figures (56.1%) with Codex; 30 matched with high fidelity.

title: Inside the Scaffold: A Source-Code Taxonomy of Coding Agent Architectures
finding: Source-code taxonomy of 13 open-source coding agent scaffolds across 12 dimensions; 11 of 13 compose multiple loop primitives, and context compaction spans seven strategies.

title: DebugHarness: Emulating Human Dynamic Debugging for Autonomous Program Repair
finding: Debugging agent queries a live runtime to repair memory-safety bugs; it patches about 90% of SEC-bench vulnerabilities, a relative gain of over 30% on state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Synthetic Sandbox for Training Machine Learning Engineering Agents
finding: Synthetic machine learning environments with 50-200 samples each cut execution time over 13 times, enabling on-policy reinforcement learning; relative medal-rate gains of 20.3-66.9% over supervised fine-tuning baselines.

title: ClawsBench: Evaluating Capability and Safety of LLM Productivity Agents in Simulated Workspaces
finding: Mock productivity services with deterministic snapshot and restore; across six models and four harnesses, full scaffolding gives 39-64% task success but 7-33% unsafe action rates.

title: How Much Heavy Lifting Can an Agent Harness Do?: Measuring the LLM's Residual Role in a Planning Agent
finding: Across 54 games, declarative planning added 24.1 percentage points of win rate over a belief-only harness with zero language model calls; model-backed revision activated on 4.3% of turns.

title: Harnessing Embodied Agents: Runtime Governance for Policy-Constrained Execution
finding: Runtime governance layer outside the agent intercepted 96.2% of unauthorized actions over 1000 simulated trials and cut unsafe continuation under drift from 100% to 22.2%.

title: Externalization in LLM Agents: A Unified Review of Memory, Skills, Protocols and Harness Engineering
finding: Review arguing memory, skills, protocols and harness engineering externalize cognitive burdens from models, tracing a progression from weights to context to harness; reports no measurements.

title: VCAO: Verifier-Centered Agentic Orchestration for Strategic OS Vulnerability Discovery
finding: Game-theoretic orchestration of a reasoning model and verifier tools finds 2.7 times more validated kernel vulnerabilities per budget than coverage-only fuzzing, replaying 847 historical vulnerability records.

title: M$^\star$: Every Task Deserves Its Own Memory Harness
finding: Mstar evolves executable Python memory programs per task through reflective code evolution; they beat baselines on four tasks and show distinct processing mechanisms per domain.

title: ClawVM: Harness-Managed Virtual Memory for Stateful Tool-Using LLM Agents
finding: Virtual memory layer manages context as typed pages; across 12 real-session traces and stress tests it removes all policy-controllable faults within budget, adding under 50 microseconds per turn.

title: CocoaBench: Evaluating Unified Digital Agents in the Wild
finding: Benchmark of long-horizon tasks combining vision, search and coding, scored on final output; the best evaluated system reaches only 45.1% success, so agents remain far from reliable.

title: Problem Reductions at Scale: Agentic Integration of Computationally Hard Problems
finding: Harness engineering with layered verification let agents build a Rust library of over 100 problem types and 200 reduction rules in about three months.

title: SemaClaw: A Step Towards General-Purpose Personal AI Agents through Harness Engineering
finding: Open-source multi-agent personal assistant framework with directed-graph team orchestration, a permission bridge for behavioral safety and three-tier context management; no measurements reported.

title: AgentSPEX: An Agent SPecification and EXecution Language
finding: Workflow language with typed steps, loops, parallel execution and checkpoints, run inside a harness; a user study found it more interpretable than a popular existing framework.

title: The Semi-Executable Stack: Agentic Software Engineering and the Expanding Scope of SE
finding: Position paper proposing a six-ring model for software engineering that expands engineered artifacts to semi-executable ones; conceptual, with no empirical results.

title: Harness as an Asset: Enforcing Determinism via the Convergent AI Agent Framework (CAAF)
finding: Harness of formalized domain invariants enforced deterministically; claims reliability on commodity-tier models, supported by benchmarks and ablations, with no single pillar closing the controllability gap.

title: Clover: A Neural-Symbolic Agentic Harness with Stochastic Tree-of-Thoughts for Verified RTL Repair
finding: Clover fixes 96.8% of hardware design bugs within a time limit, covering 94% more bugs than pure traditional repair and 63% more than language-model-based baselines.

title: Compiling Deterministic Structure into SLM Harnesses
finding: Teacher compiles agent workflows into plans for a small model; compiled workflows reach 91.3% on GSM-Hard with m=5 and 99.3% with m=3, absolute gains of 26.3-34.3 points over prompt optimizers.

title: Terminal Wrench: A Dataset of 331 Reward-Hackable Environments and 3,632 Exploit Trajectories
finding: Dataset of 331 terminal benchmark environments shown to be reward-hackable, with 3,632 exploit trajectories; monitor detection score falls from 0.97 to 0.92 when reasoning traces are removed.

title: Architectural Design Decisions in AI Agent Harnesses
finding: Source-grounded study of 70 agent-system projects finds five recurring design dimensions, with registry-based tool systems dominant and high-assurance audit rare; deeper coordination pairs with explicit context services.

title: ClawEnvKit: Automatic Environment Generation for Claw-Like Agents
finding: Pipeline generates verified environments from natural language; 1,040 environments across 24 categories; harness engineering lifts performance up to 15.7 percentage points over a bare ReAct baseline.

title: A Self-Evolving Framework for Efficient Terminal Agents via Observational Context Compression
finding: Training-free self-evolving compression rules trim noisy terminal output from agent history; gains of 1-4% on TerminalBench across models, with fewer tokens on other benchmarks.

title: Synthesizing Multi-Agent Harnesses for Vulnerability Discovery
finding: Feedback-driven outer loop searches a typed graph of agent roles, prompts, tools and protocols; it reaches 84.3% on TerminalBench-2 and finds ten unknown Chrome zero-day vulnerabilities.

title: HARBOR: Automated Harness Optimization
finding: Frames harness flag tuning as constrained noisy Bayesian optimization and reports a solver, HARBOR, compared with a four-round manual tuning case study on a production coding agent.

title: The Last Harness You'll Ever Build
finding: Two-level loop automates harness engineering: a worker's harness is evolved with an adversarial evaluator and evolution agent, and a meta loop learns a blueprint for rapid convergence on new tasks.

title: AEL: Evolving Agent Harness in Open-Ended Environments
finding: Evolving harness picks memory-retrieval policies with a Thompson sampling bandit and slow reflection; lifts Sharpe 27% over the strongest memory-only variant with lowest variance among stochastic methods.

title: ClawMark: A Living-World Benchmark for Multi-Turn, Multi-Day, Multimodal Coworker Agents
finding: Multi-day coworker benchmark of 100 tasks with stateful services whose state changes between turns; the strongest model reaches a weighted score of 75.8 but only 20.0% strict task success.

title: AgentPulse: A Continuous Multi-Signal Framework for Evaluating AI Agents in Deployment
finding: Continuous framework scores 50 agents on four factors from 18 real-time signals; a benchmark-plus-sentiment composite predicts GitHub stars with rank correlation 0.52.

title: NeuroClaw Technical Report
finding: Harness-engineered research agent for neuroimaging; with the harness, multimodal model runs score consistently and substantially higher than direct agent invocation on NeuroBench.

title: Context-Augmented Code Generation: How Product Context Improves AI Coding Agent Decision Compliance by 49%
finding: Product-context retrieval raised decision compliance of a coding agent from 46% to 95% across 8 tasks with 41 weighted decision points; the baseline reached 0-33% on decisions requiring product context.

title: Toward Scalable Terminal Task Synthesis via Skill Graphs
finding: Builds terminal task instances by sampling paths through a skill graph of command-line skills; the synthesized tasks helped train Hy3 Preview for terminal settings.

title: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses
finding: Automated coding-harness evolution with observability lifts Terminal-Bench 2 pass@1 from 69.7% to 77.0% in ten iterations, beating the human-designed Codex-CLI harness at 71.9%.

title: BioVeil MATRIX: Uncovering and categorizing vulnerabilities of agentic biological AI scientists
finding: Agentic biology scientists Biomni and K-Dense helped with dual-use tasks their base models block; Biomni's scaffolding raised weapons-proxy benchmark scores above the standalone model.

title: Affordance Agent Harness: Verification-Gated Skill Orchestration
finding: Closed-loop harness routes perception skills and verifies evidence before committing; it reaches a stronger accuracy-cost frontier than fixed-pipeline baselines while cutting skill calls and latency.

title: NORA: A Harness-Engineered Autonomous Research Agent for End-to-End Spatial Data Science
finding: Harness-engineered research agent for spatial data science with 21 workflow skills and 9 sub-agents; case studies with six specialists report substantial efficiency and quality gains over general-purpose configurations.

title: HeavySkill: Heavy Thinking as the Inner Skill in Agentic Harness
finding: Parallel reasoning then summarization, called heavy thinking, beats best-of-N strategies across domains; stronger models approach pass-at-N results, and reinforcement learning can scale its depth and width.

title: PARNESS: A Paper Harness for End-to-End Automated Scientific Research with Dynamic Workflows, Full-Text Indexing, and Cross-Run Knowledge Accumulation
finding: Open-source research framework with a directed acyclic graph kernel for user-editable workflow files, full-text paper indexing and cross-run knowledge retrieval; no measured results are given.

title: AgenticRAG: Agentic Retrieval for Enterprise Knowledge Bases
finding: Agentic harness on top of enterprise search lifts BRIGHT recall@1 to 49.6% (+21.8 points over best embedding baseline); moving from single-shot retrieval to agentic tool use gives 5.9 times improvement.

title: AlphaCrafter: Harnessing Multi-Agent Workflows for Cross-Sectional Quantitative Trading
finding: Multi-agent trading framework encapsulating each agent in programmable policy specifications; it yields superior risk-adjusted returns on China Securities Index 300 and S&P 500 with lower cross-model and cross-trial variance.

title: More Is Not Always Better: Cross-Component Interference in LLM Agent Scaffolding
finding: Across 96 conditions, the all-in scaffold is consistently suboptimal: a single-tool agent beats it by 32% on HotpotQA; the best component count depends on task and model scale.

title: ReFlect: An Effective Harness System for Complex Long-Horizon LLM Reasoning
finding: Deterministic error-detection wrapper reaches 41% task success on gpt-4o-mini and 56% on Claude Sonnet 4.5; harness gain falls as baseline success rises (slope -1.69, r = -0.76).

title: BioMedArena: An Open-source Toolkit for Building and Evaluating Biomedical Deep Research Agents
finding: Toolkit for comparing biomedical deep research agents under one harness and tool registry; equipped harnesses improve all 12 backbones, the best surpassing state-of-the-art by 15.01 points on average.

title: Stop Comparing LLM Agents Without Disclosing the Harness
finding: Position paper: among comparable frontier models, harness configuration can drive more performance variance than model choice, so leaderboards without harness disclosure risk misattributing gains.

title: Continual Harness: Online Adaptation for Self-Improving Foundation Agents
finding: Self-refining harness adapts online within one run; on Pokemon Red and Emerald it cuts button-press cost versus a minimal baseline and recovers most of the gap to an expert harness.

title: Cochise: A Reference Harness for Autonomous Penetration Testing
finding: A 630-line reference harness in Python for autonomous penetration testing, with planner and executor layers over a secure shell connection; released with replay tools and a trajectory corpus.

title: It's Not the Size: Harness Design Determines Operational Stability in Small Language Models
finding: On 24 tasks with 2-3B models, a four-stage pipeline harness reached success rate 0.952 on Gemma4 E2B; one model without harness fell to 0.429 through format violations.

title: Harness Engineering as Categorical Architecture
finding: Categorical account of agent harnesses; a compiler preserves three certificate types across four configurations by identity or replay, tested with two models on one task.

title: CAX-Agent: A Lightweight Agent Harness for Reliable APDL Automation
finding: Recovery policy tested on 50 finite-element benchmarks over 450 runs: model-driven recovery reached completion rate 0.9267, against 0.7733 rule-only and 0.6933 with no recovery.

title: AI Harness Engineering: A Runtime Substrate for Foundation-Model Software Agents
finding: Framework names eleven harness responsibilities and four levels of runtime support; on one controlled task, higher levels yield reproduction logs and verification reports, not just a final patch.

title: Harnessing Agentic Evolution
finding: Meta-agent edits the procedure or agent context that controls future evolution; AEvo outperforms five evolution baselines with a relative improvement of 26 over the strongest baseline.

title: LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Metacognitive harness turns a model's pre-solve and post-solve confidence into test-time control; on a fixed Claude model it raises pooled accuracy from 48.3 to 56.9.

title: Effective Harness Engineering for Algorithm Discovery with Coding Agents
finding: Under a fixed token budget, fewer algorithms with deeper thought beat many shallow ones on circle packing; more capable models produced evaluation hacks at higher rates.

title: Auditing Agent Harness Safety
finding: Audit framework and 210-task benchmark test whether harnesses keep trajectories within permission boundaries; across ten harness configurations, violations accumulate with trajectory length and concentrate in resource access and inter-agent transfer.

title: Orchard: An Open-Source Agentic Modeling Framework
finding: Kubernetes-native environment service plus training recipes for software engineering, graphical interface and personal assistant agents; a 35B open model reaches 69.7% to 73.0% on SWE-bench Verified.

title: Is Grep All You Need? How Agent Harnesses Reshape Agentic Search
finding: Grep generally beat vector retrieval in agent loops on a 116-question LongMemEval sample, yet scores depended strongly on which harness and tool-calling style was used, even on identical data.

title: Harnesses for Inference-Time Alignment over Execution Trajectories
finding: Harnesses split into task decomposition and guided execution; over-decomposition and over-pruning reduce final success, and partial harnesses that specify only initial steps beat fully structured workflows.

title: Harnessing LLM Agents with Skill Programs
finding: Upgrades skill guidance into executable program functions that fire on failure-prone states; inference-time functions alone raise average web-search performance by 25% over a ReAct agent.

title: Code as Agent Harness
finding: Survey treating code as the operational substrate of agent harnesses, covering harness interface, mechanisms and multi-agent scaling; it lists evaluation beyond final success as an open challenge.

title: Harnessing AtomisticSkills for Agentic Atomistic Research
finding: Open-source harness gives general-purpose coding agents more than 100 curated research skills; demonstrated on campaigns in materials, chemistry and drug discovery, with no comparative measurements reported.

title: Toward AI VIS Co-Scientists: A General and End-to-End Agent Harness for Solving Complex Data Visualization Tasks
finding: End-to-end harness designs data visualization apps from data and a task description via agents and skills; validated on scientific visualization contests, producing single-page apps with verified linked-view behavior.

title: Adapting the Interface, Not the Model: Runtime Harness Adaptation for Deterministic LLM Agents
finding: Runtime harness evolved from training trajectories, frozen weights; beats Meta-Harness and AHE by 28.7 and 7.5 points on a 4B open model; frontier models gain 3.5 points on average.

title: Sibyl-AutoResearch: Autonomous Research Needs Self-Evolving Trial-and-Error Harnesses, Not Paper Generators
finding: Self-evolving research harness turns trial outcomes into later behavior and harness repairs; a retrospective audit found eight high-confidence conversion events, median latency one iteration, no comparative claim.

title: Towards Direct Evaluation of Harness Optimizers via Priority Ranking
finding: Evaluates harness optimizers directly by asking them to rank components by potential impact; the ranking correlates with real multi-step optimization gains across 182 human-verified scenarios.

title: ProofAgent Harness: Open Infrastructure for Adversarial Evaluation of AI Agents
finding: Open infrastructure for adversarial multi-turn evaluation of agents, with multi-juror scoring and turn-level audit; a small quantized local model challenged production agents built on large models.

title: Polar: Agentic RL on Any Harness at Scale
finding: Rollout framework treats any coding harness as a black box, reconstructing training trajectories; with reinforcement learning it lifts Qwen3.5-4B by 0.6 to 22.6 points on SWE-bench Verified across four harnesses.

title: DemoEvolve: Demonstration-Guided Harness Evolution under Sparse Feedback
finding: Human demonstrations guide harness evolution; on held-out seeds, Balatro progress rises from 16.83 to 20.00 and Slay the Spire 2 floor from 18.17 to 28.83.

title: AION: Next-Generation Tasks and Practical Harness for Time Series
finding: Time series harness with six component groups; on a Kaggle sales case study it yields more process traces, artifacts and review steps than the same base agent alone.

title: Meta-Engineering Harnesses for AI-Native Software Production: A Contract-Driven Adversarial Verification Architecture with Early Deployment Report
finding: Harness routing work to role-specialized agents with adversarial verification; an early deployment of 17 features revealed contract gaps that drove harness fixes.

title: PolyGnosis 2.0: Enhancing LLM Reasoning via Agentic Harness Engineering for Polymarket and OSINT Insight Extraction
finding: Measures harness techniques for prediction-market analysis: divide-and-conquer partitioning is mandatory, unconstrained terminal reflection causes logical drift, and all agents show a consensus bias.

title: From Model Scaling to System Scaling: Scaling the Harness in Agentic AI
finding: Position paper arguing agentic progress will depend as much on harness design as on stronger models, with a research agenda for harness benchmarks; no measured results are given.

title: It's Not the Capability: Harness Sensitivity Is Non-Monotone Across LLM Agent Tiers
finding: Across 432 runs and six models, the monotone rule failed: a verbose harness cut one chat model by 29-38 points, while strict harness topped a reasoning model at 91.7%.

title: MerLean-Prover: A Recursive Looping Harness for Lean 4 Theorem Proving
finding: Recursive harness of planning, check and proof agents solves 10 of 23 FormalQualBench theorems versus 8 for the best open baseline, and closes all 12 Putnam 2025 problems.

title: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
finding: Feedback agent updates both the harness and the weights of a task agent; combining both levers beats harness-only iteration on three benchmarks.

title: FinHarness: An Inline Lifecycle Safety Harness for Finance LLM Agents
finding: Inline safety harness fuses intent and tool-call monitors with cascaded judges; on FinVault it cuts attack success rate from 38.3% to 15.0% while using 4.7 times fewer advanced-judge calls.

title: Harness-Bench: Evaluating Agent Harnesses across Models and Realistic Workflows
finding: Benchmark of 106 sandboxed offline tasks, 5,194 trajectories: completion, process quality and efficiency vary substantially across model-harness pairings, so capability should be reported per configuration.

title: Towards Cybersecurity SuperIntelligence (CSI): What's the best harness for cybersecurity?
finding: Five cybersecurity agent harnesses on 33 challenges, one fixed model: no single harness dominates; a blackboard combination solves 19 of 33 versus 15 for the best single harness.

title: Scaling Laws for Agent Harnesses via Effective Feedback Compute
finding: A feedback-based scaling measure beats raw compute (R-squared 0.93 to 0.99); a companion control layer lifts mean pass rate 61.2% to 68.2% and cuts cost 213.8 to 85.1.

title: Towards Verifiable Multimodal Deep Research: A Multi-Agent Harness for Interleaved Report Generation
finding: Ptah, a multi-agent harness whose verifier acts as the acceptance function, yields more reliable, visually informative research reports than strong baselines; PtahEval adds presentation-level scoring.

title: Crafter: A Multi-Agent Harness for Editable Scientific Figure Generation from Diverse Inputs
finding: Crafter, a multi-agent harness, generates scientific figures across types and input conditions; CraftEditor converts raster output to editable scalable vector graphics; both beat baselines on named benchmarks.

title: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
finding: Harness updating is flat across model strength: Qwen3.5-9B updates gain about as much as Claude Opus 4.6, while benefit from updated harnesses peaks at mid-tier models.

title: ExpHarness: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning through a Trainable Harness
finding: A trainable experience harness lifts frozen executors: 12.1% and 4.5% on static tasks and 21.4% and 12.7% on agentic tasks, with smaller gains for the larger executor, and fewer steps.

title: From Prompt Injection to Persistent Control: Defending Agentic Harness Against Trojan Backdoors
finding: A multi-step trojan attack reaches 95.5% attack success on GPT-5.4 where single-turn injections score near zero; DASGuard blocks it by sanitizing control text in workspace files.

title: Harnessing Agent Skills: Architectural Patterns and a Reference Architecture for Skill-Mediated LLM Agents
finding: A review of 36 practitioner systems and 51 papers yields ten patterns and a four-layer reference architecture; mapping eight systems leaves 14 of 15 evidence-and-feedback ratings partial or unestablished.

title: Sandboxed Coding Agents are Competitive Omni-modal Task Solvers
finding: Coding agents with text and image access in a sandbox match or beat native omni-modal models on audio-video benchmarks, and simple skill injection improves them further.

title: forge-harness: Engineering Methods for Robust AI Collaboration Harnesses
finding: No abstract is given; the title alone names engineering methods for harnesses that make collaboration with artificial intelligence robust, so no claim can be checked here.

title: Adaptive Auto-Harness: Sustained Self-Improvement for Agentic System Deployment on Open-Ended Task Streams
finding: With the same Sonnet solver, evolving the harness lifts market accuracy 22.2% to 80.9% and security Pass@1 37.2% to 50.2%; artifact accumulation alone does not guarantee sustained gains.

title: HarnessForge: Joint Harness and Policy Evolution for Adaptive Agent Systems
finding: Co-evolving harness and policy on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B beats harness-only and policy-only baselines by up to 12.0% across five benchmarks.

title: Absorbing Complexity: An Interaction-Native Knowledge Harness for Financial LLM Agents
finding: A knowledge harness for financial agents cuts latency 82.95% and token cost 82.29% against agent-driven wiki-walk memory on a synthetic benchmark, not live trading.

title: Harness-1: Reinforcement Learning for Search Agents with State-Externalizing Harnesses
finding: A 20B search agent trained with reinforcement learning inside a stateful harness reaches 0.730 curated recall, 11.4 points above the next open search subagent.

title: Neither Layer Alone: Epistemic Integrity Requires Hierarchical Joint Design for Long-Running AI Agents
finding: Long-running agents fail when model and harness layers upgrade independently; the paper proposes a four-level interface contract from which evaluation and training should derive.

title: DS-Lighting: Making Agent Harnesses Explicit for Data-Science Automation
finding: A toolkit splits agent harnesses into data, workflow, execution and evaluation layers on one shared task interface, and reports that explicit harness design improves reproducibility and reliability.

title: MUSE: A Unified Agentic Harness for MLLMs
finding: Wrapping frozen state-of-the-art multimodal models in a structured execution harness gives consistent gains over the bare model in every setting, largest on the hardest instances, with no retraining.

title: EvoTrainer: Co-Evolving LLM Policies and Training Harnesses for Autonomous Agentic Reinforcement Learning
finding: EvoTrainer co-evolves model policies and training harnesses, matching or exceeding human-engineered reinforcement learning references on math, code and repository software-engineering tasks, largest gain on agentic software engineering.

title: SkillHarness: Harnessing Safe Skills for Computer-Use Agents
finding: Safety-constrained skill learning for computer-use agents cuts the unsafe rate of learned skills by 57.1% and improves execution stability in dynamic environments.

title: Kernel Forge: An Agent Harness for LLM-based Generation and Optimization of CUDA Kernels
finding: An open-source agent harness optimizes CUDA kernels of unmodified PyTorch models with tree search; 14 kernels beat eager mode, up to 2.83x on a softmax kernel in Gemma 4 E2B.

title: Parthenon Law: A Self-Evolving Legal-Agent Framework
finding: On 12,510 legal agent trajectories, per-criterion accuracy rises with stronger models while strict matter completion stalls; the Parthenon harness improves state-of-the-art models on legal tasks.

title: DAR: Deontic Reasoning with Agentic Harnesses
finding: Agentic harnesses push the frontier on deontic reasoning, but gains are uneven: weaker models often degrade on numerical tasks while consuming far more tokens.

title: LeanMarathon: Toward Reliable AI Co-Mathematicians through Long-Horizon Lean Autoformalization
finding: A multi-agent harness turns long Lean formalization into recoverable parallel transactions; across three autonomous runs it formalizes all seven target theorems with no sorry, proving 258 lemmas and theorems.

title: Harnessing Generalist Agents for Contextualized Time Series
finding: A harness gives generalist language-model agents executable time-series tools, reusable routines and episodic memory, and improves results across energy, finance, weather and traffic benchmarks.

title: Statistical Priors for Implicit Preferences: Decoupling Skill Selection as a Local Harness in Personal Agents
finding: A lightweight local preference harness learns skill choices statistically and steers a remote model, reaching lowest cumulative regret and highest accuracy against memory-augmented agents.

title: Evolving Agents in the Dark: Retrospective Harness Optimization via Self-Preference
finding: Retrospective harness optimization, using only past trajectories and no labels, raises the SWE-Bench Pro pass rate from 59% to 78% in one round.

title: From Failed Trajectories to Reliable LLM Agents: Diagnosing and Repairing Harness Flaws
finding: Trace-grounded diagnosis repairs agent harnesses by attributing failures to harness artifacts, improving the initial harness by 6.3% to 18.4% across four benchmarks.

title: Act As a Real Researcher: A Suite of Benchmarks Evaluating Frontier LLMs and Agentic Harnesses in Research Lifecycle
finding: A research-intern benchmark finds the best configuration, Mini-SWE-Agent with Claude Opus 4.7, reaches only 68.3% success, and argues that more scaffolding alone will not close the gap.

title: Bayesian-Agent: Posterior-Guided Skill Evolution Across LLM Agent Harnesses
finding: Bayesian skill evolution lifts SOP-Bench from 80% to 95% and RealFin-Bench from 45% to 65% in incremental mode, across three harness backends.

title: HARBOR: A Harness Framework for Agentic Robot Reinforcement Learning
finding: An agentic harness automates robot reinforcement learning from simulator to trained policy across 16 tasks, designing rewards and tuning algorithms at practical token and wall-clock cost.

title: SkillHone: A Harness for Continual Agent Skill Evolution Through Persistent Decision History
finding: A harness for continual skill evolution keeps decision history and beats a commercial deep-research agent by 15.8 points on GAIA and 3.2 points on WebWalkerQA-EN.

title: AlloSpatial: Agentic Harness Framework for Spatial Reasoning in Foundation Models
finding: A spatial harness lifts proprietary models 5% to 18% without training, and a trained Qwen3-VL agent beats larger general models on VSI-Bench and MindCube.

title: Harness Engineering for Physical AI: Robot Middleware Is the Harness Layer
finding: Robot middleware should serve as the harness for physical artificial intelligence, enforcing three functions, Projection, Isolation and Transfer, sketched as a ROS 2 Harness Profile.

title: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
finding: An agent improves its own harness through weakness mining, proposal and regression-tested validation; every final harness gains on all nine model-benchmark pairs, up to 132% relative.

title: AutoMegaKernel: A Statically-Checked Agent Harness for Self-Retargeting Megakernel Synthesis
finding: A statically checked harness generates megakernels: its validator had zero false accepts across 7,160 adversarial schedules, and int8 kernels beat cuBLAS on inference-class hardware but trail on training-class hardware.

title: What makes a harness a harness: necessary and sufficient conditions for an agent harness
finding: A constitutive definition of agent harness, with an inclusion and exclusion test, classifies six real harnesses and edge cases consistently, and separates harnesses from frameworks and orchestrators.

title: The Scaffold Effect in Coding Agents: Harness Choice as a Hidden Variable in Coding-Agent Evaluation
finding: Harness choice changes tokens per solved task by up to 40x, while within-model pass-rate gaps stay within 0-8 percentage points; leaderboards should report the harness with the model.

title: AgenticNav: Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation as a Tool-Calling Harness
finding: A lightweight harness exposes action, depth and memory as tools; it reaches 76% success on R2R-CE, and its navigation gains grow more consistent as vision-language models improve.

title: Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems with Shared Context
finding: A shared context and task queue replacing the main agent makes multi-agent runs up to 2.49x faster than the base harness, and up to 17.5 points more accurate.

title: Layer-Isolated Evaluation: Gating the Deterministic Scaffold of a Production LLM Agent with a No-LLM, Regression-Locked Test Harness
finding: A deterministic per-layer test suite for a production ordering agent shows the aggregate pass rate moved 1.7 to 5.9 points while the matching layer slice fell 25 to 91 points.

title: Claw-SWE-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating OpenClaw-style Agent Harnesses on Coding Tasks
finding: A 350-instance GitHub issue benchmark with a shared adapter protocol shows harness success and resource use vary substantially with the model held fixed; an 80-instance Lite subset is provided.

title: HarnessBridge: Learnable Bidirectional Controller for LLM Agent Harness
finding: A learned harness controller matches or surpasses specialized harnesses on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and SWE-bench Verified with fewer tokens, and transfers from smaller generators to larger commercial models.

title: Recursive Agent Harnesses
finding: With GPT-5 held fixed, recursive agent harnesses lift the Codex baseline from 71.75% to 81.36% on Oolong-Synthetic; with Claude Sonnet 4.5 as backbone the design reaches 89.77%.

title: HarnessX: A Composable, Adaptive, and Evolvable Agent Harness Foundry
finding: A foundry for composable, evolvable harnesses averages +14.5% across five benchmarks (up to +44.0%), with gains largest where baselines are lowest.

title: AgentSpec: Understanding Embodied Agent Scaffolds Through Controlled Composition
finding: Swapping scaffold modules under controlled conditions shows embodied agent performance follows scaffold compatibility and interaction effects rather than the strength of any single module.

title: PhoneHarness: Harnessing Phone-Use Agents through Mixed GUI, CLI, and Tool Actions
finding: A mixed GUI, command-line and tool harness with a benchmark that checks observable side effects reaches a 75.0% pass rate, 12.9 points above the strongest non-harness settings.

title: ClayBuddy: A Framework, Evaluation, & Mitigation of Coding Agent Failures
finding: Sorting coding-agent failures into underspecification, capability and harness errors, a self-modifying harness with selective context truncation eliminates violations on some tasks.

title: LLM-as-Code: Agentic Programming for Agent Harness
finding: Letting the model orchestrate causes token explosion and unreliable completion; a program that governs control flow and calls the model as a component improves long computer-use stability.

title: From Question Answering to Task Completion: A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design
finding: A survey argues agent quality emerges from the interaction of model, runtime, task and evaluation design; it splits the execution harness into six runtime responsibilities and reviews evaluation practices.

title: SING: Synthetic Intention Graph for Scalable Active Tool Discovery in LLM Agents
finding: An intention-aware tool discovery graph raises Global Recall@5 by up to 59.8% and downstream success by up to 28.9% over baselines, while cutting full-corpus schema exposure by 99.8%.

title: Toward Self-Evolution-Ready Workflow Harnesses: A Reversible Migration Path and Convertibility Taxonomy for Expert LLM Pipelines
finding: Proposes a reversible migration path that refactors static expert language-model-plus-script workflows into typed, auditable stages, guided by a three-tier convertibility taxonomy; the abstract reports no results.

title: Dissecting model behavior through agent trajectories
finding: Harness-model mismatch (the intent-execution gap) limits agent performance; a simple harness reproduces or improves pass@1 across model families, and 154,000 trajectories reveal model-level behavior differences.

title: SEAGym: An Evaluation Environment for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
finding: An evaluation environment for harness updates shows frequent updates can fail to improve held-out performance, and useful intermediate snapshots can collapse later.

title: Guava: Distilling Frontier VLMs into a Compact Agent through a Robotic Manipulation Harness
finding: A 4B open model, distilled through an embodied tool harness on fewer than 2K simulated trajectories, performs comparably to frontier proprietary models on manipulation tasks.

title: StaminaBench: Stress-Testing Coding Agents over 100 Interaction Turns
finding: A harness matters most for strong models, whose best and worst harness differ up to 6x in passed turns; weaker models fail with any harness.

title: Building Agent Harnesses for Scientific Curation from Multimodal Sources
finding: A harness around a frontier agent extracts structured records from papers with provenance, scoring 81.0 on the Gold-Referenced Attribute Score, over 23 points above frontier agents.

title: A Contradiction Judge Counted Reported Teammate Errors as Hallucinations: An Assertion-Aware Re-Score of One Multi-Agent LLM Harness
finding: Re-scoring a multi-agent harness shows judge models counted correct reports of teammate errors as hallucinations; on values agents assert, the broadcast effect is -0.0208, not distinguishable from zero.

title: Harness-MU: A Safe, Governed, and Effective Harness for Multi-User LLM Agents
finding: Enforcing multi-user permissions in deterministic execution hooks, not in the model, preserves privacy against all access-control attacks and raises utility by 0.28 to 0.39 over the standard baseline.

title: Code Isn't Memory: A Structural Codebase Index Inside a Coding Agent
finding: With Claude Opus 4.7 held fixed, a structural codebase index gives a large localization gain and a statistically separated resolve gain, with no cost penalty.

title: PaperClaw: Harnessing Agents for Autonomous Research and Human-in-the-Loop Refinement
finding: A harnessed multi-agent system carries a research project from field survey to finished paper, with optional human refinement; a language-model judge rates its papers strong in both modes.

title: AOHP: An Open-Source OS-Level Agent Harness for Personalized, Efficient and Secure Interaction
finding: An operating-system-level harness built on the Android Open Source Project improves task completion by 21.12% and cuts token cost by 51.55% in preliminary experiments.

title: ActPlane: Programmable OS-Level Policy Enforcement for Agent Harnesses
finding: Enforcing agent-declared policies in the kernel with eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) catches indirect execution paths that tool-call interception misses, at 1.9% to 8.4% overhead.

title: The Interplay of Harness Design and Post-Training in LLM Agents
finding: Harness design is a controllable factor in post-training; harness-aware post-training improves in-distribution results and helps agents adapt to out-of-distribution tool shifts on ALFWorld.

title: Unlocking Model Potentials Through Adaptive Multi-Agent Scaffolding for Efficient Issue Resolution
finding: With the same models, a decentralized scaffold lifts SWE-bench Verified by 3.6 to 8.4% and SWE-bench Pro by 6.3 to 18.5%, saving 1.18 dollars per instance against Claude Code.

title: Clinical Harness for Governable Medical AI Skill Ecosystems
finding: A runtime governance architecture registers, orchestrates, constrains and monitors clinical artificial intelligence skills, illustrated with osteoporosis; the abstract reports no measured results.

title: A Process Harness for Uplifting Legacy Workflows to Agentic BPM: Design and Realization in CUGA FLO
finding: A process harness places a policy-governed agentic layer around a deterministic workflow engine, demonstrated on a loan approval workflow with regulatory override; the abstract reports no measured results.

title: NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems
finding: A verification-aware harness reaches 53.3% and 51.7% pass rates on two recommender task sets; its selected candidate lifted gross merchandise value 1.25% to 2.02% in a 5% traffic split test.

title: QueenBee: A Recursively Self-Improving Harness for Communication Topology Design in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
finding: QueenBee evolves multi-agent communication workflows from a persistent structural memory and outperforms fixed communication baselines and recent automated workflow methods on Silo-Bench.

title: Where Does Harness-Optimization Value Live? Localized Gains and the Budget-Splitting Trap in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
finding: On ALFWorld with a frozen 7B model, harness optimization value sits in the reflection and control slot (gain +0.119), and splitting budget evenly across slots is harmful.

title: Stop Hand-Holding Your Coding Agent: Engineering the Loops that Replace Step-by-Step Prompting
finding: Loop specifications with a trigger, goal, verification, stopping rule and memory can replace step-by-step prompting; of 50 real loops, 70% verify autonomously and 74% name terminal states.

title: Representation Affects Retrieval: A Case Study of Skill Discovery and Routing in a Multimodal Agent Harness
finding: In a production multimodal harness, partial in-prompt skill exposure misroutes a task through lexical competition, while full autoload selects the correct skill on all six tasks.

title: Cognitive Scaffold: From Fluid Context to Crystallized Memory for Long-Horizon DeepResearch Agents
finding: No abstract is given; the title alone names a cognitive scaffold that turns fluid context into crystallized memory for long-horizon deep-research agents.

title: Evaluating Agentic Harness Systems for Autonomous Computational Pathology
finding: ACP-Bench audits nine models across three harness systems on 41 pathology workflow tasks: initiation and diagnostic reporting are mature, while tool execution lags and end-to-end completion stays rare.

title: BudgetBench: A Budget-Tiered Protocol and Pilot Harness for Memory Strategy Evaluation in Local Large Language Model Agents
finding: A token-budget protocol and reference harness exposes budget violations and non-monotonic quality curves; pilots leave whether budgeted memory beats full context unresolved.

title: COMFYCLAW: Self-Evolving Skill Harnesses for Image Generation Workflows
finding: Evolving a reusable skill library from earlier runs gives an image-workflow agent harness the best average score across six agent configurations, beating a verifier-only baseline without skill evolution.

title: SwarmResearch: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Open-Ended Discovery
finding: An orchestrator-subagent harness with a global steering agent and branch-isolated search agents matches or beats state-of-the-art methods on 13 of 15 open-ended optimization tasks.

title: Don't Blame the Large Language Model: How Agent Harness Evolution Shapes Coding Agent Quality
finding: With the model held fixed, 35 sequential releases of the Qwen Code command-line agent show quality fluctuations, which the authors trace to specific development patterns and architectural components.

title: Harness-Aware Self-Evolving: Co-Evolving Model Weights, Harness, and Task Solutions
finding: A single Qwen3-8B model that edits its own harness matches the text-classification performance of a GPT-OSS-120B model using Claude Code as harness proposer, and repairs imperfect evaluation components.

title: Agentao: A Policy-Governed Runtime Harness for Embeddable Tool-Using LLM Agents
finding: A governed local runtime separates model-generated action proposals from host-authorized execution through permission-mediated tools and execution traces; it claims no formal safety guarantees.

title: ACE: Agentic Control for Embodied Manipulation via Zero-shot Workflow Reasoning
finding: An agentic manipulation harness pairs a language agent with a visuomotor policy, reaching 70% and 80% success on two tabletop tasks versus 55% and 70% without persistent context.

title: Measuring Harness-Induced Belief Divergence in Multi-Step LLM Agents
finding: With model and task fixed, changing only the execution harness produces substantial belief divergence in coding agents that terminal success alone often hides; a belief-rollout diagnostic traces it.

title: HarnessMDP: Learning to Control LLM Agent Harnesses with Offline Reinforcement Learning
finding: Learning which structural execution actions to take, offline from collected trajectories, consistently improves task performance over baseline harnesses on coding, tau-bench and agent benchmarks.

title: GaP: A Graph-as-Policy Multi-Agent Self-Learning Harness For Variational Automation Tasks
finding: A multi-agent coding harness generates robot computation graphs and refines them in simulation; it reports success rates that significantly outperform baselines on eight new benchmarks, four simulated and four real-world.

title: Agentic Scaffolding Amplifies Sycophantic Behavior in Large Language Models
finding: Agentic scaffolding (feedback loops, reconsideration checkpoints, refinement) amplifies sycophancy: accuracy falls 6.3 points on average, and more capable models show larger amplification.

title: The Balkanization of Execution-Security Research for AI Coding Agents: Isolation, Access Control, and Time-of-Check-to-Time-of-Use Vulnerabilities
finding: A survey of 39 papers in 17 categories finds five gaps, including that isolation and capability designs are almost never evaluated against one another on a shared benchmark.

title: Cost-Effective Agent Harnesses for Abstract Reasoning and Generalization on ARC-AGI-1
finding: An open-weight model with no benchmark-specific training reaches 67.25% pass@2 on the ARC-AGI-1 public evaluation with an orchestrator harness at $0.62 per task, up from a 15.50% one-shot baseline.

title: The Harness Effect: How Orchestration Design Sets the Token Economics of Enterprise Agentic AI
finding: Swapping only the orchestration layer, with six models fixed, cuts cost per task 41%; the quality gain tracks baseline model strength (r=0.99, n=6).

title: Thinking More, Harnessing Better: State Machine Guided Harness Automatic Generation with Project Digestion and Workflow Decomposition
finding: A generator that writes fuzz test drivers reaches 3.07x, 1.71x and 4.26x the branch coverage of three existing generators, and found seven previously unreported bugs.

title: From Prompts to Contracts: Harness Engineering for Auditable Enterprise LLM Agents
finding: Code-owned enforcement keeps full utility (120/120) and blocks recommendation-language and trace-leakage violations that prompts alone let through; a bolt-on guardrail drops utility to 88/120.

title: TTHE: Test-Time Harness Evolution
finding: A harness evolves during evaluation on unlabeled execution traces, improving fixed ReAct-style baseline harnesses on six benchmarks without weight updates or answer labels.

title: Harness VLA: Steering Frozen VLAs into Reliable Manipulation Primitives via Memory-Guided Agents
finding: A memory-augmented harness wraps a frozen vision-language-action model as a retryable primitive, improving on the strongest baselines by 38.6 points on LIBERO-Pro and 25.4 on RoboCasa365, without finetuning.

title: Better Harnesses, Smaller Models: Building 90% Cheaper Agents via Automated Harness Adaptation
finding: On many routine business tasks, small models with an adapted harness can match frontier performance at 90% lower cost; the best recovers 89.7% at 4% of the cost.

title: Scoped Verification for Reliable Long-Horizon Agentic Context Evolution under Distribution Shift
finding: Over five replications, a typed instruction graph lifts Gemini 2.5 Flash's pass^3 reliability from 0.091 to 0.673, above a Gemini 3.1 Pro zero-shot reference of 0.242.

title: MAG: A Web-Agent Benchmark and Harness for Multimodal Action and Guide Generation
finding: A benchmark and harness for web-agent actions and guides; policy optimization with expert trajectories nearly doubles a supervised 9B agent's success (6.9% to 13.2%).

title: FORCE-Bench: A Benchmark, Dataset, and Evaluation Harness for Agentic AI in Enterprise Finance
finding: A 251-query finance benchmark with rubric scoring on eight dimensions shows general-purpose agent systems miss finance quality requirements under operational constraints, while a purpose-built agent is more reliable.

title: StructAgent: Harness Long-horizon Digital Agents with Unified Causal Structure
finding: Structured verifier-gated state lifts OSWorld-Verified success: Qwen3.5-9B from 27.0% to 46.9%, Qwen3.5-27B from 31.6% to 62.2%.

title: Agentic Routing: The Harness-Native Data Flywheel
finding: Routes each agent step to one or several models using harness state, and logged runs become training data; no headline number is given.

title: ToFu: A White-Box, Token-Efficient Agent Harness for Researchers
finding: Open-source white-box harness for researchers, claimed more token-efficient and cheaper than existing harnesses; no figure given in the abstract.

title: Phantom Guardrails: When Self-Improving Agent Harnesses Fix Failures That Never Happened
finding: Self-improving harness proposers invent failures: 15 of 60 runs added a guardrail for a nonexistent rule on legal input, versus 0 of 60 on featureless input.

title: Baselines Before Architecture: Evaluating Coding Agents for Autonomous Penetration Testing
finding: Plain coding agents already solve much of the 104-task XBOW benchmark; report model-matched plain-agent baselines before crediting harness architecture for gains.

title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
finding: Automatic harness evolution fails to beat simple test-time scaling on Terminal-Bench 2.1; it wins only on long-horizon games, by 80% on ARC-AGI-3.

title: Agent-Safety Evaluations as Load-Bearing Evidence: A Vendor-Neutral, Cross-Harness Reconstructability Metric
finding: Scores whether captured agent traces can reconstruct the decisions a safety claim rests on; sufficiency spans 0.458 to 0.833 across four inputs.

title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable,Navigable, and Editable
finding: A behavior-to-code map built from a harness codebase improves edit planning while using fewer planner tokens, with largest gains on scattered sites.

title: MemoHarness: Agent Harnesses That Learn from Experience
finding: Harness that learns from its own executions beats fixed harnesses on shell, code and reasoning benchmarks; statistical robustness is left to future work.

title: Set-shifting Behavioral Test for Harnessed Agents
finding: Silent shifts in which tool is reliable show weaker models often drop the reliable tool, while frontier models keep calling it.

title: HarnessBank: Semantic Gene-Bank Search with Gated Verification for Agent-Harness Self-Evolution
finding: Self-evolving harness with a gene bank and gated screening improves seven agent benchmarks by 5.1% to 15.4%; gains depend on the model used.

title: Partially Correlated Verifier Cascades in LLM Harnesses: Concave Log-Odds, Polynomial Reliability, and Blind-Spot Ceilings
finding: Correlated verifier gates fail polynomially, not exponentially, and can plateau below full reliability; independence underestimates failure 20 times at k=5 in synthetic tests.

title: Harness Engineering: Anatomy, Architecture, and Evolution of Coding Agents -- A Source-Code Study of Eleven Systems
finding: Source-code audit of eleven coding harnesses yields seven subsystems and 29 design patterns; none of them retrieves code with vector embeddings.

title: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
finding: Refining the harness lets low-effort agents beat maximum-effort settings on 30 synthetic research tasks while cutting inference cost by up to 60%.

title: Understanding Agent-Reactive Bugs at the Model-Harness Boundary: An Empirical Study of LLM Agent Issue Reports
finding: Analysis of 255 bug reports finds agent-reactive bugs often fail silently without test oracles, and stochastic model output complicates reproduction.

title: Co-Harness: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Model Weights for LLM Agents
finding: Co-optimizes harness and model weights in post-training; a 200-hour autonomous case study recovers from crashes, with no benchmark figure in the abstract.

title: DataFlow-Harness: A Grounded Code-Agent Platform for Constructing Editable LLM Data Pipelines
finding: Platform-grounded agent builds editable data pipelines with 93.3% pass rate on 12 tasks, at 72.5% lower measured cost than Vanilla Claude Code.

title: Harness Engineering for LLM-Driven GPU Kernel Generation
finding: Harness separating evaluation from profiler-guided optimization gives mean-latency speedups of 1.12x to 29.68x on five kernel operators; expert directions stay critical.

title: FlashRT: Agent Harness for Guiding Agents to Deploy Real-Time Multimodal Applications
finding: Agent harness guides coding agents from reference code to multi-GPU deployments, up to about 70 times lower latency on NVIDIA B200 GPUs.

title: Automated Discovery Has No Universally Superior Harness
finding: Across 30 budget-matched harnesses on 12 model-problem pairs and 3.1 million rollouts, no fixed harness is reliably superior; harness choice acts like a hyperparameter.

title: PRO-LONG: Programmatic Memory Enables Long-Horizon Reasoning
finding: Programmatic memory over a full interaction log adds 18.0 points on ARC-AGI-3 over the base agent and matches or exceeds specialized harnesses with 4.2 to 5.8 times fewer tokens.

title: Delivery, Not Storage: Cue-Anchored Working Memory as a Harness Property for Coding Agents
finding: Harness-injected, cue-triggered memory arrives in every seeded run, while voluntary memory use is near zero (0 operations in 114 turns).

title: Agentic Context Management: Solving Agent Memory and Cost by Treating Them as Lifecycle and Architecture Problems
finding: Argues agent context management is a lifecycle problem; validated compaction keeps token cost linear, and a reference service reports 92% on LongMemEval.

title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
finding: Open framework trains agents inside their real harnesses; reaches 37.7 on OSWorld-Verified, matches models several times larger, and some harnesses are much harder to learn.

title: The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents
finding: Nearly 6,000 runs show skills raise average success but also cause regressions; the best skills win mainly by regressing less, not by gaining more.

title: Loop Engineering: Version-Bound, Evidence-Gated Coordination for Production Coding Agents
finding: Six-element loop method with evidence gates: in five pull requests, three reached test releases with independent evidence and two stopped before merge; not a controlled benchmark.

title: JarvisHub: An Open Harness for Canvas-Native Multimodal Creative Agents
finding: Canvas-native harness keeps creative project state as typed nodes and links, letting agents revise and version multimodal assets the user can inspect and steer; no figures given.

title: From Proposal to Verified Effect: Praxa, an Evidence-Bound Harness for Governed AI Agent Execution
finding: Reliability layer passed 17 of 36 trials, same as baseline, using 37.49% more input tokens; a development comparison showed 37.11% fewer tokens at equal measured accuracy.

title: Context Assembly as the Controlled Variable: A Control-Theoretic View of Harness Policies for Frozen LLM Agents
finding: Treats context assembly as the controlled variable, learned online outside a frozen model, with a stability argument for non-decreasing expected reward; reports no headline numbers.

title: ARCHER: Agentic Rule and Compliance Harness for Executable Regulations
finding: Deterministic multi-agent harness lifts mean union accuracy 82% over single-pass prompting; a self-hosted open-weights model reaches 97.8% of frontier accuracy at a quarter the cost.

title: CHILL-Harness: Counterfactual Harness Learning for Efficient Reasoning in Long-Horizon Agents
finding: Learns when to adapt the orchestration layer of a harness; keeps task success while substantially cutting token consumption and execution time, with no figure in the abstract.

title: Distributing Security Controls Through Harness Engineering
finding: Security controls packaged in a distributable harness reach a 100% adjusted score, matching the best securely configured commercial agent; model non-determinism makes security outcomes inconsistent.

title: Living-Harness Is an Interactive-Agent Evolver
finding: Self-evolving harness turns trajectories into episodic memory and a state graph; improves Pass@1 by 10.07 and 9.91 points over the strongest interactive baseline.

title: DREvo: Distilling Recalibrated Historical Experience for Harness Self-Evolution
finding: Recalibrates historical experience during harness self-evolution, giving smoother trajectories and the highest accuracy on all five benchmarks, with average gains of 16.2% and 14.2%.

title: Scores Are Not Decisions: Cost-Aware Stopping for Tool Acquisition in LLM Agents
finding: Cost-aware stopping decides how many ranked tools an agent acquires; exposes 37% fewer tools than full access while keeping task success comparable.

title: Harness-G: A Graph-Structured Harness for Search Agents
finding: Replaces free-form search queries with finite evidence selection; beats the strongest baseline, Graph-R1, by 10.74 F1 points at 1.5B and 3.98 at 3B.

title: Albilich: Steerable Proof-State Orchestration for LLM-Based Mathematical Research with CAS Integration
finding: Computer algebra tools solve 10 of 10 RealMath problems versus 9 of 10 without them, and cut tokens by 32.0% on one problem when enabled.

title: SKIMIX: Multi-Agent Harness-Time Scaling with Skill Mixture for Dynamic Harness Engineering
finding: Multi-agent skill mixtures help open-ended math reasoning but give limited or negative gains on multiple-choice tasks; most gains arrive in the first refinement round.

title: DataClawEval: A Benchmark for Data Engineering Agents in Real Industrial Harness
finding: Benchmark of 100 end-to-end data engineering tasks graded by deterministic scripts; the strongest of 16 frontier agents scores 74.9, and no single model dominates.

title: Agent Harness Distillation: Inference-Time Harness Extraction and Exploitation in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems
finding: Black-box interactions let an attacker rebuild a multi-agent system's inference-time harness, showing intellectual property leakage; a deception defense cuts extraction and keeps utility.

title: Model or Harness? An Interaction-Centric Taxonomy for Localizing Agent Failures
finding: Taxonomy of 41 failure modes assigns each agent failure to a component edge and a fault side, separating model fixes from harness fixes; the strongest judge reaches kappa 0.76.

title: RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems
finding: Bandit router picks the modification direction while the language model writes the edit; more stable gains than language-model reasoning search, and a 7-day online test lifts revenue 0.534%.

title: LoopsBench: From Harness Engineering to Loop Engineering in Coding Agent Evaluation
finding: Benchmark of 112 long-horizon coding tasks; the best configuration, Opus-4.7 with Claude Code, resolves 25.00% of tasks, and regressions stay visible across loop profiles.

title: DarwinX: Evolving Agent Harnesses Through Natural Selection
finding: Population-based harness evolution with a frozen model adds about 17 points on average; Terminal-Bench 2.1 rises 7.7 points to 83.2%, and WebArena-Infinity rises from 43.5% to 93.0%.

title: AutoFyn Technical Report: Non-Parametric Expert Iteration for Long-Horizon Agents
finding: Keeps the model frozen and updates persistent state between rounds; on six 2026 International Mathematical Olympiad problems, every model scores higher than under its provider's own coding agent.

title: Prompt-Induced Waste in Coding Agents: Reasoning, Effort, Harness Design, and End-to-End Cost
finding: Prompt wording, inference effort and harness policy interact; token counts are not sufficient targets, so measure cost per successful task. No headline number is given.

title: HarnessCompass: Guiding Automatic Harness Evolution toward Generalizable and Effective Agent Harnesses
finding: Constrained, component-wise harness evolution lifts SWE-bench Verified Pass@1 from 54% to 66% with GPT-5.4 in five iterations, beating prior automatic harness evolution.

title: LongHorizon-Harness: Advancing Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Tasks
finding: Explicit task-state manager with independently audited environment facts lifts Qwen 3.7-Plus from 51.8% to 80.7% on WeaveBench and Claude Opus 4.7 from 20.0% to 34.3% on an OSWorld 2.0 subset.

title: Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories
finding: Trained engineer model edits an agent's runtime harness from failures; raises vanilla Qwen3.5-9B success from 44.3% to 53.6% across WebShop, ALFWorld and DBBench.

title: Towards the Harness of Embodied Agents
finding: Adapts the coding-agent harness to robots, with a scene graph as context and exit-code style evaluation; the abstract gives no quantitative result.

title: OneDayAgent: Towards a Long-Horizon Harness for Autonomous Agents
finding: Long-horizon harness splits requests into subtasks with managed memory and repair; scores 0.821 on AgentIF-OneDay with the GLM-5.2 backend and runs across five backends without tuning.

title: Skill-Use: Can LLMs Actually Use Skills in Agentic Harnesses?
finding: Benchmark of 79 real skills and 177 tasks: the strongest of eight models reaches a Skill-Use score of only 0.613, and model rankings shift with the harness.

title: EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement
finding: Clients evolve a shared harness on local workloads and a server merges their changes; experiments across five settings show improvement, with no figures in the abstract.

title: EvoHarness-RL: Learning Runtime Harness Coordination for Self-Evolving Agents
finding: Learned harness coordination adds 8.5 points over the strongest open baseline; as the policy grows more capable, agents use external scaffolding more selectively.

title: DCAS: Decoupling CLI Agent Scaffolding to Internalize Planning across Scaffolds
finding: Trajectories tuned on one scaffold degrade under others; a routing layer lets a model trained on planning-aware trajectories gain across non-training scaffolds.

title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
finding: Benchmark of five frontier models as harness optimizers over 111 scored runs; optimizer models differ more than the coding harnesses they act through, and native harnesses are not consistently superior.

title: HarnessSafe: Evaluating Safety Across Persistent Carriers in Agent Harnesses
finding: Benchmark of 328 cases across seven persistent-carrier families; containment depends on harness and model together, and attack success rates miss how far attacks progress.

title: $A^2E$ : An End-to-End Agent Auditing Engine
finding: The A2E engine evaluates agent harnesses with multidimensional metrics; no single model-harness combination consistently outperforms all others across every task type.

title: A Domain-Specific Harness for End-to-End Automation of Optimization Research
finding: Domain harness runs optimization research through four stages, including Lean 4 formal verification, yielding an accelerated method with an O(1/N^4) rate and machine-checked proofs.

title: Ouroboros: A Self-Developing Frontier Coding Agent with Reviewed Core Evolution
finding: Self-developing harness reviews its own commits; an Opus 5 run scores 86.74% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 90.69% on OSWorld-Verified, reported as best results.

title: Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses
finding: Task-specific harness evolution adds 15.0 to 39.3 points on moderate BALROG tasks with a frozen model, but gives no gain on tasks beyond the backbone's capability.

title: The Scaffolding Matters More Than the Interface: A Controlled Comparison of MCP and CLI Tool Use Across Seven Agent Scaffoldings, Five Language Models, and One Software Task
finding: Scaffolding moves cost more than the tool interface: command-line-only scaffolds ran 5.0x to 28x cheaper than Model Context Protocol scaffolds; paired ratios span 0.43x to 29x.

title: Evo-Bench: Can Language Models Improve Agent Harness?
finding: Benchmark of nine frontier and open-weight models evolving their own harnesses; top models gain up to 16.6 points, and evolved harnesses transfer to boost diverse policy models.

title: From Prompt to Harness: Coderlet from Scratch
finding: Walks one request through a compact harness with model, execution and state boundaries; the abstract gives no measurements, and the artifact is released on GitHub.

title: Macaron-V1: Towards Open Continual Learning with Self-Improvement and Mixture-of-LoRA
finding: Open agent-model family pairs a 748B flagship with a 50B local variant, both built from frozen bases with specialist adapters and model-harness co-design; no headline numbers.

title: Agentic Harnesses: LLM-Driven Verification Layers for Robot Autonomy
finding: A language-model judge ensemble gates robot plans between planning and execution: near 85% precision across accept, escalate and reject, and 97% containment of adversarial attacks.

title: SHE: Trajectory-driven Safety Harness Evolution for LLM Agents
finding: Evolves safety harness artifacts from rollout trajectories; achieves 3.1x lower attack success than static SafeHarness on Agent-SafetyBench while improving benign utility.

title: SBCO: Self-Supervised, Verifier-Grounded Harness Optimization For Planning Agents
finding: Self-supervised harness optimizer with a fixed meta-agent matches or exceeds a customized self-modifying baseline across two planning domains while using 4 to 5.5 times less compute.

title: One Recipe, Many Harnesses: What Self-Evolution Encodes Across Languages and Models
finding: One evolution recipe fixed across eight languages and three models improves solve rates in most cells; gains track recoverable execution defects and are near zero where those are absent.

title: Self-Evolving Embodied Agents via Skill-Harness Evolution
finding: Frozen model evolves reusable skills and a context-code harness through target-environment rollouts, avoiding training runs; the abstract gives no figures.

title: Evaluating Agentic Learning Harness Capabilities Without Labels via the Scaling Hypothesis
finding: Scores a learning harness without labels by how far a smaller student converges toward a stronger teacher; that lift correlates with lift against held-out gold labels across security tasks.

title: Harness-IF: Evaluating Instruction Following Across Instruction Surfaces in Coding Agents
finding: Scores 256 operational rules from execution evidence; across 12 frontier models every model follows rules less well when they oppose unprompted defaults, by 3.6 to 7.4 points.

title: Capability Sheaves for Compositional Agent-Harness Repair: Controlled Quotients and a Real-Repository Stress Test
finding: Repair method reaches 127 of 160 issues, tying the strong anchor; its 118-versus-116 edge over a matched selector is not supported across repositories, so no real-world advantage is shown.

title: AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design
finding: Meta-harness optimizer raises average PosterBench score from 54.99 to 67.39 across seven code-agent configurations, and reaches 78.32, 7.45 points above a commercial system.

title: Engineering Reliable Coding Agents: Evaluating and Operating the System Around the Model
finding: Monograph synthesizes 164 scholarly works and 206 reliability records; many apparent model failures originate in the surrounding system, and layer improvements often fail to reach end-to-end outcomes.

title: HELIX: Model-Harness Co-evolution for Recursive Self-Improvement
finding: Evolved harness improves task coverage 4.0% over the Pi baseline on code repair, and the full portfolio exposes up to 58.0% more verified coverage through complementary sibling behavior.

title: MedClaw: Heuristic Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Surgical Video Reasoning
finding: Text-only orchestrator with frozen vision sub-agents, plus skill distillation from about 100 labeled examples, outperforms one-shot vision-language models, most on long out-of-domain surgery videos.

title: Harness the Memory: A Holistic Evaluation of Memory Substrates in Memory Agents
finding: Eleven memory substrates tested under one harness with 26 metrics; no single substrate consistently dominates, and choosing one per operating regime beats the best fixed substrate.

title: Evo-Harness: Context-to-Harness Skill Compilation for Self-Evolving Agents
finding: Compiles noisy single-shot executions into reusable skill harnesses for a frozen agent, evaluated on five realistic benchmarks; the abstract gives no figures.

title: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a \$15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
finding: Runtime harness raises GPT-5.5 from an 83.1% reference to 92.1% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, and DeepSeek-V4 Flash from 82.7% to 88.1% with under $38 of adaptation.

title: Training Agents to Evolve with Their Harness: TaoLive Digital Avatar Agent Technical Report
finding: Trains compact models to adapt to changing harnesses; reaches 94.8 on Live-Stream QA, above the strongest general model at 93.0, with median latency of 3.4 seconds on one graphics processor.

title: Security Assessment of DeepSeek Harness with A.I.G: Evaluating Resistance to Indirect Prompt Injection
finding: Indirect prompt injection against DeepSeek Harness over 14,560 controlled executions: strongest attack success is 25.5% under the rule-based judge, for hidden Unicode in file mode.

title: Zetta $ζ$: An Efficient Closed-Loop Embodied Harness for Self-Evolving Physical Intelligence
finding: Closed-loop embodied harness evolves runtime critics and recovery skills with the base policy frozen; reaches 90.8% on LIBERO-Pro and 93.6% on RoboCasa with 11.1x inference speedup.

title: ClawGym II: Exploring Black-Box RL on Agent Harness
finding: Black-box reinforcement learning on unmodified harnesses raises Qwen3-30A3B Pass@1 on ClawGym-Bench by 9.98 points through OpenClaw and 14.81 points through Claude Code.

title: LEGO-RL: Harness-Native Reinforcement Learning for Coding Agents
finding: Mixture-of-experts 35B model trained inside three native coding harnesses; SWE-bench Verified rises 64.0% to 70.4% in OpenHands SDK, 62.4% to 68.2% in Claude Code, 57.2% to 66.6% in OpenCode.

title: Task-Aware Harness Provisioning for LLM Agents in Mission-Critical Infrastructure Operations
finding: Matching harness information to each task lifts liquid-cooling accuracy from 0.652 to 0.715 and matches Reflexion with 48% fewer tokens; power grids favor full provision.

title: Agent Lightning v1.0: Towards Harnessed Agentic RL
finding: Lightweight framework for training inside arbitrary agent harnesses; using 6K examples, reinforcement learning lifts Qwen3.5-9B on SWE-bench Verified from 41.8% to 56.4%, a 14.6-point gain.

title: HarnessRisk: A Lifecycle-Oriented Benchmark for Agent Harness Safety
finding: Lifecycle benchmark of 128 sandboxed cases across three harnesses: attack success ranges from 12.6% to 80.9%, and some configurations detect risks in over 90% of runs yet stay attackable.

title: SemaPLC: A Project-Grounded, Verification-Gated Agent Harness for PLC Code Generation
finding: Verification-gated programmable logic controller code harness reaches a 72.6% mean verified-pass rate across seven backbones, 8.7 points above the strongest baseline; KUKA's deployment reports a 45% efficiency gain.

title: Harness Continual Learning: Continual Adaptation Beyond Model Parameters
finding: Harness continual learning with guarded evolution gains over 10% relative to baselines in multiple settings, and controlled sweeps measure harness-level forgetting.

title: Task-CoEvolve: Efficient Harness Optimization via Adaptive Validation Task Selection
finding: Adaptive validation task selection matches full-set search final performance while cutting optimization evaluations by 80%, on online text classification and Terminal-Bench 2.1.

title: Applying Anthropic Primitives at Large Enterprises: Harness Paradigm for Knowledge Work
finding: Argues large enterprises should run one unmodified coding-agent harness as shared infrastructure with credential-scoped tools; the abstract reports no measured results.

title: Bounded Loops: Pre-Run Spend Bounds, Proved Termination, and Verified Completion for Agent Harnesses
finding: Proves a bounded-loop harness terminates and neither drifts nor overspends; the instrument found 47 vacuous gates in shipped, reviewed code across a 69-loop catalogue.

title: Graph Engineering in the Era of LLM Agents: From Individual Intelligence to System Intelligence
finding: Review proposing Graph Engineering, explicit evolving graphs of tasks, agents and states, as the next paradigm beyond prompt, context, harness and loop engineering; no measurements.

title: HiMA-MDD: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Harness for Interpretable Multimodal Depression Detection in Clinical Interviews
finding: Three-layer multi-agent harness scores depression from clinical interviews with an auditable evidence trace; beats compared state-of-the-art methods on E-DAIC with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as backbone.

title: AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces
finding: Automatic harness optimization from agent failure traces adds 9.0, 9.6 and 10.0 percentage points over base harnesses on GAIA2, SWE-Bench Pro and Terminal-Bench 2.0.

title: From Natural Language Policies to Executable Obligations: A Verification Harness for Dependable In-Car LLM Agents
finding: Verify-and-revise harness for in-car agents compiles written policy into machine-checkable rules and 25 deterministic gates, with a bounded revision loop tuned for the pass-k metric.

title: MetaCaster: Meta-Harness-Optimized Agent for End-to-End Few-Shot Learning of Lightweight Time Series Forecasters
finding: A meta-harness-optimized agent prepares lightweight time series forecasters from a few examples, tested on 18 datasets, showing data and compute efficiency.

title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
finding: Open-source harness raises ARC-AGI-3 score from 30% to 95.5% and matches or exceeds native and popular harnesses on coding, kernel, emulator and speedrun tasks.

title: Feedback That Backfires: Why Small Language Model Agents Repeat the Call They Just Watched Fail
finding: Feeding a failed call back to small models makes them repeat it: repeat log-probability rises from 0.06 to 0.54; a runtime-written failure description removes 76% of the effect.

title: Beyond Executable Models: The Pufibara Agent Harness and the Modelica Agent Workflow Benchmark for Physical System Modeling
finding: Pufibara harness passes 202 of 232 Modelica tasks against 185 and 187 for Claude Code under matched backends, with 76.4-82.5% lower logical-token totals.

title: The Empire, Long Divided, Must Unite: Architectural Convergence in Three LLM Agent Harnesses
