finding: Source study of three open coding-agent harnesses finds convergence on five shared elements; none has external verifiability, a tamper-evident record an outside party can check.

title: VideoHarness-RSI: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Long-Video Understanding with Frozen Vision-Language Models
finding: Recursive search discovers context-construction programs around a frozen vision-language model, keeping its advantage under matched visual-token control and transferring to other long-video benchmarks.

title: StarHarness: Evolving Harnesses with Stratified Search for Enterprise Environments
finding: Harness evolution with weights fixed adds 20-35 percentage points over the default harness on three enterprise benchmarks, persists on held-out tasks, and transfers across GPT and Qwen families.

title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses
finding: Recursive working-memory harness improves 35 of 37 model-benchmark pairs, adding 15.6 to 17.8 points on tau-bench for frontier models and up to 32.2 points on the longest tasks.

title: Harness Engineering for Predictable Agentic Systems: An Empirical Study of Deterministic Execution Constraints
finding: Schema-validated structured planning makes three of four model-task cells fully reproducible (rate 1.000 at sample size 100); a first-pass harness helped one cell and hurt two.

title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
finding: A trained model writes task-specific harnesses on the fly: with it, DeepSeek-V4-Flash beats GPT-5.6 on DeepSearchQA by 9.1 points, and the strong GLM-5.2 gains up to 20.2.

title: From General Agents to RCA Experts: A Self-Evolving Harness for Root Cause Analysis
finding: Self-evolving root cause analysis harness reaches 59.0% top-1 accuracy, 63.4% above the bare general agent, across two public benchmarks and an industrial deployment.

title: Same Model, Different Harness: Different Coding-Agent Results
finding: Same coding model under a context-shortening harness: on 169 tight-window tasks, complete SWE-bench Verified solutions rise from 43 to 72; model and harness must be tested together.

title: When Context Gets Root: Privilege Escalation in LLM Harnesses
finding: Harness context construction can raise attacker content to a higher instruction level; attacks reached all 13 objectives on all six coding-agent harnesses with unrestricted execution.

title: Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification
finding: Verifying harness changes only on behavior-relevant tasks, with attributable evidence, improves held-out performance by 7.6-13.6% across three harnesses with much less evaluation budget.

title: Credo: Reusable Declarative Primitives for Agentic Workflows
finding: Proposes storing searched harnesses as tagged, provenance-carrying declarative primitives that a compiler reuses for new tasks instead of searching again; preliminary results only.

title: openJiuwen: Beyond Static Harnesses for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
finding: Open-source coding-agent harness scores 82.6% on SWE-bench Verified and 87.19% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 3.4 and 3.39 points above the strongest official leaderboard estimates.

title: EvoUndo: Recoverability-Constrained Self-Evolution for LLM Agent Harnesses
finding: 197 of 600 self-evolution mutations that raised capability failed recovery checks; an extended recovery language lifts oracle recovery from 48 to 191 of 197, with model-dependent interactions.

title: Harness-RL: Black-Box Reinforcement Learning with Action-Args Decoupling for Central-Agent Multi-Agent Harnesses
finding: Reinforcement learning for the central agent of multi-agent harnesses splits action and argument gradients; reaches average F1 scores of 42.93 and 47.79 with 1.5B and 3B Qwen models.

title: Towards Agentic Cloud Engineering: Graph and Loop Engineering with a Zero-Trust Agent Harness
finding: Zero-trust harness with graph, loop and harness engineering turns cloud engineering tasks into verified Google Cloud deployments, or into an auditable failure under bounded recovery.

title: CUDA-Harness: Harnessing Agentic CUDA Kernel Generation and Optimization from Natural Language
finding: Agentic framework generates CUDA kernels from natural language, using synthesized isolated tests to dilute reward hacking and correctness-first evolution to improve performance.

title: Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents
finding: Self-improving agents' harness edits can fake gains or break integrity; audits of real trajectories show tampering recurs and persists in the best agent's lineage.

title: Graph, Loop, and Harness Engineering for Zero-Trust Agentic Data Engineering and Analytical Processing
finding: Two zero-trust frameworks: one for cloud data engineering, one for analytical queries that release answers only after same-snapshot execution and exact result equivalence checks.

title: Scaffolding Foundation Models into Physical-World Agents Pushes the Frontier of Long-Horizon Navigation
finding: Scaffolding that couples a vision-language model with a navigation executor beats an episodic interface by 14.9 points on HM-EQA and reaches 78.3% success on a Unitree Go2 robot.

title: Reining in an Agentic Harness for High Energy Physics
finding: Position: stable scientific operations should become versioned, machine-readable components that general harnesses can specialize for high energy physics; no measurements given.

title: WHALE: A Simple Recipe for Joint Harness-Weight Optimization
finding: Alternating weight updates and harness search beats weight-only, harness-only and Fast-Slow training by 4.15-24.38 points in best mean@8 accuracy on Qwen3.5-2B and 4B agents.

title: Memory as Infrastructure: Reliability Engineering for Persistent Agent Memory in Months-Long LLM-Assisted Development
finding: Months-long operational record of one project's memory harness: 85 recorded failures, none silent, plus a pre-registered ablation protocol; one project, no control arm, self-reported.

title: Runtime-Independent Persistent Agents: Preserving Identity, Memory, and Code Across Models, Harnesses, and Servers
finding: Persistent agents keep identity, memory and code across model, harness, host and chat-surface swaps; continuity is shown in tested deployments, not behavioral equivalence or unattended reliability.

title: Agentic programs: an emerging form of scientific software in computational materials science
finding: Position: recent harnesses enable agentic programs that combine deterministic algorithms with bounded model judgment, illustrated by DeMARS for atomistic models of disordered crystals.

title: MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw
finding: Self-distillation method (SDCC) closes the train-rollout log-probability gap that context compression creates, including for black-box harnesses such as Claude Code and OpenCode.

title: What's in Your Agent's Context? Context Privilege Escalation Attacks against AI Agent Harness
finding: Systematic analysis of context assembly in 12 real harnesses, including Claude Code and Codex, finds two privilege-escalation attack classes with outcomes from full agent compromise to remote code execution.

title: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
finding: Benchmark: models building agent harnesses from scratch produce harnesses that trail human references on code and search, match or exceed them on writing and ML, and evolution gains are unstable.

title: Harness-of-Harness: Multi-Day Autonomous Software Development with Continual Improvement
finding: Wrapper improves three standalone coding harnesses by an average 52.25 percent relative gain after three iterations, maximum 82.86 percent, and builds a playable game over 70 iterations.

title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
finding: Benchmark of 1,200 questions on how models reason about component teardown in dynamic agent harnesses; models handle small systems well but grow less reliable as relevant interactions increase.

title: Harness Engineering in LLM Tool Use via Agent-Native Reusable Tool Primitives
finding: Harness with planner, router and verifier over natural-language tool primitives beats fine-tuned models by 10% and frontier models by 6% on average, cutting API cost by up to 85%.

title: Measuring the Microtask Eligibility Gap: When Is an Off-the-Shelf SLM Enough for an Agent Harness?
finding: Zero of 16 small-model configurations (four microtasks, four Qwen3 sizes) pass practitioner thresholds; the paper advises placing small models behind a baseline that meets the threshold.

title: Improving Evaluation Realism with Inference-Time Compute and Deployment Scaffolds
finding: Deployment-imitating agent harness and inference-time critique make simulated alignment tests harder to tell from real deployment; applying both gives larger realism gains than either alone.

title: CORAL: An LLM-Native Harness for Production Recommender Systems
finding: Language-model agent loop reconfigures a production recommender: in A/B tests it lifts engagement at no added serving cost on one platform and cuts serving cost without losing engagement on another.

title: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
finding: Co-evolves a safety prompt, skills and a reinforcement-learned policy; for Qwen3.5-4B, attack success on AgentDojo falls threefold while benign utility rises from 59.79% to 61.86%.

title: SHELF: A Synthetic Harness for Multi-Task Bibliographic Benchmarking
finding: SHELF generates synthetic benchmark data from library classification schemes; subject classification reaches 0.8887 while genre-form classification reaches only 0.2605.

title: What Do CAE Simulation Agents Really Need Beyond a Generic Harness?
finding: Generic single-agent harness matches or beats specialized multi-agent simulation systems (FoamBench 96.4% vs 88.2%); specialized machinery suited weak base models, and domain tutorials are the largest measured gain.

title: Bioinfoysis Technical Report
finding: Multi-agent bioinformatics harness with validated handoffs lifts average accuracy across four models: SeqQA2 from 27.81% to 64.13%, DbQA2 from 3.13% to 31.25%; BixBench reaches 82.4%.

title: A Blind Trust, the Bloody Thrust: When Attacker-Controlled Hook Updates Steer AI Agent Harnesses towards Malicious Behaviors
finding: Attacker-controlled lifecycle-hook updates trojanize benign plugins; HookPry compromises all seven tested harnesses, reaching 92.5% per-harness success, while Microsoft Defender has 0% recall.

title: SWE-Gate: Passing Functional Tests Is Not Enough for Software Engineering Agents
finding: Benchmark adding review constraints to repair tasks: of 644 repairs passing functional tests, 221 break review constraints, so functional-only evaluation overestimates agent ability.

title: EvoHarnessBench: Can Your Agents Keep Pace with an Evolving Harness?
finding: Benchmark of 17 harness-evolution streams finds that harness expansion alone can degrade previously solved tasks, and self-evolution gains are inconsistent across stages and environments.

title: Harbor Adapters and Harbor-Index: Infrastructure and a Curated Meta-Dataset for Large-Scale Agentic Evaluation
finding: Adapters port more than 80 agentic benchmarks; 8 models run with Terminus-2 and three native harnesses; on the curated Harbor-Index no configuration exceeds 30% pass rate, best 28.0%.

title: Multi-Harness Reinforcement Learning for Coding Agents: Training Gains and Harness Dependence
finding: Harness choice moves SWE-bench Verified solve rates by 7.13 points, more than reinforcement learning gains of 0.48 to 0.77 points; gains do not transfer reliably to unseen harnesses.

title: From Language Models to World-Acting Systems: Progress and Limits of Agentic AI across Digital, Social, Virtual, and Physical Environments
finding: Critical review finds action-interface expansion documented better than robust completion, recovery, authorization or independent verification; proposes justified delegation as a heuristic, not a score.

title: RefactorPlatform: An Open-Source Harness for Controlled Evaluation of Repository-Scale Refactoring Agents
finding: Open-source refactoring harness: a lean retrieval-augmented single agent scores 86% versus 66% for the sub-agent design on matched tasks; retrieval's gains absorb its token overhead.

title: Beyond Prompts: Measuring and Optimizing LLM Tool-Agent Harnesses
finding: Protocol reports harness lift, worst-condition lift and repeatability; PRISM gains 14.2, 14.9 and 10.1 points on three tool-use benchmarks, though some optimizers still pick brittle updates.

title: EvoSafeHarness: Evolving Model- and Domain-Specific Harnesses for Securing Agents
finding: Evolves a safety harness per deployment: attack success on DecodingTrust-Agent falls from 50.9% to 12.6% for direct attacks, at a 3.3-point utility cost.

title: From Narrative to Auditable Forecasts: A Structured Scaffold for Agentic Forecasting
finding: Structured forecasting scaffold anchors a quantitative baseline and aggregates factor updates in odds space; beats agentic baselines and costlier deep-research agents on accuracy and calibration.

title: CHART: A Harness-Rotation Curriculum for Harness-Robust Search Agents
finding: Training a search agent across rotating harnesses keeps parallel search on 89% of held-out turns, versus at most 5% for fixed pools; single-harness training makes the behavior fragile.

title: Predictors and Orchestrators: Parsimonious Machine Learning within an Agentic AI Harness for Multi-Horizon Karst Aquifer Forecasting
finding: Gradient-boosted trees forecast Edwards Aquifer spring discharge and groundwater level best over 1-12 weeks (coefficient of determination at least 0.94); a five-agent architecture automates the workflow.

title: Scanning the Harness: Configuration Exposures in AI Coding-Agent Supply Chains
finding: Of 2,660 coding-agent setups, 15.4% carry an exposure: unpinned tool-server package declarations in 9.8%, broad execution grants in 2.5%, broad skill preapprovals in 3.8%.

title: Search-to-World: Evaluation of 3D World Delivery from User Request through Web Search
finding: Benchmark and metrics for turning web search results into 3D worlds: observing relevant content does not ensure world delivery, and delivery depends on the underlying agent model.

title: VEX-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Assessing Exploitability of Software Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
finding: Benchmark of 75 real-world supply-chain vulnerability cases: about 80% F1 on binary exploitability status, but only GPT-5.5 passes 70% macro-F1 on fine-grained justifications.

title: A Theory of Reliable Self-Evolution for Agent Harnesses
finding: Theory: a self-evolved harness can be adopted reliably under a validation rule with guarantees, and the ceiling on progressive improvement is set by verification and evaluation costs.

title: NeoHorse-1: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
finding: Post-training on routing records and evaluation feedback raises macro-average from 58.94 to 64.87 at 4B and 65.60 to 69.04 at 9B, narrowing the gap to the 9B base model.

title: Authority Is Not a String: A Capability-Scoped Harness for Prompt-Injection-Resistant Coding Agents
finding: Harness-level capability checks on each tool call cut injected-action executions from 33-47 of 75 runs to 3 of 75 while completing 68 of 75 repairs, against 68-72 for baselines.

title: Experience Funnel: A State-Policy Alternating Loop for Self-Evolving Agents
finding: Alternates fast textual-state adaptation with slow policy consolidation; consistently beats state-only evolution and policy-internalization approaches across diverse agent benchmarks.

title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
finding: Imitating a stronger expert's full trajectories regresses a weaker model 4 to 30 points on seven enterprise tasks under the evolved harness; correcting only failing turns on-policy keeps the gains.

title: Benchmarking Hybrid Deep Research Across Database Querying and Web Search
finding: Benchmark of 380 tasks needing both web search and SQL for one verifiable answer; GLM-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.6 and GPT-5 reach only about 50-54% Pass@8 on the hard subset.

title: Code-to-Harness: Distilling Black-Box Optimizers from Self-Play
finding: Text harness distilled from executable practice cuts Gemini Flash regret by 48% in an independent study and transfers to Claude Sonnet; an independent replication reaches the same performance tier.

title: Benchmarking Agentic HLS Design Tasks With HLS-Eval
finding: Extends HLS-Eval with an agentic flow for high-level synthesis design (file tools, compiler self-check); open-source models with the harness solve every simple generation task.

title: Harness or Model? Isolating the Harness Effect in Agentic Coding with a Contamination-Controlled Private Suite
finding: Same-model contrasts on 80 private tasks show no average harness advantage: Opus 4.8 is -1.25 points (interval -10.0 to +7.5), GPT-5.5 is +1.25 points (interval -4.4 to +6.9).

title: RobustSGPO: Search-Space Control for Agent Harness Evolution
finding: Search-space control with checked patches and retained snapshots lifts completion on 30 held-out tasks from 60.0% to 80.0% under a 20-million-token budget.

title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
finding: Semantic action interface lets closed-source frontier vision-language models control robots zero-shot, and small open-source models adapt with a few hours of fine-tuning; no added model capacity is claimed.

title: Auto-RecSys: Harnessing Autonomous Research Agents for Industry-Scale Recommender System
finding: Research system runs recommender experiments in parallel with recoverable execution and self-evolving playbooks; reduces human time per cycle and improves execution reliability as playbooks mature.

title: Harness Robotic OS: A Unified Embodied-Agent Runtime for Closed-Loop Quadruped Inspection
finding: Harness Robotic OS unifies robot runtime, agent runtime and operations for quadruped inspection; the prototype reaches 100% waypoint reachability and 99% success in alarm delivery and report generation.

title: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents
finding: Aggregating failures that recur across tasks before changing a harness improves reasoning accuracy of evolved harnesses by 18.56% over existing harness evolution and trains up to 1.84 times faster.

title: COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization
finding: Contextual-bandit scheduling of skill evaluations cuts optimization cost 55-58% relative to SkillOpt across six benchmarks using 50 examples each, and stays robust to harness changes.

title: Online Video Agent Harness for Long Video Understanding
finding: Video agent harness with on-demand expert tools matches frontier-level results on MINERVA using about 15% of a 1,024-frame dense baseline's context, and still works with a text-only orchestrator.

title: Tasks over Application Manuals: Revealing Gaps in Long-Horizon Procedural Reasoning for Language Models
finding: Benchmark of long rule-based procedures from clinical coding and federal sentencing: best exact-match is 1% on ICD-10-CM coding and 15.5% on sentencing, even with an agent-harness baseline on GPT-5.

title: Asclepius: An Adaptive Harness for Long-Horizon Clinical Agents
finding: Self-evolving clinical harness improves critical-action correctness by 22% over a strong baseline agent framework on held-out batches while keeping diagnostic accuracy; the three components must act together.

title: HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning
finding: Online scheduler chooses one harness per training step for a 2-billion-parameter Qwen agent trained across six harnesses, improving over mixed-batch training on PinchBench and ClawEval.

title: When Malicious Instructions Persist: Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack on Harness-Based Agents
finding: Malicious instructions planted in external sources make harness agents write poisoned persistent memory: injection success 73.7% on OpenClaw and 66.9% on Claude Code; a prompt-level defense fails after poisoning.

title: Fabrication After Tool Failure: Tool-Augmented Agents Assert Values Their Tools Did Not Return
finding: Tool-augmented models assert values their failed tools never returned in 14.10% of responses; one sentence requiring an OK or FAILED status flag cuts this to 0.87%.

title: OmniHarness: Harnessing Generalizable Visual Generation via Symbolic Policy Learning
finding: Symbolic policies distilled from verified executions raise the ComfyBench Creative resolve rate to 95.0%, 27.5 points above the strongest baseline; frozen snapshots plug into existing visual agents.

title: Agent Harness Awareness: Turning Verified Telemetry into Operational Control for Tool-Using Agents
finding: Giving the model verified tool-health state before each action cut mean regret 96.9% against a neutral control and raised single-dispatch completion from 69.4% to 95.8% across three models.

title: ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
finding: Evolves five harness modules separately on 2,000 tasks disjoint from evaluation benchmarks; improvements hold on unseen tasks for TB2.0 and SWE-Bench Verified and transfer across foundation models.

title: MUSE: A Theory-Harnessed Story Engine for Vibe Narrativizing
finding: Story-theory harness improves WritingBench by 1.1 to 6.2 points over zero-shot generation across four base models, the only multi-stage system in the comparison to do so.

title: HarnessVLN: Unifying Training-Free Embodied Navigation through an Agent Harness
finding: Training-free navigation harness validates planner proposals before dispatch and reaches 59.6%, 51.4%, 76.0% and 59.3% success on R2R, RxR, HM3D-v2 and HM3D-OVON.

title: The Router Within: Eliciting Native Skill Routing from a Frozen LLM
finding: Reads skill routing from a frozen model's own passes via two trained linear maps; on Qwen3-32B it beats retrieval pipelines by up to 13.4 points, and 21.9 mid-rollout.

title: Stellar Colosseum: A Many-Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Research in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
finding: Many-agent harness allocates inference across proof routes with a readiness gate and section-level subproblems; with Gemini 3.1 Pro it reaches 71.0% on TCS-Bench and solves 218 of 222 Codeforces problems.

title: Agentic Societies Need a Social Harness
finding: Position: in agent societies even honest agents often fail under current harnesses and messaging, so a social harness must manage agent-to-agent interactions through a layered architecture.

title: Reflections on Trusting Trust, Revisited: Contaminating Self-Modifying AI Coding Agents with Poisoned Benchmarks
finding: Poisoned benchmarks can make self-modifying coding agents evolve instructions that disable certificate checks for secure web connections; contamination persists after clean re-evolution, shown on Hyperagents with Sonnet 4.5.

title: BENCHCOMPASS: From Scores to Signals for Training and Harness Decisions in Payment-Domain LLMs
finding: Payment-domain benchmark across 16 model variants: best frontier model reaches 89.6% on context-grounded reasoning and 81.7% under attacked inputs, versus 69.8% and 42.6% for a 32B open-weight model.

title: Bad Genius: Counterfactual-Guided Harness Evolution Beyond Task-Specific Shortcuts
finding: Counterfactual benchmark transformations expose harness-evolution shortcuts: CHASE keeps released-benchmark gains on Syn-Ledger and OfficeQA while substantially reducing gains lost under valid protocol changes.

title: AeroWeaver: An Embodied-Agent Harness for Weaving Aerial Skills into Distributed, Adaptive Swarm Execution
finding: Embodied harness for drone swarms connects language model decisions to governed skills and role-based local agents; reports valid skill execution under tested conditions, without central joint actions.

title: GAVEL: Graph World Models for Verified and Efficient Long-Horizon LLM Task Planning
finding: Explicit graph world model harness verifies and repairs language model robot plans: with Qwen3-8B, single-task success on BEHAVIOR-1K rises from 41.2% to 91.8% and multi-task from 19.9% to 92.6%.

title: From Rollout to Reset: A Graph-Based Harness for Autonomous Long-Horizon Manipulation Evaluation
finding: Graph harness with a language model restores scenes in 76% of long-horizon Franka episodes versus 52% for AutoEval, and cuts operator time by 72% against manual reset.

title: How Do Agent Harnesses Create Value? Planning Information and Release Control in Stateful LLM Agents
finding: Task-specific plans raise oracle-verified success 7.17 points over a word-matched shuffled-text control; a read-only verifier rejects 61% of invalid Retail episodes at under one cent per episode.

title: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness
finding: Four harness mechanisms match Pi on 51 EdgeBench tasks across two frontier models, cutting recorded token traffic 44.7-49.0% and cost by about one third.

title: Inference-Engine Fingerprinting Attacks are Practical: Exploring Model-Driven Environmental Discovery, Exploitation, and Escape
finding: Shows a misaligned model can fingerprint its inference engine from output tokens alone and then exploit it; agentic harnesses let it identify the local engine.

title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
finding: Across four models and 176 settings, planning cuts cost for stronger models but mainly helps weaker ones' accuracy; context management matters most as the window tightens.

title: Coding Agents with Harness for Safe Robot Control
finding: Obstacle-aware harness lifts a robot-controlling coding agent to 81.2% task success and 91.9% collision avoidance with GPT-6-Astra, 31.2 points above no harness.

title: Presage: Prefetch Search via Agent-Guided Experiments
finding: Multi-agent software-prefetch harness yields a 10% geometric-mean speedup across 81 workloads and 17% on its own suite, versus 10% for the prior best approach.

title: From Capability to Assurance in Autonomous Penetration-Testing Harnesses: A Framework and Reference Implementation
finding: Defines five assurance properties penetration-testing harnesses should enforce in code, each with an acceptance test; running them on NeuroSploit exposed a real authorization gap, with no performance comparison.

title: A Design-Intent-Preserving Agent Harness for Parametric CAD Modeling
finding: Harness binds CAD modeling commands to explicit geometry references, raising static shape-match scores by 11.1% and 5.6% and edit-case scores by 7.0% and 4.2%.

title: CraftBench-UE: Deterministic Evaluation for Coding Agents in Unreal Engine
finding: Deterministic evaluation harness: on paired tasks C++ completes 30.0-42.9 points more often than Blueprint, and 42.2-50.0% of Blueprint submissions that pass asset checks fail runtime assertions.

title: Divergent strategies and convergent outcomes in autonomous materials discovery
finding: Sixteen runs of one model-harness setup reached the same materials frontier; enforced checks raised fresh-run reproduction from one of eight to eight of eight, but not conclusion validity.

title: Self-Healing Harness for Runtime Oversight of Agent Self-Modification
finding: Of 383 rejected self-edits, 211 (55%) fixed their trigger failure but broke a working case; the harness scores higher in all 16 matched pairs and is more reliable in 12.

title: MimicAgent: Quadruped Skills via Prompt-to-Trajectory Generation
finding: Coding agents inside a harness write quadruped reference motions; with one model, 87% of prompts yield semantically aligned trajectories for training deployable policies.

title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
finding: Regularized harness evolution gains up to 6.0 points on its training split and 4.3 points on five unseen benchmarks, with a harness using 30% fewer policy tokens.

title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
finding: Harness-guided training lifts the base model from 23.3% to 44.3% with the harness removed, above the 41.7% reached with the harness still attached.

title: Qwen3.8-Omni: Towards Native Omni-Modal Agents
finding: Releases an omni-modal agent model with a one-million-token context and two open-source harness frameworks; the abstract gives no harness-level measurements.

title: FIRE: Failure-Informed Runtime Engineering for Reliable Language-Model Agents
finding: Runtime policies raise repeated success over two attempts in all three GPT-5.6 tiers, such as 64.4% to 73.6% for Sol; in a randomized test, 61% succeed with policies versus 39% without.

title: Autonomous Quantum Transport Measurements of 2D Semiconductors by an AI Agent
finding: Agent harness runs multi-day quantum transport measurements on MoS2 devices end to end, determining spin-orbit coupling in monolayer and mapping a bilayer phase diagram.

title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
finding: Code harness keeps 44.7-45.3% success across 4B to 120B models while tool calling falls to 6.7% at 4B, and cuts model calls by 76.0-91.8%.

title: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents
finding: Orchestrator-free harness with 1,024 self-organizing agents raises the pandoc test-pass rate from 33.89% to 55.06%; 1 to 128 agents lift ProgramBench tasks from 19.31% to 28.78%.

title: Harness as a Language: A Minimalist Agent Framework With Maximal Expressivity
finding: Single-primitive harness, using prompting only, beats Letta by 8% on long-recall tasks at half the cost and ACE by 4% on AppWorld at lower cost.

title: Unmodeled states and uncertain action outcomes in agentic scanning tunneling microscopy
finding: Agent harness puts a language model in a scanning tunneling microscope feedback loop; frontier agents autonomously conditioned a tip and passed verification, but hidden states limited them.

title: EVAGE: Autonomous MEV Generation and Adaptation via Multi-Agent Harness
finding: Multi-agent harness writes maximal extractable value bot code offline; it finds five Ethereum strategy variants with 1.02x to 15.97x profit increases for under 60 dollars of model cost.

title: RegenHarness: A Robot Agent Harness with Evidence-Gated Recursive Self-Improvement
finding: Evidence-gated harness self-improvement changes only configuration, never trusted task state; a quadruped robot completes voice-triggered warehouse missions with linked receipts.

title: Who Is Behind the Harness? Fingerprinting LLMs through Agentic Behavior
finding: Coding-agent behavior under three probe pairs identifies which model sits behind a harness across 36 models, with high top-1 accuracy and outperforming four baselines.

title: A Harness for Synthesizing Diverse Naturalistic Full-Duplex Conversations
finding: Synthesized intent-labeled two-channel speech helps the Moshi speech model take turns; with reference context its frame-level floor F1 rises from 0.893 to 0.962.

title: ElectrolyteMD-Bench: How Well Do AI Agents Conduct Molecular Dynamics Studies across Electrolyte Solvation Regimes?
finding: Across eight model-harness setups, all 24 system runs produced valid trajectories, yet none of eight studies met every scientific requirement; completion claims outran retained evidence.

title: Automatic Harness Evolution for Hardware Design Verification: Can LLMs Consolidate Gains Across Discovered Harnesses?
finding: Evolved harnesses raised completed attempts 71-76% but total correct attempts only 18-24%; the strongest reproducible gain improved just one task.

title: Harness Tokenomics: A Router for the Enterprise Agentic Control Plane
finding: A calibrated router recovers 13-21% of model spend, 3.3 to 5.1 million dollars a year across an emulated 10,000-seat enterprise, and the top-priced model can cost less on long sessions.

title: Calibrated Decision Models for Autonomous Penetration-Testing Harnesses: JEV and Laya as System One Decision Layers for LLM-Driven Pentest Agents
finding: Proposes calibrated classifiers for four harness decisions; one exploratory run with and without them shows severity and runtime differences, but no statistical significance.

title: Where Does Exactly-Once Live? Model, Harness, and Tool-Contract Effects on Duplicate Side Effects in LLM Agents
finding: Across 25,930 episodes, frontier models rarely duplicate a write (0.5%) when a read-back reveals the outcome but duplicate 56-74% when it cannot; the harness barely matters.

title: HarnessPAI: An Evolving Harness for Physical AI
finding: Code-based harness evolves executable programs for embodied robots across arms, household robots, a vacuum and a walker; the converged program also generates training data for action models.

title: AdaHVLA: Adaptive Harnesses for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Execution
finding: Adaptive harness refines robot coordination code from execution evidence; NaVILA-LH simulation success rises from 22.5% to 57.5%, and manipulation gains reach 30.8 points.

title: Policy as Code: A Coroutine-Bridge Harness for Fast-Reasoning Reliability on CAR-bench
finding: Harness whose action is a Python program wins CAR-bench Track 2 with a 60.0% triple-trial pass rate, 4.5x the baseline; cache-stable prompts served 78% of input tokens from cache.

title: Robo-Harness K1: Harnessing Robot-Use Agents via Perception Augmentation
finding: Perception tools lift Gemini to 77.8% and GPT-6 Astra to 88.9% on LIBERO-PRO, versus 61.1% for Astra with an RGB-only harness; a 9B student reaches 44.2% on new initial states.

title: Demystifying Agent Skills for Smart Contract Auditing: Design, Effectiveness, Behavioral Impact
finding: Skill effectiveness depends mainly on the model rather than the harness; Codex with GPT-5.5 gains most, raising detection score 22.8% and captured award 43.2%.

title: World Action Agent: Harnessing VLMs for Robot Manipulation via World Action Rehearsal
finding: Vision-language-model harness reaches 75.6% average success on LIBERO-Pro, beating end-to-end and code-policy agents; fine-tuning a 9B model on its traces lifts out-of-domain success from 1.7% to 43.3%.

title: What Will Remain Human in Software Architecture? A Focus Group Report
finding: Focus group of 22 practitioners agreed architectural decisions, accountability and guardrails stay human; harness engineering emerged as the discipline of governing automated system creation.

title: AGATE: Provenance-Based Runtime Defense Against Compositional Attacks on LLM Agents
finding: Deterministic provenance gate at harness boundaries decides without a model; replay matches live graph results in all 63 scenarios, but six of eleven benign file scenarios trigger denials.

title: MoMHa: Multi-Objective Optimization of LLM Harnesses over Accuracy, Safety, and Tokens
finding: Joint-reward harness search scores 0.482 on synthetic suites versus 0.198-0.422 for ten baselines and reaches the top measured behavioral safety composite, 0.781.

title: MammoClaw: Towards Skill-Evolving Agent Harness for Breast Cancer Mammography Analysis
finding: Tools alone did not reliably improve mammography analysis; skills evolved from failed runs improved tool use and performance in some settings. The abstract gives no figures.

title: CP-Agent: A Harness-Engineered Agent for Crystal Plasticity Simulation Workflows
finding: Harness with typed tools and a bounded loop runs crystal plasticity workflows; across four case studies the agent inferred the correct sequence and gave consistent results across repeated runs.

title: Omni-IO Skills: Harnessing Your Agent Omni-Native
finding: On UniM-90, the harness raises input-support rates of GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5 from 40.00% and 38.89% to 100%, and quality scores from 26.99 to 74.94 and 27.82 to 77.78.

title: Methodological Harness in Agentic Software Engineering: An Empirical Study on Mining Software Repositories
finding: Across 5,435 repositories with agent activity, 21.7% show at least one harness mechanism versus 65.3% of the most visible; multi-mechanism configurations are rare.

title: AI Harness: Certification under Proposal-Conditioned Information for Foundation-Model Agents
finding: Shows a harness that sees only model state can lose certifiability; observing the proposal before intervention restores safe action when hidden modes need incompatible interventions.

title: HM-ROUTER: Joint Model and Harness Routing for Agentic Systems
finding: Router choosing a model-harness pair per query beats the strongest learned baseline by 7.3 points in mean routing accuracy across 293 routes, 73 models and 25 harnesses.

title: SCLATE: a Substrate for Continual-Learning Agent Training and Evaluation
finding: Ten unmodified harness-memory configurations on ten models show added memory does not reliably beat native memory; a post-trained 4B model gains 16.7 points on SWE-bench Verified.

title: PluginRSI: Recursive Improvement of Agent Harnesses with Reusable Plugins
finding: Harness built from reusable plugins beats existing harness optimizers across software, command-line and question-answering tasks, and the evolved plugin library speeds later optimization.

title: Beyond the Model: Demystifying Harness Effects in Software Engineering Agents
finding: Complex harness components give diminishing gains on issue repair as models strengthen but help stronger models on open-ended repository tasks; NanoHarness adds 7.37 and 6.21 points.

title: Hearsay: Can an Auditor Trust the Record a Deployed Agent Harness Writes?
finding: Examiners name the right fault in 74-91% of 140 runs, but fewer than one in ten citations land on anything the harness did not write; an outside append-only log catches all 28 planted omissions.

title: Silent Failures in Agentic Security Evaluation: A Validated Harness for Tool-Call Mediation Under Indirect Prompt Injection
finding: Auditing an injection benchmark harness finds four defect classes; the tool-identity scorer reports 21.7% attack success where the argument-level rate is 1.2%, and a 62.8% model scores 0% once corrected.

title: Beyond Token Savings: A Systematic Study of Context Compression in LLM Agents
finding: Across nearly 35,000 runs of three open-weight models, fewer tokens did not mean faster runs: one compression policy used a third of the tokens yet ran 20-80% longer on Terminal-Bench.

title: More Programs or More Rolls? Separating Coverage from Specialization in LLM Harnesses
finding: Identical baseline copies show 2.16 points of repeat-averaged headroom; generated harnesses give repeatable patterns, but the frozen selector gains 0.00 points, so coverage alone proves nothing.

title: Compositional Safety Failures in Harness Evolution: Identification and Runtime Monitoring
finding: Individually safe harness component updates combine into unsafe behavior: 43 pairwise and 18 three-way failures found; a hypergraph monitor rechecks only the changed interactions.

title: LiteEvo: Automated, Cost-Efficient Harness Evolution for Generalization to Unseen Tasks
finding: Automated harness evolution on a frozen 9B model lifts pass-at-two by 10.5-67.7 points across five benchmarks, matching a reproduced HarnessX at lower service cost.

title: Long-Horizon Analog Design Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hours-Long Analog and Mixed-Signal Circuit Design Tasks
finding: Fifty analog circuit tasks: 15 agent setups pass 8.0-78.0%; longer budgets help, general skill documents add little, and a reference topology adds 18.7 points for one model.

title: Recursive Harness Distillation across Agents for Robot Manipulation
finding: Playbook distilled from a strong agent lifts real-world manipulation success from 37.3% to 64.0%; on SimplerEnv Bridge a light agent with it reaches 66.7%, above the strong agent without it.

title: MetaBench-Harness: Unlocking End-to-End Optimization of Benchmark Harnesses
finding: Dual-loop harness search evolves benchmark generation for CodeContests and AIME-2024 that stays challenging for frontier models; the abstract reports no score.

title: Raven: The Harness of Harnesses for Composable Agentic Intelligence
finding: Open-source ecosystem builds and evolves domain harnesses and routes subtasks among them; claims significant gains over state-of-the-art agent systems, with no figures in the abstract.

title: SecProbe: Adaptive Evaluation of Coding Agents on Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities
finding: Adaptive evaluation estimates coding-agent ability with item response theory and synthesizes tasks; success peaks at 28.33%, with up to 29.5% fewer tasks than random for similar estimates.

title: Vestrum: Improving Agent Harnesses by Adapting Their Verification, Structure and Memory
finding: Component-level edits lift Claude Code on Terminal-Bench 4 Hard from 63.7% to 70.3% at 1.03x test cost; the method beats the GEPA prompt search in every paired evaluation.

title: Towards Certificate-Driven Software Porting: A Self-Improving Agentic Harness for Scientific Program Optimization
finding: Certificates of failed assumptions raise candidates passing correctness checks from 55% to 90% when porting two particle-simulation functions to graphics processors, reaching 13.78x and 23.54x speedups.

title: GlyphBench: A Playground for Language-Model Reinforcement Learning
finding: Renders game states as character grids; a 4B model trained with reinforcement learning on 100 tasks reaches 63.48% on held-out reasoning problems, above base, math-trained and code-trained baselines.

title: When Harness Beats Scale, and When Reading Beats Both
finding: Program-of-Thoughts harness adds 0.282 joint accuracy to a 7B model but at most 0.005 to a 72B model; a 27B model with the full harness matches the 72B.

title: GenMem: Generative Symbolic Memory for Self-Evolving Harness
finding: Memory agent generates symbolic addresses while evolution rewrites payloads at fixed addresses; the abstract is truncated before its results, so no figures are given.

title: Beyond Skill Evolution: Self-Evolving Context Management Policies for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses
finding: Learned context-management policy starting from the Pi harness matches or beats Codex, OpenCode and OpenClaw on three long-horizon benchmarks; fixed context strategies fall short under information pressure.

title: Timeline-Bench: Evaluating Agents on Realistic Video-Editing Tasks, from Raw Footage to Final Cut
finding: Video-editing benchmark of 56 tasks: the best of 16 agent setups resolves 26.8%, the average 14.0%, and most unresolved runs fail only the quality test.

title: Towards Reliable AI Data Scientists: Data Agents with Workflow Harnesses
finding: Survey organizes data agents into five stages and 15 technical approaches, and names four open reliability problems, including a missing verification-repair resource.

title: Planarian: Managing Agent State with Statepoints
finding: Agent runtime with snapshot, rollback and fork over local and remote state lets agents undo mistakes and explore in parallel, improving task quality by up to 15x at 3% user-recovery overhead.

title: SRHarness: A Harness for Agentic Symbolic Regression
finding: Symbolic-regression harness reaches 93.69% symbolic accuracy with DeepSeek-v4-flash, versus 62.16% for SR-Scientist on the same backbone; plain Codex with the same tools does not match it.

title: AutoRef: Harness Optimization for Agentic Multi-Reference Image Generation
finding: Coding agent rewrites a harness for a frozen 4B open-weight image generator, raising held-out MultiBanana score from 5.72 to 7.37, matching or exceeding proprietary image models.

title: GPUPhysBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Correct and Efficient GPU Physics Simulation
finding: Benchmark of 50 graphics-processor physics tasks: two of six model-harness pairs pass all 50, but the fastest pair reaches 0.9 of reference speed on only 22% of tasks.

title: Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation
finding: Trains a proposer model with reinforcement learning to revise a solver's harness from execution feedback; the test-time revisions transfer to unseen reasoning and question-answering tasks without weight updates.

title: MMSkillRisk: Can Agents Stay Safe When Multimodal Skills Become Traps?
finding: Image-borne instructions inside skills trigger unauthorized actions in all nine model-harness configurations, pooled 43.1% success, 16.4 points above text-carried attacks, while tasks still complete.

title: Strategies for Deploying AI Agents in Production at Scientific User Facilities
finding: Perspective from deployments at a light source distills harness principles for beamline control, facility knowledge retrieval and data analysis, meant to be reused across facilities.

title: Evaluating Bounded Autonomy in Regulated Agentic AI: A Diagnostic Harness with Constitutional Rewards, Escalation Labels, and Runtime Governance
finding: Nominally identical 3B-model setups gave task success 0.25 and 0.12; configuration variance overwhelmed apparent tuning effects, so the authors call for larger sets and repeated runs.

title: Coding LLMs Can Be Harnessed to Learn Interpretable Models from Data
finding: A harness that prompts a coding model for one interpretable rule at a time matches or beats state-of-the-art rule learners on tabular data, especially with small training sets, and beats standard harnesses.

title: SafeCoEvo: Co-Evolving Safety Harnesses and Guards for LLM Agents at Test-Time
finding: Test-time co-evolution of a safety harness and guard model cuts unsafe outcomes by 10.05% and raises task success by 12.15% over the strongest baseline.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Agent Distillation across Models, Artifacts, and Harnesses
finding: Survey formalizes agent distillation across models, artifacts and harnesses, classifies transfer by where knowledge persists, and reviews evaluation protocols for retention and utility.

title: Harnessing Large Language Models to Compile Task-Relevant Context into Bayesian Optimisation
finding: A Bayesian-optimisation harness compiles task context into standard optimisation; general coding harnesses work in familiar domains but fall short on unfamiliar, context-rich ones.

title: GitHarness: Git Init Your Harness Working Memory for Perpetual User Requirements
finding: Git-style version history for requirement changes lets an agent branch from compatible past work; the abstract claims strong task performance, with no numbers given.

title: AI as a Compiler: Compiling Triton kernels without the Triton compiler
finding: Agent translates Triton kernels directly into PTX, reaching 0.83x to 3.34x autotuned Triton speed; the largest gains come from transforms that Triton's own lowering pipeline omits.

title: S4VY: Segment Anything in Feed-Forward 4D Visual Geometry
finding: Segmentation model for 4D scenes with an agentic grounding harness that searches frames and selects masks; reports state-of-the-art instance segmentation, with no figures in the abstract.

title: Harness Evolution as Learning: Approximation, Generalization, and Optimization Limits of Self-Improving Personal Agents
finding: Frames harness evolution as learning and attributes personal-agent limits to approximation, generalization and optimization errors; introduces a preference benchmark for personal agents.

title: VACE: Validation-Gated Alternating Co-Evolution of Agent Models and Harnesses
finding: Accepts harness revisions only when validation improves; 17 of 44 proposals were rejected, and the gated loop beats weight-only reinforcement learning by 6.43 points on OfficeQA.

title: Mixture of Self-Improving Branches For Agent Harness Optimization
finding: Branching harness search with a development-data router beats Meta-Harness by 34.8% on Olympiad math, 11.6% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and 3.8% on SWE-bench Lite, without test outcomes.

title: AgentBug-Smith: Automatically Reproducing Real-World Harness Bugs in Agentic Systems
finding: Reproduces real harness bugs automatically: 200 reproducible bugs in a live benchmark show limited repair by current software agents, and distilled skills raise repair rates by 6.32%.

title: Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution
finding: Video agent tests competing failure explanations on its training videos, then keeps harness revisions that improve accuracy; the evolved agent processes fewer frames.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Skill Optimization via Cross-Harness Adaptation
finding: Retrieval from a public skill corpus, adapted across harnesses, beats skill optimization without retrieval on four agent benchmarks with two models.

title: LongHarness Bench: Stress-Testing Language Model Harnesses for Long-Context Reasoning
finding: Long-context harness benchmark: the best model-harness pair reaches 68% macro-average accuracy, and one model shows markedly different efficiency under different harnesses.

title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
finding: Builder learns reusable meta-skills from a target's feedback to construct harnesses for unseen tasks, gaining 8.95 points over no-skill construction and 12.02 over direct delivery.

title: HARDE: Optimizing Agent Harnesses for Runtime Risk Detection and Execution Control
finding: Two-stage optimization of a runtime-defense harness improves safety while keeping utility, beating hand-built harnesses and naive optimization across three attack benchmarks.

title: MILO: Automated Harness Discovery via Orchestrated Multi-Agent Evolution
finding: Co-evolved harnesses lift Opus 4.8 by 12.0%, 28.3% and 10.3% over its initial harness on three benchmarks, beating eight harnesses and six search methods; the open-weight gpt-oss-120b also gains.

title: Multi-Task Self-Evolving Harnesses with the Agent as Its Own Optimizer
finding: Frozen model evolves its own 49-line seed harness, gaining about 5 points in distribution and matching Codex on five unseen benchmarks; continued evolution beats Codex and Claude Code on Claw-Eval.

title: VidHarness: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Cost-Efficient Long Video Understanding
finding: Monte Carlo tree search evolves cost-aware video harnesses; a frame-budget mixture sets new results on three benchmarks, beating the strongest hand-built video agent by up to 11.2 points.

title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Action Models
finding: RoboHarness gives a coding agent a visual-geometric control panel for robots; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next outperforms vision-language-action models on BEHAVIOR Challenge 2025 tasks.

title: LVMH: A Meta-Optimization Harness for Long-Video Agent Memory
finding: LVMH evolves long-video memory policies with multi-agent code search; the discovered policy reaches 65.7% average accuracy with GPT-5, 7.7 points above prior work, at about 32x lower token use.

title: Toward Quantum Software Automation: A Quantum-Aware Harness for LLM-Guided Evolution
finding: A quantum-aware harness steers evolutionary language-model search for quantum software: utilization up 4.2% to 9.5%, mitigation time cut at least 96.8%, for $6.9 model cost.

title: Composing Task-specific Agent Harnesses at Test Time with Reusable Primitives
finding: STITCH selects reusable harness primitives per task and compiles a task-specific harness at test time; success rises up to 12 points over fixed harnesses, at 2.7% composition overhead.

title: Approval Laundering: Systematizing Approval--Execution Binding Failures in AI Coding-Agent Harnesses
finding: Six approval laundering modes let a harness execute an action other than the approved one; an Approval Token eliminates Delegation and seeded Temporal laundering, not Scope or Argument laundering.

title: Schema: Discovering Unknown Environments via Agentic Program Induction
finding: Schema, a harness with a persistent program workspace, raises the ARC-AGI-3 score from 58.7% to 99.2% with the same base model and solves all public DiG-bench games.

title: Fyan: A Human--AI Harness with Semantic Auditing for Document-Level Formalization
finding: FYAN, a harness pairing people and a language model for Lean formalization, proves 86 of 143 theorems versus 69 for a general agent harness, same model throughout.

title: EngramBench: A Capability-Grounded Benchmark for Skill-Evolution Harnesses
finding: EngramBench tests skill-evolution harnesses without solution leakage; static skill banks cut coding time over 55% but cannot fix the final-implementation bottleneck of the base model.

title: Scale and Selection: What Makes Automatic Harness Evolution Work for Visual-Interface Robot Agents
finding: Harness revisions must be promoted only if they beat the incumbent on fixed cases; this champion-challenger rule lifts held-out LIBERO success from 51% to 67% over 30 rounds.

title: RankEvolve: A Reliable Multi-Agent Auto-Research Harness for Evolving Ranking Models
finding: Runtime-controlled composition of Claude Code and Codex lifts execution accuracy from 45.8% to 62.5% over the best single product, with a 10.4% silent critical-defect rate.

title: Thinking Outside the Box: Can Language Models Rely on External Guidance Selectively?
finding: Frontier models gain from reliable workflow guidance but stay vulnerable to misleading guidance; counterfactual fine-tuning and outcome reinforcement learning improve selective reliance in open models.

title: Capture the lifecycle: KV Cache management in ReAct Agents with KVTether
finding: KVTether uses lifecycle signals from agent harnesses to manage the serving cache of ReAct agents; it cuts latency up to 26.3% against LMCache and task cost 40.0% on average.

title: Better Deck or Different Judge? Evaluating Agentic Harness Gains in Corporate and Investment Banking
finding: Five judges score the banking harness 20.4 to 33.6 points above direct generation, but margins over direct Opus shrink to -4.7 to +0.8, and repeated grading shifts unchanged decks.

title: Mid-Harness: Scaling Actions Between Model and Harness for Terminal Agents
finding: Sampling and verifying candidate actions before execution lifts a 9B terminal agent's success from 50.00% to 68.03% with a stronger verifier, using 8 samples.

title: Learning from Research: Toward Lifelong Agent Harness Evolution
finding: ScholarEvolve evolves harnesses from published research strategies; it raises Qwen3.5-27B goal completion on AppWorld from 49.6% to 63.6%.

title: cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents
finding: Standard virtual machines and task sets make computer-use agent speed comparable across four benchmarks; environment latency and reasoning effort change speed and cost rankings.

title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?
finding: Under equal time budget and the same frontier backbone, elaborate open harnesses give no advantage over one session of a minimal coding agent; the backbone drives performance.

title: Cogentic: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Automated Proof Discovery
finding: Cogentic runs parallel provers under adversarial verification and a persistent verified ledger; with Gemini base models it produced novel results on open problems in learning, auctions and mechanism design.

title: Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization
finding: Turbo Harness adapts a globally optimized harness to each instance using a playbook from the original optimization run; it outperforms existing harness optimizers across seven benchmarks.

title: When Harnesses Lose the Signal: Causal Evaluation of Recovery in LLM Agents
finding: Recovery in agent harnesses can rescue or harm the same trajectory; a router that intervenes only when worthwhile raises Qwen3-14B ALFWorld success from 70.33% to 73.33%.

title: LabBook: Harnessing Experimental History for Efficient LLM-Driven Discovery
finding: LabBook is an agent-maintained memory that retrieves from the full experimental history; on 49 Frontier-CS problems it improves the quality-cost trade-off over evolutionary baselines.

title: From Monolithic Prompts to Scaffolded Execution for Memory Agents with Small Language Models
finding: No abstract; from the title only, scaffolded execution for memory agents on small language models is proposed in place of monolithic prompts.

title: FORALL-LEAN-AGENT for Auditable Reasoning in Formal Mathematics and Software Verification
finding: Adding isolated workspaces, Lean tools and fresh review lifts GPT-5.6 Sol's VeriSoftBench success from 93 to 100 on 100 tasks while cutting cost from $69 to $62.

title: Cross-Benchmark Transfer from RL on Agentic Coding Tasks
finding: Reinforcement learning on 1,700 expert-built coding tasks lifts Kimi K2.7 Code on six external benchmarks across three harnesses, e.g. SWE-Bench Pro from 60.1 to 64.8.

title: ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization
finding: ActiveSaddler chooses harness-optimization training scenarios with a bandit over failure patterns; it adds 4.4 and 7.5 success points over a fixed scenario order on GAIA2 and Terminal-Bench 2.0.

title: Finding the Right Fit: Model-Harness Interactions across Agent Tasks
finding: Model rankings reverse across harnesses: on Terminal-Bench 4, Claude leads GPT by 7.94 points in OpenHands but trails by 30.16 in PI; evaluate model, harness and task together.

title: GUI-HARVEST: Self-Improving GUI Agents through Evidence-Driven Harness Evolution
finding: A harness optimizer that diagnoses GUI failures from before-and-after screenshots and repeated runs raises OSWorld-Verified scores across six backbones; Qwen3-VL-32B gains 12.33 points.

title: Harness Annealing: Learning to Act with Less External Control
finding: Training with harness-supported trajectories lets 9B and 35B models use tools alone and approach full-harness scores on SWE-QA; the benefit varies with model scale.

title: A Design Theory for AI-Assisted Software Development Derived from Christopher Alexander's Theory of Form
finding: Misfit-Governed Development wraps a language model in deterministic misfit detectors, a fix loop and human-gated rules; rebuilding a four-aggregate system used about 1,300 generated tests and 28 gates.

title: VideoEvolve: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Video Temporal Grounding
finding: VideoEvolve evolves agent harnesses for video temporal grounding with branch-guided edits; instruction refinement is the consistent source of gains, and evolved code benefits vary.

title: Continuous Process-Level Evaluation for Evolving Enterprise AI Agent Skills
finding: Of 175 runs passing final numerical checks, 162 (92.6%) still showed another process deviation, so final-output tests miss process drift in evolving enterprise agent skills.

title: Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks
finding: Mingbird, a local harness, lifts small open models to 0.886 overall versus 0.631 for the next harness across 288 cells; replications move single-mechanism results by up to 0.069.

title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
finding: VISTA gives a general multimodal model lossless visual memory; it lifts Claude Opus 5 on ARC-AGI-3 efficiency from 40.68 to 100.00 and beats same-model minimal harnesses on three more benchmarks.

title: Fast Models, Slow Evidence: A Paired and Self-Audited Evaluation of System-1 Decision Models for LLM Agent Harnesses
finding: A hosted System-1 decision model beats an open-weight one on 9 of 11 harness decision points; the paper's own audit cuts its claimed 23.9% cost saving to 4.3%.

title: OpenRUA: Robot-Use Agents Are Zero-Shot Visuomotor Policies
finding: A minimal workspace harness gives Claude Code with Claude Opus 5 terminal access to ROS 2 and reaches 99.0% on CaP-Bench and 87.0% on LIBERO-PRO with no bespoke primitives.

title: Harnessing LLMs as Agents: What Does It Cost?
finding: A resource theory of language model agent harnesses proves communication, memory access and recomputation bounds, plus a checkpoint interval law, tested in controlled GPT-6 Astra experiments.

title: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses
finding: VERSE lets a harness optimizer test draft edits and replay failures before submission; its best validated harness reaches 42.3% on held-out SWE-rebench tasks versus 39.2% for the strongest baseline.

title: WebUIProof: Benchmarking WebUI Code Generators with UI-Agent Execution Harness
finding: WebUIProof checks interactive web interface code with executable browser tests run by a UI-agent harness; eight commercial models often fail interaction requirements even when pages render.

title: Harness-Aware Distillation for Small Language Model Agents
finding: Harness-Aware Distillation trains a small agent only on what the teacher adds beyond the harness; it beats on-policy distillation with the same fixed harness and loops less.

title: HASTE: Evolving Agent Harnesses Against Emerging Attacks Using Sparse Evidence
finding: HASTE evolves safety harnesses from sparse threat evidence; attack-case generation probes each update, consistently lowering attack success while keeping benign-task utility.

title: MOF-VERIFY: A Failure-Aware Agentic Harness for MOF Hypothesis Verification
finding: MOF-Verify, a failure-aware harness for materials hypothesis checking, beats direct inference and retrieval baselines on average across backbones, with gains concentrated in structural grounding.

title: EvoRiskBench: An Evolving Benchmark for Runtime Security Risks in Workspace Agents
finding: EvoRiskBench runs 450 adversarial tasks on nine model-harness pairs; attack success reaches 68.44% for Codex with DeepSeek-V4-Pro and varies more across models than across harnesses.

title: Dynamic Harness Search: Building Multi-Agent Systems Per-Query via Prediction
finding: SHIFT builds a per-query harness with a local architect model and tree search; mean accuracy about 80% over 9,193 tasks, 7.2 points above the best of 17 baselines.

title: SHarP: Saliency-based Pruning of Agent Harnesses
finding: Ablating each harness module and pruning the least salient ones shows most studied harnesses are redundant, keeping comparable performance and efficiency after much of their modules are removed.

title: Autonomous Active Directory Exploitation via Multi-Model Harness Orchestration: A Benchmark Study with NeuroSploit on GOAD
finding: Inside one harness, nine frontier models cover 96-100% of attack-chain techniques at 90-97% precision, while direct invocation covers 21-54% and produces 3.2x more false positives.

title: What Does a Harness Buy? Tokens, Mostly
finding: With the model held fixed, swapping among three production harnesses moves SWE-bench Verified scores little beyond rerun noise, yet cost per task differs by up to 3x.

title: Are We Measuring Scientific Intelligence? Rethinking the Evaluation of AI Scientists
finding: Benchmark scores credit correct answers that ignore changed evidence; Claude agents answer 83% of single-cell questions correctly with no data but only 41% evidence-grounded accuracy.

title: Complex Agents, Shallow Tests: Demystifying and Enhancing Test Adequacy of Agent Harness in the Wild
finding: Fewer than half of LLM-dependent harness lines and branches are covered by existing tests; HarnessTester finds 122 real harness bugs, 88 of them previously unknown, in widely used agent systems.

title: RobotUse: Allocating Computation, Context, and Decisions
finding: RobotUse, a robot agent harness with subagents and a persistent playbook, reaches 45% task success on RoboLab, 6.7 points above CaP-X.

title: Causal Improvement Graph for Agentic Harness Optimization
finding: Causal Improvement Graph records evidence, hypotheses, interventions and outcomes so proposers build on prior findings; it finds stronger harnesses than previous meta-harness baselines.

title: Harnessing LLMs with Direction-Scope Control for Combinatorial Solver Refinement
finding: DiSH controls revision direction and scope in combinatorial solver refinement; across nine benchmarks it reduces feasibility oscillation and roughly halves feedback tokens against prior methods.

title: MESH-Harness: Self-Improving Agent Harnesses via Bandit-Guided Compositional Evolution
finding: MESH-Harness recombines harness modules with bandit-guided search; it beats Meta-Harness by 2.00 to 7.01 points under matched budgets and cuts aggregate test-time cost by 44.2%.

title: AIProver: Agentic Auto-Formalization of Mathematical Research via Certificate-Driven Evolving Harness
finding: As a skill, the AIProver harness lifts Claude Code's semantic correctness on proof formalization from 41.9% to 79.8% and Codex's from 34.1% to 62.4%.

title: Harness-Search: Guiding Long-Horizon Search through Multi-Agent Coordination
finding: Harness-Search splits proposing, memory commits and stopping across three authorities; under the same backbone it raises recall by 4.60 to 27.92 points over the strongest harness baseline.

title: LifeLong Digital Twin: A Unified Modeling Paradigm and Agent Harness for Event-Driven Lifelong Health State Trajectories
finding: A health-state paradigm with an agent harness that adds multimodal evidence; model-averaged F1 rises 22.0% for disease identification in trajectory forecasting over the reference condition.

title: MedicalHarness: A Controlled Evaluation of LLMs and Agent Harnesses on Medical Tasks
finding: Five open-weight models under five harnesses, changing only the harness: harness and model interaction explain about a quarter of outcome variance; no harness is best everywhere.

title: Correct Code, Broken Contributions? SWE-CC: Benchmarking Repository Policy Compliance for Coding Agents
finding: SWE-CC checks 500 coding tasks against 823 machine-checkable repository policies; agents violate 43.1% of applicable policies despite functionally correct patches.

title: HERA: Harness-Environment Co-Evolution for Reliable Agentic Abstention
finding: HERA co-evolves a harness with mutated environments; the evolved harness raises abstention accuracy from 61.7% to 83.3% and transfers to 19 other models, letting smaller models match stronger ones.

title: Can Agent Harnesses and Inference Engines Hear Each Other? The HEAR Protocol for Agentic LLM Serving
finding: HEAR is a protocol letting an agent harness and an inference engine share workflow intent and runtime state; it reports a 1.61x batch speedup on SCBench.

title: Internalizing Agent Experience into Diffusion Model Weights via On-Policy Context Distillation
finding: D-OPCD distills an image agent's harness benefit into diffusion model weights, raising direct-generation score from 60.52 to 65.09 across four benchmarks without running the harness.

title: HarnessSecurity-Bench: Do Security Mechanisms Really Protect Coding Agent Harnesses?
finding: Across six coding harnesses, enabling auto-approve raises attack success from 29.2% to 95.6% while utility rises; read-only mode and network isolation cut attacks but cost substantial utility.

title: From Evidence to Action: How Tool-Using Agents Fail
finding: Across ten model-harness configurations, strong static action judgment coexists with weaker interactive execution; failures often start before execution, when agents act without established evidence.

title: ServeLearnBench: How Well Can Agents Self-Improve from Serving Experience?
finding: ServeLearnBench tests five learning harnesses across six models on 7,718 tasks; continual adaptation is costly and can degrade already-correct behavior, and weak exploration limits learning.

title: Harness Engineering for Software Engineering via Modular Executable Dev-Primitives
finding: HERMES pairs repository components with resident language models; it beats matched baseline harnesses by 12.4% on average, and Qwen3-8B stays within 4.5% of a GPT-5.6 Sol configuration.

title: ChartBmkAgent: Harness-Governed Multi-Agent Construction of Chart QA Benchmarks from Sparse Error-Taxonomy Specifications
finding: A harness-governed agent set builds Chart QA samples from error-taxonomy specifications; 86.4% of generated samples were judged to test their specified error category.

title: Learn2Play Bench: How Well Do LLM Agents Learn from Experience in Unfamiliar Environments?
finding: With the backbone fixed, changing the agent harness improves Learn2Play scores while reducing estimated inference cost; keeping full action and feedback records beats summarizing them into rules.

title: Lachesis: Lifetime-Aware KV Cache Placement for Agent Serving across HBM and High-Bandwidth Flash
finding: Lachesis places agent memory segments in fast memory or high-bandwidth flash by the lifetime the harness sets; in trace-driven simulation it extends flash lifetime 1.19-3.13x over fast-memory-first placement.

title: EMHO: EMbodied Agent Harness Optimization via Experience Traces
finding: EMHO revises an embodied agent's harness from execution trajectories while the model stays frozen; it consistently improves EmbodiedBench task success for Qwen 9B and 27B models.

title: Recursive Game Creator: An Agentic Product-Level Experience-Oriented Game Harness
finding: Recursive Game Creator's Designer, Builder, Player and Reviewer loop reaches 53.2% strict task success on GameASG-Bench, a 34.1% gain over the same-model baseline.

title: VeriFine: Scaling Verification for Self-Improvement in Embodied Reasoning
finding: VeriFine co-evolves a policy, its training curriculum and a judge, refining the judge with selective human guidance; tested on driving and robot navigation tasks.

title: An Empirical Study of Agent Skills' Downstream Utility
finding: Same skills help some model-harness configurations and hurt others on 36.78% of tasks; reranking candidates by support for required operations lifts first-choice pass rates by 4.35 to 5.80 points.

title: From Plausible Hierarchies to Useful Taxonomies: Evaluating Agentic Harnesses on Customer Feedback
finding: Six harness-generated customer taxonomies pass generic checks, yet at least 97.7% of leaf names restate an ancestor; trees rated equally correct differ by 27 points in cross-branch leakage.

title: Goldsmith: Gold-Loss-Guided Definition Optimization with an Agentic Annotation Harness
finding: Goldsmith turns a small expert gold set into an annotation definition through textual revisions, accepted only when a structured loss falls; it beats direct rewriting and three published prompt optimizers.

title: AgentTime: Can Agents Estimate and Control Their Own Runtime?
finding: AgentTime finds agents deviate from requested durations by 2.9x (Fable 5.1, Claude Code) versus 1.2x (GPT-6 Astra, Codex); 14 of 158 Astra runs slept after appearing to finish.

title: CoTrace: Data Recipes for Training Terminal Agents with Harness-Model Co-Evolution
finding: CoTrace trains terminal agents only on rollouts matched to the runtime harness; Qwen3.5-9B rises from 78 to 88 solved tasks under supervised fine-tuning, and 90 with online reinforcement.

title: EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution
finding: EmbodiedRSI, a self-evolving robot harness, reaches 77.0% overall success on RoboCasa365 against 40.1% for the best baseline, and transfers zero-shot to a real robot at 71.3%.

title: The Harness as the Only Mutable Surface: Compliance-Bounded Self-Evolution of LLM Agents in Credit Pipelines, with a Measured Admission Gate
finding: In simulation, a harness-only self-evolution gate admitted 144 of 7,449 candidate changes, none worsening held-out error; without it, 309 harmful changes passed.

title: NavGPT-3: Harnessing Context in a Hierarchical Navigation Runtime
finding: NavGPT-3's harness lifts R2R-CE success from 76.94% for its 8B action policy alone to 81.51%, and on RxR-CE matches human followers.

title: When Interfaces Speak: Data-Aware Generative UI Harness for Active Interaction
finding: GenUI-Harness trains a 4B backbone from 9.33% to 58.00% three-attempt pass rate on UI-TAU Bench, above Claude Opus 5 at 46.67%; generated interfaces cut dialogue rounds from 3.4 to 1.2.

title: DuplexAgent-RSI: Recursive Harness Improvement for Full-Duplex Voice Agent Collaboration
finding: A simulator generates timed test conversations to find failing harness modules, and a closed repair loop revises them; it outperforms the initial harness and repeated editing without diagnosis.

title: Safe, Persistent, and Evolving Agent Harness for Understanding Partially Observable Worlds
finding: E-Ledger with WorldAbduct checks actions against policy and evolves hidden-rule ledgers; across four backbones it beats the strongest evolution baseline by 5 to 15 points.

title: Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling: When Weight Training Should Begin
finding: Harness evolution fixes process failures and weight training fixes content failures; on DeepPlanning a harness loop lifts Qwen3.5-4B from 0.16 to 0.30 and 9B from 0.32 to 0.44.

title: EvoAlloc: A Self-Evolving Resource Allocation Agent for Efficient Program Evolution
finding: EvoAlloc revises which candidate programs get costly evaluation; across coding and harness-optimization benchmarks it needs 59-82% fewer full evaluations to reach baseline performance.

title: SuperNav: An Agentic Navigation System for Any Task in Any Scene
finding: SuperNav gives a pretrained multimodal model a navigation harness with skills and tools, without fine-tuning it; it outperforms four baselines on instance, multi-object and demand-driven tasks.

title: A Closer Look at Agentic BBO: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Black-Box Optimization
finding: Agentic black-box optimization beats direct language model methods in all five domains and the best numerical optimizers in four; under a Codex harness, GPT-6 Astra and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash lead cost-performance.

title: HarnessSQL: Harness-Native Training for SQL Agents in Realistic Database Environments
finding: HarnessSQL trains SQL agents inside their execution harness; it raises Qwen3-8B execution accuracy on Spider 2.0-SQLite from 15.5% to 45.2% and Qwen3-14B from 22.2% to 54.8%.

title: Embodied Turing Machines: Stateful Code for Robot Recursive Self-Improvement
finding: Code-Only-as-Policy tracks robot and task state in code with no model in the loop; its library reaches 70.24% success on 42 RoboDojo bimanual tasks, offered as a new paradigm.

title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
finding: In SWE-Duel, coding agents write and repair each other's bugs at evaluation time; newest-version tasks defeat a fixed solver 42.9% of the time, older versions 4.0%.

title: Recurrent Harness for Agentic Continual Learning
finding: ReHarness revises retrieved reflections after each instance from the trajectory; it outperforms raw-context, memory and prompt-optimization baselines across three benchmarks and three backbones.

title: EmbodiedCLBench: Evaluating Continual Learning for Self-Evolving Embodied Agents
finding: EmbodiedCLBench tests whether embodied agents recombine basic-task experience on advanced tasks; experience helps consistently, but gains do not scale with more learning samples.

title: Don't Guess, Just Ask: Evaluating Interactive Requirement Clarification for Repository-Level Software Development
finding: ReqClarifyBench tests interactive requirement clarification on 341 repository-level tasks; coding-agent harnesses do not improve requirement document quality over their base language models.

title: Evo$^2$: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution
finding: Evo² co-evolves weights and harness with one proposer-reflector policy; it reaches 82.1% on Polyglot and lifts a GPT-5-mini agent from 24.4% to 48.3%.

title: LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management
finding: LongHarness keeps acquired evidence and conclusions explicit; on OfficeQA Pro V1 it lifts GLM-5.3-Flash exact match from 15.8% to 60.2% over direct reasoning on the same backbone.

title: The Silent Failures in Agentic Data Science
finding: Most agentic data science solutions across 220 tasks contain at least one methodological failure, such as data leakage, despite harness complexity or model capacity; leakage tracks higher accuracy.

title: ClawLoop: Self-Improving Agents via Harness-Native Training Loop
finding: Self-improving training loop for harness-based agents needs no external teacher; the Qwen3.6-27B loop's gains transfer to 4B and 9B models on all benchmarks.

title: Cortex: Measurement-Gated Evolution and Pruning of Coding-Agent Skills and Rules
finding: Cortex keeps a harness change only after repeated runs show gains; rules did most of the work with Haiku 4.5, but under Sonnet 5 a single run's harness added little.

title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
finding: Recursive harness editing without ground-truth verifiers lifts GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash by up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, with more gain as the edit budget grows.

title: Compaction-Aware Reinforcement Learning For Ascend Triton Kernel Generation
finding: A compaction-aware segment-level reinforcement learning method with a lightweight harness beats a group-relative baseline on Ascend kernel generation in correctness and speedup.

title: Reels-RSI: Program-Level Self-Improvement for Code-Rendered Explainer Videos
finding: Learned rules caught four defects in later frames; rules guard a weaker director (thirty violations unguarded versus five) while lessons do not move the judge.

title: EvoCowork: A Benchmark for Real-World Office Tasks
finding: A 240-task office benchmark shows harness gains on feedback file types do not transfer to cross-office workflows: +0.03 and -1.72 points for two evolution methods.

title: EnactOpt: Diagnosis-Guided Harness Evolution for Embodied Agents
finding: Evolving skills and context code from limited execution feedback raises embodied task success by about 10-27 points over initial harnesses.

title: TurnCost: Turns, Not Observations: Cache-Aware Loop Engineering for Coding Agents
finding: Turn count explains 84% of trajectory cost variance versus 4% for observation size; 98.6% of input tokens hit the prefix cache, so flat pricing overstates cost about 7x.

title: Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses
finding: Multi-objective, decomposition-based harness evolution beats single-objective monolithic baselines by more than 10% on SecRepoBench and BaxBench.

title: PANINI-DR: Controlled Deep Research through Generative Semantic Workspaces
finding: A verified shared-workspace deep-research harness reaches 73.3% on BrowseComp-Plus, 16.0 points above the next of seven harnesses on the same backbone.

title: HarnessNet: Feedback-driven Hierarchical Joint Harness Evolution for Multi-agent Systems
finding: Hierarchical harness evolution for multi-agent systems matches a single global optimizer's gains on AgentBench while using fewer tokens per optimizer call.

title: Evolving to Match Capabilities: Improving Harness Self-Evolution via Skill Adaptation
finding: Skills raise GPT-5.6-luna by 31.1 points on 103 task-skill pairs but cut Gemma-4-E4B by 8.8; adapting skills to the executor adds 2.0-5.1 points.

title: VideoEvoHarness: Self Evolving Agent Harness from Unlabeled Videos for Video Understanding
