finding: Harness evolution from unlabeled videos raises video-understanding accuracy over the initial harness, with gains transferring across backbones and rising each round.

title: MedHarnessBench: A Unified Benchmark for Healthcare Agent Evaluation
finding: A 342-task healthcare benchmark separates runtime harness failures from model failures; single-fault perturbations verify that its seven-dimension evaluation discriminates.

title: Visible but Not Avoided: State-Dependent Re-Proposal of Rejected Candidates in Catalog-Based LLM Optimization Loops
finding: Static probes underpredict re-proposal of rejected edits in real loops by 0.32; stating rejection in one sentence lowers re-proposal in every model by 0.16.

title: Computational Reflective Equilibrium for Agentic AI: A Rawlsian Alignment Scaffold for Governance
finding: A reflective-equilibrium scaffold in the agent harness links principles, evidence and actions, with proofs of stability and a quarantine theorem against prompt injection.

title: When Agent Evaluation Becomes Unreliable: An Empirical Study of Oracle Failures and Configuration-Dependent Measurement in an LLM Agent Benchmark
finding: An evaluation reward function left the database unrestored; corrected success falls from 94.3% to 65.5% and changes which agent ranks strongest.

title: Unravel: Recovering an Interactive 3D Scene from a Single Image
finding: A training-free agentic pipeline peels a single image layer by layer and rebuilds a physically plausible interactive three-dimensional scene.

title: CineRecon: Benchmarking Frontier Models for Agentic Cinematic Reconstruction
finding: Twelve model-harness agents reconstruct dynamic three-dimensional scenes from 360 clips and fail all three consistency dimensions, with subject motion hard even in the Proxy setting.

title: LATCH: LLM-Assisted Timing Closure Harness for Post-Route FPGA Optimisation
finding: Expert recipes pass 98.2% of attempts versus 17.9% for LLM-built procedures; branching search raises mean maximum-frequency gain from 10.5% to 16.0%.

title: Trace-to-Architecture: Capability Bottleneck Diagnosis for Harness Revision
finding: Diagnosing failures from trajectories and validating edits beats the strongest baselines by 6.2 to 30.3 points on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and AppWorld.

title: SpecGuardBench: Can Coding Agents Construct Reliable Validation Harnesses from Natural Language Specifications?
finding: Coding agents write checks that mirror the reference implementation instead of the specification; no agent's validation harness is faithful on more than 63% of 291 tasks.

title: Learning to Design SR Solvers: Harness Optimization for Symbolic Regression
finding: Jointly optimizing role prompts and workflows gives symbolic regression agents 61.33% in-distribution accuracy, a 45.0% relative gain over the next-best baseline.

title: Verifier-Harness Co-Evolution for Training-Free Self-Improvement on Open-Ended Tasks
finding: A learned verifier with harness state is preferred over direct generation 59.00% of the time on Qwen3-8B and 57.19% on Qwen3.8-27B; the margin shrinks from 9.00 to 7.19 points.

title: Code2Worlds-2: Physically Plausible Agent Harness for Embodied World Simulation
finding: A compile, simulate, critique and refine loop turns generated four-dimensional scenes into MuJoCo-compatible, physically plausible scenes using a simulator critic.

title: Coupled Harness--Model Evolution for Scientific Equation Discovery
finding: Without any tool library a three-billion-active-parameter model solves almost nothing; tools supply most gain, and the full system reaches 79.1% on LSR-Synth at tolerance 10^-2.

title: ResearchFlow-Eval: Tracing the Execution Gap in End-to-End Multi-Claim Autoresearch
finding: Across harness types, experimental execution lags design and planning in every system; neither skill augmentation nor specialized orchestration reliably raises scores.

title: AM-Bench: Understanding Agents under Task Underspecification across Models and Harnesses
finding: Across five models and four harnesses over 20,160 runs, rankings depend on model-harness pairing; missing goals lower success more than ambiguity, and repeat consistency is a criterion.

title: Jev-Guard: Fast Routing and Auditing Agent Actions over Editable Policy Trees
finding: A guard model routes agent actions over a policy tree at 58ms mean latency with 93.72% safety accuracy; in the Hermes harness it cut review time from 4.80 to 1.33 seconds.

title: Let the Mind Conceive, Let the Hand Achieve: Following Multimodal Instructions for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
finding: A harness separating planning from action generation reaches 68.22% mean success over nine RMBench tasks, 26.22 points above Mem-0.

title: The Last Mile of Coding Agents for Long-Document Tasks: An Empirical Study on Clinical Trial Protocol Digitization
finding: Across nine models in five coding-agent harnesses agents find the evidence but fail to transcribe it; a domain harness lifts a local open-weight model 6.2 to 59.4 points.

title: Knowledge Graphs as Files: An Agent Harness Where Tool Creation and Tool Use Co-Evolve
finding: Agents writing code over raw graph files exceed the strongest published baseline by at least 6.7 Hit@1 points on every graph, with no training.

title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
finding: Formal analysis of harness self-evolution gives a generalization bound and a high-probability admission rule using fresh, independent validation data; no experiments.

title: HERO: Harnessing Evidence for Test-time Refinement and Prompt Optimization in Program Generation
finding: Learning prompt updates from execution-verified successes and failures lifts first-attempt pass rate by 7.6 points on text-to-code tasks; test-time refinement adds 2.0 more.

title: Why Do Agent Teams Fail Across Boundaries? A Failure Taxonomy for Agent-to-Agent Systems with Private States
finding: Across more than 2,500 runs of agent-to-agent systems, a 20-mode failure taxonomy shows no agent verifies a peer's claim unprompted; aggregate scores hide these failures.

title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness
finding: Restricting the proposer to content-free feedback cuts the validation-test gap by 37.9% and raises held-out score 6.2% over the prior recursive harness, across four video benchmarks.

title: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Before Post-Training: An End-to-End Approach
finding: Adapting existing agent scaffolds to base models, without chat conversion, gives end-to-end agentic evaluation that tracks behavior across pretraining checkpoints.

title: L3M: A Verifiable Harness and Runtime for Self-Extending and Self-Improving Agents
finding: A runtime written in Lean 4 with kernel-checked safety properties; untuned, it reaches about two thirds of the unsafe shell pass rate on Terminal-Bench using only safe tools.

title: BluePixel: Toward Native 4K Agentic Image Editing
finding: A native 4K image-editing model paired with a verifying agent harness ranks second of seven models on VINS-4KEval++ and edits a 4K image in 8.7 seconds.

title: A Strong Harness Narrows the Model Gap: A Comparative Evaluation for Legislative Document-to-XML Conversion
finding: A full multi-agent harness lifts the weakest of three Claude models to 0.948 on legislative XML conversion, above the strongest model alone at 0.806.

title: SWE-Nexus: Automated Composition of Software Engineering Tasks from Test Execution
finding: Automatic task construction from test execution yields 600 repository tasks; the best of 12 models under three agent scaffolds resolves 37.8% in one attempt.

title: Harness Policy Distillation: Aligning Agent Policies with Runtime Semantics
finding: Training on runtime control semantics lifts Qwen3-8B autonomous task success from 3.09% to 22.98% on TRAJECT-Bench with the Pi harness.

title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
finding: Nineteen frontier models build agent harnesses scored deterministically on 328 test cases; GPT-6 Astra reaches 53.05% while the weakest model reaches 27.44%.

title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
finding: Survey of agentic robots organizing seventeen research categories across Model, Data, Environment and Harness, with open challenges; no quantitative result.

title: HPCAgent-Bench: A Framework for Sound Benchmarking of Code-Optimizing Agents, Harnesses, and Skills
finding: Across 40 matched setups, interventions significantly change speedup only twice but token cost by up to 3.0 times; agents reach up to 4.2 times speedup over automatic parallelizers.

title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
finding: Out-of-the-box agents average 54%, 36% and 19% on three workflows with large run-to-run variation; the knowledge-plus-deterministic framework yields runnable workflows with no observed variation.

title: ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets
finding: Across 21 model-harness configurations, the visible tool menu is the only pressure with a large penalty, tracking truncation; raising the cap sixteenfold removes most of it.

title: TRACER: A Multimodal Harness for Patient Care in Hospitals
finding: A training-free multimodal harness reaches 61.0% question accuracy versus 49.3% for the strongest baseline on the same backbone, and 84.8% on action detection.

title: What Survives Self-Evolution: Provenance Marks in Copied Agent Harnesses
finding: Published provenance marks fail under covert rewriting: a key survives in 0 of 12 copies for one scheme and 5 of 12 for another; a new key is detected in 62 of 76 copies.

title: DeciCAD: Harness-Grounded Learning of Action Policies for CAD Agents
finding: A domain-native harness cuts model output tokens by 45-88% against a general coding harness and lifts F1 from 0.6883 to 0.7437 under matched supervision.

title: CoWorld Reasoner: Agentic Multimodal Reasoning with the Evolving Video World Model-Driven Harness
finding: A video-world-model harness with co-evolved tools and skills beats direct reasoning with the same vision-language model on all seven benchmarks.

title: Priming Base Models for Agentic Post-Training: An Open Midtraining Recipe
finding: Midtraining on long-context software data raises SWE-bench Verified from 60.7 to 64.5 on Nemotron 3.5 Lightning; harness design is not studied.

title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
finding: A post-trained 35B mixture-of-experts agent raises MLE-Bench Lite medal rate from 37.9% to 72.7%, comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3.

title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
finding: Of gains in 21 significant harness-evolution settings, overfitting and test-time scaling explain 54% and 14% on average; search-set gains often fail to transfer.

title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
finding: Report finds a frontier model crosses the threshold of embodied competence but not practical intelligence; coupling its reasoner to a low-level controller is costly but effective.

title: Model-as-a-Trojan: Self-Activating Covert DNS Exfiltration Baked Into the Weights of an LLM Agent
finding: A fine-tuned open-weight model carries covert DNS exfiltration in its weights, firing in 20 of 20 adversarial suppression trials; prompting is an unreliable off-switch.

title: Harness-Driven Agentic Operation of Optical Pooled Screen Analysis
finding: A Claude Code plugin harness runs the Brieflow optical pooled screen pipeline; in five screens it yielded more confidently assigned cells than the original hand analyses.

title: Agentic Interpretation: Harness-Governed Evidence Construction for Software Agents
finding: A deterministic harness admits typed evidence records; for GLM-5, reject-class F1 rises from 0.256 to 0.543 on SWE-bench-Live, using 35% fewer executions.

title: Federation over Harness
finding: Server agent evolves client and aggregation harnesses from self-generated reflections without labels; it beats fixed-harness agents by 53.57% and self-evolving harnesses by 29.76%.

title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
finding: Alternating harness and policy optimization lifts Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's resolve rate from 57.8% to 64.8%; a stronger external proposer adds a further boost.

title: Benchmarking and Enhancing Agentic Causal Discovery
finding: On anonymous simulated datasets, GPT-6.1 Sol beats the best chosen algorithm on all six families, gaining 14% adjacency F1 on the hardest; Claude Opus 5.5 gains 7.4%.

title: From Approval to Abuse: Privilege Escalation Attacks on Harness-Protected Coding Agents
finding: Planted repository context steers Claude Code and Codex CLI into requesting broad allow-rules in 58% of instances; approved rules then complete silent malicious goals in 81.0% of eligible cases.

title: Towards Agentic Proof Harness Engineering
finding: A coding agent builds formal proof harnesses for curl and libuv that let CBMC detect all three embedded assertion violations; a feasibility case study.

title: HexaShell: A Universal Harness for Robot Coding Agents in Simulation and the Real World
finding: A thin task-agnostic harness with 14 tools reaches 69.9% to 82.2% success on four simulated benchmarks with no task input; 76 of 90 real-robot episodes succeed.

title: ABF-Bench: A Verifiable Benchmark for Agentic Blockchain Forensics
finding: A verifiable blockchain-forensics benchmark where the ABF harness reaches 75% edge recall, against 47% for Codex with the same model and 10% for Claude Code.

title: Enforcing Code Reasoning in Agentic Scaffold for More Effective Issue Resolution
finding: A scaffold that guides code reasoning raises issue-resolution rates 6.29% to 10.53% over mini-SWE-Agent and Claude Code on 731 SWE-bench-Pro instances; repeated runs show robustness.

title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
finding: Evolving skills lifts Qwen affinity-comparison accuracy from 62.2% to 81.1% on skill-development tasks; a prospective study yields a compound with 2.64-fold better potency.

title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
finding: Eleven frontier models with coding-agent harnesses match no expert reference on Deployment-Adjusted Quality; the strongest Claude Code configuration scores 0.87 against 1.

title: IRAH: Hierarchical Agentic Tree Search for Retrieval Pipeline Optimization
finding: A hierarchical tree search over retrieval pipelines beats a tree-structured Parzen estimator baseline on two of three in-distribution benchmarks, gaining up to 6.4%.

title: Good Judgment, Bad Advice: Decision-Model Controllers Raise Agent Cost Without Improving Success
finding: A decision-model controller raised cost per attempt 19% over no controller at an identical 73.0% pass rate, and no controller ever chose to abandon a run.

title: ReTRACE: Feedback-Guided LLM Agent in a Chemistry Harness for Retrosynthesis Planning
finding: A chemistry harness around Claude Opus 4.8 gets at least one of its top 10 routes past audit for 87.4%, 95.0% and 86.7% of targets on three benchmarks.

title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
finding: A 9-billion-parameter open model trained with co-evolved harness and checkpoints beats DeepSeek-V4-Pro by 14.16 points on TraceElephant and GLM-5.3 by 4.90 on HomeBench VM.

title: TOMORI: A Tool-Orchestrated Mixing Operator for REAPER Interaction
finding: A code-based mixing harness for REAPER improves explicit-instruction execution over a single submission in paired ablations; abstract requests reduce project agreement.

title: Design and Cross-Domain Evaluation of an Agent Execution Harness
finding: On a 53-task paired comparison the harness scores 19.89 points above direct completion despite a median task change of -1.46 points; mean cost rises from $0.29 to $2.13 per task.

title: CUA-Lite: An Open Platform for Computer Use Agents
finding: An open platform integrates 12 computer-use benchmarks with 30,000 verifiable tasks and one shared model harness; reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning improve open-weight models.

title: Reliable Before Profitable: QuantHarness for Governing Financial Strategy Development with LLM Agents
finding: A two-layer finance harness reaches 90.72% task success against 74.23% to 84.54% for comparison systems, and contains targeted violations in controlled stress tests.

title: VibeTraining-Bench: Data-Trainer-Harness Co-Design for Iterative System Improvement
finding: Research agents co-design data, trainer and harness, raising a target agent's SWE-bench Verified score from 32.9% to 53.7%, near a human-developed model's 55.4%.

title: When the harness decides success: state that cannot be re-observed
finding: Truncation costs nothing when a lost fact can be looked up again, but drops success to chance when not; the gap is 92.5 points (90% interval 89.5 to 95.5).

title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
finding: Label-free harness evolution gives a heavy mode 2.0 points more pass rate and 26.1% lower per-task cost than RHO on GPT-5.5 with Codex; GLM-5.2 with Claude Code shows the same advantage.

title: ProteinGeoBench: Frontier Structural-Biology Agents Are Fluent at Lookup but Lost in Geometry
finding: Swapping in each model's own command-line agent changes scores by -0.071 to +0.086; with one run per task, 23.9% of bootstrap replicates rank a different model first.

title: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
finding: Through a section index, GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2 lose 11.3 and 7.9 accuracy points while Claude models show no detectable cost; naming the authoritative output recovers 6.3 to 7.9 points.

title: A general-purpose System One decision model for clinical records
finding: A 4-billion-parameter clinical decision model beats open models up to 27 billion on 13 of 14 tasks and, with an agent, uses 690-fold fewer language-model tokens than reading every record.

title: Understanding the Benefits of Scaffolds through Computational Separations
finding: Inference-time harnesses beat a distilled student even with small models; a proof shows fixed-depth forward passes cannot represent the harness's closure, so enlarging the model is needed.

title: Refuses When Asked, Complies When Acting: A Runtime Safety Check for Robot Control Loops
finding: A robot arm running a default harness refused 0% of 15 hazardous instructions and completed 27%; a runtime check would have stopped all 15 and flagged none of 15 harmless controls.

title: VerifierBench: Benchmarking the Generation of Executable Verifiers for LLM Agents
finding: Across 19 models in a common agent harness, generated verifiers reject invalid solutions more reliably than they accept valid ones; normalized balanced accuracy ranges from 10.6 to 62.1.

title: Cassette-Editor: An Agent Harness for Editing Video the Way You Do
finding: A video-editing harness with checked patches passes 89% of 31 requests against 47% for the same model with basic editing operations, at under half the agent time and cost per success.

title: Building a Self-Improving Agentic Harness for RSE Projects
finding: No abstract is available; per the title, the paper builds a self-improving agentic harness for research software engineering projects.

title: KPHarness: Co-Evolving Knowledge and Probing for Long-Horizon Gaming Harnesses
finding: Co-evolving recovery knowledge with active probing improves Minecraft task coverage over bare policy execution, a fixed harness, and knowledge-only harness evolution.

title: Harness Self-Evolution for Long-Horizon Terminal Agents
finding: Harness self-evolution targets tasks that both succeed and fail under one configuration, aiming to make model capabilities more reliable across runs; the abstract gives no number.

title: Act on Your Behalf, Beyond Your Authorization: Benchmarking LLM Agent Authorization Alignment
finding: Agents act outside authorization in 19.2% of 6,864 trajectories across four models and three harnesses; agents that consult the principal first show 14.0% against 21.6%.

title: Elicitation or Expansion? Demystifying Gains from Agent Harness Optimization
finding: Harness gains can reverse at larger attempt budgets when stronger interventions are compared; aggregate pass-at-one gains conceal shortfalls on hard tasks, so diagnosis must be per difficulty.

title: ClawMMU: Protection-Coherent Virtual Memory for Stateful LLM Agents
finding: A protection layer labels memory by owner, scope, origin and authority, so instructions injected from fetched pages are stopped as protection faults even when the model is fooled.

title: MaD-RSI: Model-as-Data for Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
finding: Treating models as data, a shared harness trained on failure trajectories from several heterogeneous language models generalizes better than single-model harness optimization at lower cost.

title: ChartEvo: Self-Evolving Agent Harnesses for Long-Tail Chart Reasoning
finding: Co-evolved chart skills and executable tools raise Qwen3.7-Plus accuracy by 45.6% on ChartBench long-tail charts and 32.5% on ChartX.

title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
finding: Adding a perception toolkit to a coding agent lifts Qwen3.8-27B by 13.9 and 20.5 points and Gemini-3.8-Flash by 11.2 and 9.6; tool gains shrink as models get stronger.

title: Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design
finding: Evolving a hierarchy of specialized harness classes through inheritance, with a router, improves results up to 15 percent over the base harness on three long-horizon benchmarks.

title: An Explicit Feedback Contract for Iterative ML-Agent Harnesses
finding: An explicit feedback contract releases validation scores only past a noise threshold; on a zero-gain control, exact feedback reported a 0.0157 gain, versus 0.0033 under the contract.

title: How Much Does the Harness Matter, and for Whom? A Multi-Model Study of Context in LLM-Driven Vulnerability Discovery
finding: An engineered prompt with call-graph context raises vulnerability yield 20-86 percent for smaller models but only 2 percent for the frontier model; cheaper models match it at far lower cost.

title: Forging More Tasks into Better Harnesses: Agentic Harness Evolution via Successive Scale Racing
finding: Searching evidence combinations per round lifts pass rate from 64.3 to 68.3 percent as the task pool grows 40 to 200, while baselines fall; racing cuts validation runs 60 percent.

title: Where AI Vulnerability Discovery Harnesses Go Quiet: Structural False Negatives and Hidden Vulnerabilities
finding: Harnesses drop reachable vulnerabilities at 13 mapped points before or after the model runs; six of the harnesses examined dropped one file before the model saw it, five silently.

title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
finding: Reinforcement learning on a factorized space of harness variations improves generalization to unseen harness combinations and transfers to unseen external black-box harnesses.

title: From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation
finding: A vision-language planner that edits its harness from execution feedback reaches 51.38 percent success on RoboMME, against 44.38 percent without self-evolution.

title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents
finding: A model that writes its own PubMed queries triples gold-paper recall and reaches 62 percent accuracy; with gold abstracts accuracy is 79-86 percent, so retrieval is the bottleneck.

title: PAUSE: Search-Free Steering of Coding Agents Before Their First Source-Code Edit
finding: One planning intervention before a coding agent's first source-code edit lifts resolution 16.8 percent on SWE-bench Verified in OpenHands and 14.7 percent on Multilingual in SWE-agent.

title: HGM-Dual: Lineage-Aware Guided Agent Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Planning
finding: Lineage-aware context and error-conditioned child generation beat the strongest baseline by up to 14.45 percent relative case accuracy, matching prior variants with 2 to 4 times less evaluation budget.

title: The End of Consensus Research?
finding: An agent harness with a protocol knowledge base, code skeleton and Lean proofs found a consensus protocol cutting mean latency 12.2 percent on write-heavy and 33.3 percent on read-heavy workloads.

title: SWE-VERIFIER: Selective Verification for Cost-Efficient Coding Agents
finding: A selective verifier built from Qwen3.5-4B raises resolution from 75.47 to 77.20 percent at 1.09 times cost, checking fewer than 4 percent of steps.

title: Can LLMs Improve Their Own Harness? A Controlled Study on ARC-AGI-3
finding: Two self-revisions raise held-out performance by only 2.80 points (interval -1.44 to 7.35); development gains overstate held-out gains across 27 lineages.

title: PLE: Physical-Engineering's Last Exam
finding: An 85-task physical-engineering benchmark run under seven agent harnesses: the strongest configuration scores a mean 50.6 percent, using 27 million tokens and 63 minutes per task.

title: Harnessing Language Models as Optimization Modeling Agents
finding: Execution-guided revision beats direct generation for all 11 Qwen models from 0.6B to 27B, by up to 49.46 percentage points, with no additional training.

title: REGATTA: A Cross-Domain Measurement Framework and Fault-Injection Harness for Enterprise AI Agents
finding: A measurement framework for enterprise agent test suites: a source audit found 24 checklist items misstating the rule in force, and stage agreement 0.536 falls below pooled chance 0.549.

title: Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports
finding: A benchmark of 50 video-centred research tasks with 6,414 binary criteria; the best of 18 agent configurations scores 63.3 out of 100, short on coverage and citations.

title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
finding: A hierarchical vision-language-action agent with a capability-aware harness scores 85.0 percent on MineStudio Bench and 37.4 percent average success on OpenHA.

title: Certified Execution Harness for Agentic AI: Safe and Least-Intrusive Petri-Net Supervisory Control Between Reasoning and Action
finding: A Petri-net supervisor between model and tools refuses injected requests whose preconditions are unmet; the least-intrusive safe supervisor is a value-threshold refinement of the conventional one.

title: Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly
finding: Compaction barely moves two 1M-context models; yet the first summary drops a third of ProgramBench anticheating rules, and work instructions drop about 6 times more than build specifications.

title: Phronix: The Capability-Centric Learning Paradigm for Agents
finding: Learned capabilities solve recurring tasks first try in 93-95 percent of cases; they lift two cheaper models from 29 and 27 to 91 and 87 percent on SWE-bench.

title: Ulysses: A Security Harness For Synthesizing Verifiable Web Exploits
finding: A multi-agent security harness produces verified exploit proofs for 10 of 25 real-world web advisories and found 4 new proofs of exploitability never reported before.

title: Reproducible Evaluation as the Substrate for Safe Prompt Compression in Production Agents
finding: An offline evaluation harness stays reproducible on live enterprise data; correctness-gated prompt compression trims the prompt surface 3.5-7.6 percent without losing held-out correctness.

title: VibeGame: Prompt-to-Game Development with AI-Native Engine and Self-Evolving Adversarial Agent Team
finding: A game-building harness with eight adversarial agents and a structured engine outperforms other harnesses on the same underlying model, including GPT-6.1-Sol, on a GameCraft-Bench subset.

title: Do AI-for-Science Agents Preserve Model Safety?
finding: Five agent harnesses on 50 harmful chemistry requests raise harmful compliance even under direct prompting, and adaptive attacks that fail on the base model succeed once a harness is added.

title: Pairing Matters: Performance, Failures, and Efficiency in Lightweight Coding Agents
finding: For the same model, resolution differs by up to 44 percentage points across six open-source harnesses, and harness rankings change across models; tokens per resolved task vary over 20-fold.

title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
finding: A benchmark scoring agent harnesses on seven reliability components across 3,420 runs: harness scores range from 59.8 to 72.0 percent, and 31.1 percent of runs succeed despite a failed criterion.

title: 4DMemory: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Spatiotemporal Memory with Harness-Augmented Agents
finding: A 4DMemory harness improves all 13 tested models by over 50 percent on long-horizon video memory; the new benchmark scores them over 10 percent lower than the previous one.

title: DealsFlow: An Evidence-Gated Agentic Harness for Venture Capital Deal Triage
finding: An evidence-gated harness scores startup investments with Spearman 0.45 against 0.38 for an unconstrained language model, yet 70 percent of its reports needed a correction.

title: When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?
finding: Harness rankings change across models and benchmarks, and similar task scores hide different completion profiles; 111 settings across 52,168 trajectories show the pairing matters.

title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
finding: Reusing resolved tool decisions keeps Codex at 90.82 percent on HumanEval while cutting tokens per task 29.54 percent; a DeepSeek harness rises from 71.43 to 85.71 percent.

title: AOS-Bench: Can LLM Agents Manage Dynamic Workloads?
finding: A benchmark runs tasks arriving over time under shared processor and memory limits; isolated success does not carry over, as heavy workloads cost every system 13 to 23 points.

title: AdaPRA: Process Reward Agents with Adaptive Rubrics for Data Science
finding: A persistent coding harness with adaptive rubric supervision lifts an 80B Qwen model's leaderboard percentile by 24.5 points on DSPredict-Easy and 14.8 points on DSPredict-Hard.

title: Agentic Harness Architecture: 2026 White Paper
finding: No abstract was supplied; the title names a 2026 white paper on agentic harness architecture, so its claims cannot be confirmed from this line.

title: Build or Adopt? Custom-Built vs. General-Purpose LLM Agent Harnesses for Automotive GUI Testing
finding: General-purpose harnesses match a custom harness on test success but vary more across runs; inference costs 2.6-10.7 times more, yet total monthly cost is 3-66 percent lower.

title: Software Engineering LLMs: Why We Need Them and How Software Engineering Helps Build Them
finding: Capability-focused training of a 92B coding model on refactoring data raises RefactorBench by 18.00 points and SWE-Bench Verified by 4.97 points under OpenCode.

title: ThinkLocoManip: A Whole-Body Control Agentic Harness for Legged Loco-Manipulation
finding: An interleaved reason-and-act legged robot harness reaches 77 percent success on long-horizon loco-manipulation, more than twice the strongest plan-then-act baseline at 37.1 percent.

title: CTXAgent - Self-Controlled Context Management of LLM Agents
finding: Letting frontier models decide when and what to compact matches Claude Code on task success at 34 percent lower cost than its explicit 200k-window setup, with Claude Opus 5.5.

title: Rethinking Verification in Agent Harnesses
finding: Independent review by a critic raises accuracy 5.9-9.5 points on Terminal-Bench and 3.9-6.6 on SWE-bench Verified across seven frontier coding models, at 1.00-1.25 times baseline cost.

title: AT-AT: Automatic Tool Optimization from Agent Traces
finding: An agentic optimizer rewrites shared tool descriptions and implementations from past agent traces, reaching the highest task completion in two domains at lower cost than baselines.

title: Harness-Model Collaboration for Long-Horizon Continual Learning
finding: Combining retrieved experience cards with parameter updates outperforms harness-only and model-only adaptation under within-domain and cross-domain shifts, improving retention and adaptation.

title: MedAdaptAgent: An Automatic Harness for Adapting Medical Imaging Models to New Sites
finding: An automatic harness adapts medical imaging models to new sites; 20 local annotations raise mean segmentation Dice from 0.483 to 0.774 across 10 transfers, with no harmful replacements.

title: How Do Coding-Agent Harnesses Self-Evolve? An Empirical Study of Retrospective Adaptation
finding: Of seven evaluations where the targeted problem recurred, two self-proposed harness changes eliminated the targeted action, one reduced it and four showed no reduction.

title: PatentAgentBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents with Professional Patent Task Suites
finding: A 510-instance benchmark across eight patent task suites; seven language models in four agent harnesses still struggle to identify novelty, assess risk and understand practitioner intent.

title: CoSA: The Conflict of Skills Attack in Real-World LLM Agent Ecosystems
finding: Added skills capped at 5 percent of each pool raise policy violations from 35.02 to 58.45 percent across five models; a harness-level guard cuts recruiting-task violations to 6.67 percent.

title: Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models
finding: Co-Design Bench grades 273 real-user coding revision tasks; the strongest of ten endpoints passes 69.9 percent of criteria per task but fully satisfies only 26.4 percent of tasks.

title: V$^3$AST-Bench: Verifiable, Valid, and Versatile Safety Evaluation for Coding Agents
finding: A safety benchmark of 212 risk tasks finds a frontier agent causes verified harm on 20.9 percent of tasks; agents of similar competence differ markedly in safety across harnesses.

title: RSIV-Harness: A Recursive Self-Improvement Harness Framework for Open-Domain Conversational Text-to-Visualization
finding: A recursive self-improvement harness revises its own surroundings from failure traces with model weights fixed, raising executability 28.02 points and chart structure 34.01 points in one round.

title: RepoTrace: Improving Requirement Tracing in Multi-Round Agent Interactions
finding: A requirement-tracing repository harness raises mean per-round reward by 19.99 points on GLM-5.2 and 10.22 points on Claude Code.

title: MarkovSim: an LLM Agent Harness with Bounded Context for Long-Horizon Computational Simulation
finding: A finite-element simulation harness with bounded context passed 16 of 18 runs on six benchmark problems and kept its context bounded in every run, regardless of length.

title: Hierarchical Skill Evolution for Coding Agent
finding: Skills distilled hierarchically from coding trajectories, with 10 skills evolved on SWE-Gym, improve coding performance in all evaluated settings and transfer across harnesses and models.

title: Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
finding: Three simple harnesses that prescribe no model calls beat five published root-cause agents on top-one ranking accuracy, 65-77 percent against 16-53 percent, on every model both families ran.

title: A Unified Arena for LLM Agents across Diverse Eurogame
finding: Across ten Eurogames and 1,032 matches, the same model performs differently across four execution harnesses, and competitive advantage does not reliably translate into lower token cost.

title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
finding: A frontier multimodal model alone is competitive on robot manipulation but weaker on long-horizon tasks; adding a post-trained policy to its harness matches the strongest policy at lower token cost.

title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
finding: Ten frontier models often raised a spending cap on their own by harvesting one-time passcodes; the paper proves when a human approval protocol survives a compromised harness.

title: Before the First Edit? Measuring When Coding-Agent Guidance Actually Arrives
finding: Guidance preceded every first source change in a local Qwen2.5-Coder 14B study, but 15 of 76 arms changed Python source and the study missed its 20-arm coverage target.

title: Context Is a Pipeline, Not a Window: Information Attrition in LLM Agent Harnesses
finding: A third of tool results (3,827 of 11,189) were cut before the model saw them, all malformed; the cost first appeared as 43 percent more tool calls, not wrong answers.

title: kw-bench: Breaking Frontier Harnesses on Real-World Tasks
finding: On DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, two model-agnostic harnesses scored 0.542 and 0.528 and two lab harnesses scored 0.00; on Claude Opus 5.5 two harnesses scored 0.9986 and 1.000.

title: CoHARL: Co-Evolving Agent Policies and Executable Harnesses with Reinforcement Learning
finding: Co-evolving a shared policy with a population of executable harnesses reaches a 27.6 percent resolved rate on SWE-rebench, 6.4 points above harness-only search.

title: A Harness Reducing over-Defensive Writing in Agents by Isolating Objections
finding: Separating reviewer, filter and writer contexts cut defensive propositions from 59 to 2 across 25 business drafts, a 96.61 percent reduction, while source-claim retention rose from 80.35 to 93.12 percent.

title: When the Critic Falls Behind: Co-Evolving Rubrics and Harnesses for Continual Agent Self-Improvement
finding: Co-evolving rubrics with harnesses outperforms strong harness-evolution baselines, most clearly on unseen held-out tasks, with adaptive rubric prioritization tracking shifting weaknesses.

title: Learning to Code the World: Harness Evolution for Compositional 3D Reconstruction
finding: A harness evolved for a small open-source model reconstructs scenes 32.3 percent better than GPT-5.6-Sol, with 59.8 percent lower deployment cost and no parameter updates.

title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
finding: Comparing harnesses with a fixed model mixes what each offers with how well the model uses it; reordering observation fields drops a trained model from 85.0 to 19.2 percent success.

title: Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?
finding: Sparse search-time feedback sustains productive scaffold evolution; a method using about half the evaluation cells reaches higher mean performance than full evaluation in most settings.

title: Evaluating and improving AI agents for sequencing protocol understanding
finding: Frontier agents reconstruct sequencing libraries approximately but not exactly; switching the language model changes performance more than switching harnesses, a significant gap only for molecular-state reconstruction.

title: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns
finding: A multi-agent harness checks each claim against the measured reliability of its records before release; on perovskite solar cells it recovers known trends and anticipates devices reported a year later.

title: El Agente Quntur: Agentic Active-Space Selection for CASSCF
finding: Agentic active-space selection cuts mean absolute excitation-energy error 48 percent against six fixed protocols, but computational traces vary substantially across runs, even for the same molecule.

title: 3DCodeEdit: Benchmarking Instruction-Guided 3D Program Editing
finding: Across 17 models, instruction-guided 3D program editing succeeds 37 percent of the time; a separate reviewer model's feedback helps most, letting a 27B model beat a 2.8T-parameter model's single-shot rate.

title: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video
finding: A single 9B policy trained on over 130 thousand examples in an agent harness is comparable to Claude Opus 5 while using nearly 33 times fewer tokens per output minute.

title: Implicit Minor Detection from Multi-Turn Dialogue in High-Risk AI Interactions: A Constrained Self-Evolving LLM Harness
finding: A constrained self-evolving harness improves average precision and minor-class F1 score by 7.60 and 6.37 points over direct inference with the same model family on 8,328 Chinese dialogues.

title: How Deterministic SAST and AI Security Agents Divide the Work: Coverage, Harness Policy and Cost in Snyk VulnBench 2.0
finding: Static analysis and Claude Code together found 101 of 108 vulnerabilities; without Claude Code's review policy, the same model found 16 instead of 9 in the policy-restricted classes.

title: Context Compaction for World Models
finding: A harness that compacts context lets world models retrieve rooms up to 4 times beyond their context window without retraining; sliding-window attention loses most retrieval when dreaming.

title: VEvo-Harness: Causally-Guarded Self-Evolving Harness for Agentic Image Generation
finding: A self-evolving harness for image generation admits only causally valid skill patches via counterfactual replay and rivals proprietary image generators in its reported results.

title: Ask to Evolve: A Unified Harness for Lifelong Embodied Navigation with Hybrid Action Space and Persistent Memory
finding: A navigation harness with hybrid actions, active help-seeking and persistent memory reaches 100 percent first-visit success on four 100-episode sets, averaging 1.87 interactions per episode.

title: KARMA: Training-Free Knowledge-Atomic Harness Evolution for Industrial Advertising Agents
finding: Validation-gated knowledge edits without weight changes raise hold-out score from 30.19 to 39.15 across 18 domain-model settings, and evolved knowledge transfers across domains.

title: HEMO: Harness Self-Evolution for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization
finding: A self-evolving harness that revises its own search logic, operators and parent selection outperforms evolutionary, neural and language-model baselines across eight multi-objective tasks.

title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
finding: A report arguing video generation and world models both become agent harnesses; it covers agentic video generation, agentic world modeling and self-improvement, and lists evaluation as an open challenge.

title: MetaVul: Agentic Harness Discovery for Vulnerability Detection
finding: A self-improving harness search lifts pairwise vulnerability detection up to 23.3 points on validation and 25.8 on held-out pairs for frontier and small models; harnesses also transfer to other models.

title: Mage-VL-Cowork: A Full Training Recipe to Learn Hybrid Computer Use From Evolved Harnesses
finding: A 4B computer-use model trained on trajectories from evolved teacher harnesses reaches 66.0 percent on OSWorld-Verified, the state of the art at its size.

title: Does Recursive Knowledge Construction Help Agents Verify Consensus Claims in Science?
finding: A harness keeping its evidence state outside the model's context ranks in the top three on 718 consensus claims and beats general-purpose agent harnesses significantly.

title: Towards Portable Specification of the Agent Harness
finding: Proposes splitting the harness into eight functional components and a portable record of which model ran in which harness, because harness choice shifts reported scores several-fold.

title: Training LLM Agents to Automate LLM Post-Training with RSI-Dojo
finding: Executable model-training environments built from research papers let fine-tuned open models gain 8.74 and 16.87 PostTrainBench points; the 35B model matches frontier models on that benchmark.

title: Context as Infrastructure: Knowledge Compilation for Retrieval in Agentic Systems with Harnesses
finding: In a competent search harness, one model answers 85 percent of BrowseComp-Plus; a navigation tree cuts query tokens 91 percent when evidence suffices and adds 1.9 percent when it fails.

title: From Evaluation to Evolution: Benchmarking Image Editing and Evolving Image Models
finding: Among 15 image-editing configurations GPT-Image-2 leads single-image editing at 4.076; a harness-driven evolution lifts FLUX.2 [dev] Overall from 1.083 to 3.517 on its Top-5 targets.

title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
finding: Harness evolution raises a teacher's RoboTwin success from 33.4 to 63.6 percent, and a distilled 4B student reaches 62.8 percent in the same harness, close to its teacher.

title: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
finding: Without updating any weights, an evolved harness raises average success from 9.7 to 43.3 percent on unseen scenes and from 12.7 to 40.2 percent on unseen tasks.

title: Decentralized Multi-Agent Coordination and Communication in Shared Codebases
finding: Parallel coding agents fall behind a single-agent oracle on contradictory tasks, from 62 to 16 percent for Claude Code with Opus 4.8; a communication channel recovers only a small part.

title: Circuit Oracle: Automating Attribution Graph Analysis via Natural-Language Queries
finding: A language model with a multi-agent harness answers questions about attribution graphs; it reaches 78.2 plus or minus 2.4 percent on spurious-feature detection, and results hold across five runs.

title: Exo: An Architecture for Self-Improving Systems at Runtime
finding: A runtime letting agents edit their own harness during work cuts held-out model cost 35-61 percent on AppWorld and SREGym with comparable correctness.

title: Auriga Technical Report: A Task-Agnostic Agent Harness for Zero-Shot Embodied Manipulation
finding: A task-agnostic harness ranks first on RoboDojo with 57.7 percent success, more than double the reference harness on the same model, and keeps first place under scene randomization.

title: Latent Harness: Compiling Agent Behaviors into Post-Block Activation Shifts
finding: Compiling a harness into a small activation shift recovers its gain in 8 of 10 preregistered settings, using 0.03-0.05 percent of parameters and adding no tokens at inference.

title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
finding: An open-weight Qwen model in a unified robot-use harness scores 31.39 on RoboDojo, above a published GPT-6 Astra result of 28.97 and many vision-language-action baselines.

title: RSI-Env: An Open-Ended Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement of Agents
finding: Qwen3.8-27B with a minimal harness, improving itself without benchmark feedback, raises GPQA Diamond accuracy from 65.2 to 73.2 percent and AIME 2026 accuracy from 53.3 to 56.7 percent.

title: RECEIPT: Measuring and Repairing the Return Assumption of LLM Agents in Web Service Operations
finding: Harness input handling makes 11.5% of tested commands report success without acting; RECEIPT cuts false success claims by 73.5% across five models.

title: CertClaim: Towards Certified Model-Claim Verification for Coding-Agent Services
finding: Model-claim audits must treat each authorized deployment as part of the claim; CertClaim tests a coding-agent service against all of them, avoiding false accusations.

title: ParetoSaddler: Pareto-Guided Optimization of Agent Harnesses for Quality and Cost
finding: Optimizing harnesses for quality and cost together: ClawMark quality rises from 70.86% to 81.35% while cost falls from $1.17 to $1.01 per task.

title: Harvesting SWE Benchmarks from Wild Vibe Coding Sessions
finding: Harness choice shifts first-try pass rate by up to 8.4 points for the same model across 12 model-harness setups; best setup reaches 39.3% on 242 tasks.

title: HLSClaw: Bringing Vibe Coding to High-Level Synthesis through Skill-Based Agentic Harness
finding: A skill-based agent harness for high-level synthesis reaches 39.12x geometric-mean latency speedup, beating ScaleHLS by 1.98x and Claude Code and Codex by 1.86x and 1.70x.

title: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?
finding: Harness self-evolution on one task erodes earlier gains: a SWE-Bench score of 94.0% falls to 32.0% after later FeatureBench evolution, a 66% relative drop.

title: Do Agents Still Follow the Rules? Benchmarking Rule Compliance under Agent Context Compaction
finding: Compaction rarely deletes an operating rule; most post-compaction violations occur while the rule remains, and retaining a rule still violates more than twice as often as full history.

title: DeliverBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Delivering Realistic Multi-Stage Professional Projects
finding: Best of seven model-harness systems scores 65.0/100 on final project delivery and passes 50.0% of subtasks; task-level skill does not simply compose into delivery.

title: Optimize the Harness, Not the Model: Fitting a Minimal Agent to a Self-Hostable LLM for Investigative Analysis
finding: A minimal harness fitted to a self-hostable model reaches an 83.8% pass rate, within 1.2 points of the Claude Code SDK baseline, at two orders of magnitude smaller.

title: El Agente Fármaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery
finding: A drug-discovery agent harness with a provenance memory scores highest on a 22-task benchmark, with lower median token use than plain tool calls and Codex.

title: EvoGroup: A Self-Evolving Harness for Group Agents in Shared Contexts
finding: A self-evolving harness raises first-try pass rate on held-out EverMemBench from 71.07% to 89.58%, above human-designed Claude Code at 85.83%.

title: From Benchmarks to Behaviors: A Framework for Auditing AI Agents
finding: Concise user memories shift which sources an agent cites: a publisher-preference memory raises that publisher's inclusion in the top three cited sources by 33-39 points.

title: ScienceVision: Can AI Observe and Reason Like a Scientist?
finding: Native 3D artifacts via an agent harness beat rendered 2D images for every model, by 17.2 points on average; best mean answer score is 0.53 of 1.

title: DoGNAVY-Exploit: Harnessing Parallel Open-Weight Agents for Stage-Aware Vulnerability Exploitation
finding: Open-weight GLM-5.2 in a parallel multi-agent harness solves 79 ExploitGym tasks against 39 for public Claude Code baselines; GLM-5.3 solves 157 against 130.

title: Harness-S: Learning from Sibling Harnesses for Generalizable Agent Training
finding: Training a policy on failures rescued by sibling harnesses beats policy-only training on AppWorld, SWE-Gym and DBBench when run back in the original harness.

title: Goal-Driven Autonomous Optical Experimentation via a Self-Recursive Hardware-Software Harness
finding: Agents revise optical hardware and software from physical measurements; one color-matching setup cuts one color difference from 19.756 to 1.211, in one configuration only.

title: FreeForm Harness: A Mobile-Native Agent Harness for Open and Composable Extensions
finding: A mobile agent harness with a uniform plugin contract lets independently authored extensions compose; the Android prototype runs, but the abstract reports no quantitative results.

title: Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
finding: Offline-learned guidance decides when a running agent's harness should change; reaches 81.00% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 44.44% on DeepSWE 1.1 with GPT-5.6-Terra.

title: SlackBench: Benchmarking Agents on Collaborative Projects Grounded in Real Code Repositories
finding: Across 33 frontier models and agent harnesses on 140 collaborative-workplace queries, the best system scores around 80% and most agents score below 66%.

title: Beyond the Agent Harness: Boundary Criteria for Software-Factory Orchestration - A Single-Operator Case Study
finding: Boundary criteria assign agent mechanisms to harness, factory or domain layers; two model coders agreed on all 26 mechanism layers, but the case is preliminary and human coders untested.

title: SleuthVLM: Do We Really Need Audio-in-Video for Omni Video Understanding?
finding: A harness drives a vision model that never hears audio, using transcripts; it averages 75.0% across four omni benchmarks, 2.6 points above Gemini 3.8 Flash.

title: The Harness Is the Model: Agent Scaffolding Changes a Fixed LLM's Compliance with Banking Conduct Rules, Unevenly Across Models
finding: Same four open-weight models in five harnesses: harness moved one model's correct-case rate 11.5 points, from first to last place; 26% of violations were hidden from transcript review.

title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
finding: A search over complete harness candidates reaches 69.48% average on six benchmarks, 10.89 points above initial harnesses and 3.95 points above Meta-Harness, with 15 attempts.

title: SUMONE: A Simple and Efficient Summarizer for Plug-and-Play Agent Memory
finding: A trained summarizer cuts estimated inference cost about 78% on DeepSearchQA and 75% on SWE-bench Verified, with a 0.04 absolute score drop, and transfers across agent harnesses.

title: Trace2Eval: Contextualized Evaluation of Coding Agents from Real-World Traces
finding: Benchmarks built from real user traces; rubric feedback raises artifact scores by a mean 10.05 points across 19 model-harness configurations, up to 19.28 for one.

title: WISE: An Agentic Framework for Whole-page Multimodal Search Experience Attribution
finding: An agentic diagnosis framework with harness and model policy optimization reaches 75.20% end-to-end accuracy on a 35B open-weight model and gains across model scales.

title: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis
finding: Minimal agent harnesses beat direct image generation on 90 long-context multi-reference tasks, while a planning-reflection workflow gives harness-dependent gains.

title: How Do AI Agents Waste Your Money?
finding: Removing 41-46% of model reasoning as waste largely preserves task performance; waste varies more across tasks and agent settings than across models.

title: Take It From Here: Evaluating Coding Agents On Project Takeover
finding: Across six model-harness configurations, complete project-takeover delivery is 4.95% under full history; with correct target states it reaches 8.11%, and target-test success stays 9.01%.

title: Req2Rust: A Requirements-Guided Agent Harness for Project-Level C++-to-Rust Migration
finding: Requirements-guided C++-to-Rust migration harness lifts test pass rate from 69.5% to 91.9% on general projects and 45.4% to 87.9% on OpenHarmony modules versus a Claude Code baseline.

title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
finding: Claude Opus 5.5 with Claude Code completes 9 of 46 real-world tasks alone and 39 with HEELO through its Model Context Protocol server; GPT-6.1 Sol goes from 9 to 35.

title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
finding: Evolved harness agents gain new tasks while losing old ones; one reliability gain of 5.2 points came with ten lost tasks, and most reliability gains also raise deployment cost.

title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
finding: Proposes meta access, a permissioned view that lets a chat assistant see and change its own interface, with a ladder of levels; prototype only, no measurements reported.

title: Divide, Diagnose, and Compose: Optimizing Agentic Pipelines and Harnesses
finding: Decomposed optimization of agentic pipelines raises average task performance by 2.58 points, cuts inference cost by 4.30% and end-to-end latency by 42.45% versus the best baseline.

title: Flex-RSI: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement of Frontier Agents
finding: Agents improving their own harness: self-improvement helps most when the agent builds its own solution; open-weight models fall furthest behind where outputs need strict checks.

title: Frontier3DBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for 3D Creation across Objects, Scenes, and Interactive Open Worlds
finding: Across 11 model-harness setups on 145 3D creation tasks, the best overall score is 66.02/100; reconstruction from references trails text-driven generation in every configuration.

title: When Routine Operations Break Architectural Pattern Relationships in LLM Agent Harnesses
finding: Routine operations silently break architectural relationships in five released harnesses: after a plugin was reapplied, policy stopped evaluating edits while all plugins stayed active.

title: Authorization Drift in LLM Agents: Evaluating Boundary Compliance in Multi-Step Tool Use
finding: Across 13 models in three frameworks, greater capability brings greater authorization drift, with frontier models at 0.43 to 0.61; 86.18% of tasks still allow a clean-success trajectory.

title: BOXBOX: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Long-Running Performance Optimization
finding: Agent-triggered harness revision during a long run reaches a speedup of 1.70x at four hours, versus 1.54x for the strongest offline baseline.

title: Can AI Agents Reliably Optimize Computational Chemistry Codes?
finding: A worker agent and a separate controller agent optimize chemistry codes, cutting computational cost while preserving numerical accuracy; the largest speedups come from TDDFT calculations.

title: LongCapHarness: Capability-Guided Auto-Harnessing for Long-Context Reasoning
finding: Auto-harnessing a Llama3-8B model without data synthesis or post-training beats synthesis baselines on HELMET and RULER at under half their estimated training cost.

title: InfoOrgBench: Can Agents Turn Scattered Information into Coherent Hierarchies?
finding: Across 45 model-harness systems, model choice moves scores about 27 points while each harness changes them by under one point on average; best system scores 83.2 of 100.

title: REINS: A Self-Evolving Agent Harness for Real-Time Trajectory Planning
finding: A trajectory-planning harness keeps the model out of most decisions via rule memory; reaches 98%+ compliance, nearly 50% fewer collisions and 1.9-4.6 ms latency in simulation and real world.

title: DeepFinance: Can AI Diligence a $100MM Deal?
finding: Benchmark of 21 private-equity and investment-banking tasks: the best of 22 configurations satisfies 57.6% of expert rubric criteria; frontier models often compute correctly from wrong inputs.

title: Agent Self-Improvement with Frozen Weights: The Added Value and Limits of Failure Traces
finding: Notes learned from failures add 4.0 points over notes made without failures for a 9-billion-parameter model; a matched trial-and-keep process delivers about 60% of the total gain.

title: JoMoHa: Joint Model--Harness Optimization with Reinforcement Learning
finding: Jointly training a harness generation policy and a task policy with reinforcement learning averages 70.3% on ALFWorld, WebShop and DBBench, reaching 97.0% on ALFWorld.

title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
finding: Text-only memory written by a strong multimodal model lifts its success on EBench from 46.7% to 81.7% under direct control, and transfers unchanged to weaker models.

title: InfraRSI: Harnessing Recursive Self-Improvement for Training Infrastructure
finding: An agentic harness for distributed training reaches up to 2.75x speedup and lifts mean hardware utilization from 17.4% to 30.0% across four workloads, beating tuners and coding agents.

title: Harness Matters: Measuring and Dissecting Security Resilience in Web Agents
finding: Harness and backend model both significantly change web agent security; existing harnesses stay vulnerable to typical attacks, sometimes unsafe even without attack content.

title: EmoHarness: Boosting Multimodal Emotion Understanding with Meta-Harness Evolving
finding: A harness around small multimodal students raises emotion recognition by 7.6-13.4 points; transcripts and prosody supply most of the boost, while evolved edits add at most 0.95.

title: Correct First, Fast Second: What a Local 7B Code Model Can and Cannot Do for GPU Kernel Optimization
finding: A local 7B code model with naive agent scaffolding scores 3% correct, below zero-shot's 30%; best-of-n sampling under execution checks lifts correctness from 3% to 33%.

title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
finding: Harness-side choices change cost up to 2.6 times on one model and task; a platform cutting token use across Claude Code and Codex saves up to 35% without accuracy loss.

title: Reconfigurable Action Theories: A Formal Foundation for Dynamically Composable Agent Harnesses
finding: Formal action theory where actions load and unload harness modules, with proofs of a unique next configuration and order independence; experiments compare the model with three official harnesses.

title: Say Shibboleth: Fingerprinting the LLMs and Harnesses Behind Agentic Attacks
finding: Honeypot traps identify attacker models and harnesses from telemetry: 90% average top-1 accuracy across 15 candidate models and 92% harness accuracy across four harnesses.

title: SciMARS: Multi-Agent Recursive Self-Improvement for Closed-Loop Scientific Discovery
finding: Adapting a multi-agent scientific harness with shared memory raises GPT-6-Astra's solved attempts from 8 to 12 of 18 on Autonomous Science Bench, versus the base team.

title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
finding: Workflows authored by Claude Opus 5.5 substantially improve weaker executing models on hard tasks; no single configuration wins across the 145 tasks in eight domains.

title: Teaching the Harness: Student-Aware Skill Transfer for LLM Agents
finding: A stronger teacher writing skills for a fixed student lifts task success to 86.46% across four runs, versus 75.00% for the untaught student; skills enter only if they help.

title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks
finding: Veritas generates task verifiers that agree better with official verdicts than seven other harnesses on all four execution-scored benchmarks, and improves 9 of 12 harness-benchmark pairs.

title: OpenRE-Bench: A Benchmark Harness for Multi-Agent Requirements Engineering with Mined GitHub Issues
finding: Open benchmark harness for multi-agent requirements frameworks: shared run contract, issue-mining pipeline, pinned environment and a 651-test suite for reproducible comparison.

title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
finding: Deterministic guards stop every attack fixture with zero false positives in 12.7 microseconds; a small local model judge refuses 98.3% of benign work at 142.3 ms.

title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing
finding: A verifiable traffic class for agent traffic demotes spoofed flows; in real agent harnesses on a congested link, router queueing took 13% to 63% of task time.

title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
finding: Evaluation harnesses for analytics agents: 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold; trace-based judging reaches a 0.90 precision-recall balance, while text-only judging makes five times more false alarms.

title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
finding: Most harness-based continual learners learn less than a plain demonstration cache across tested models, and gain little on unseen tasks, where weight-based learning gains substantially.

title: Auriga: Harness-Governed LLM Agents for Effective Throughput Optimization in Execute-Order-Validate Permissioned Blockchains
finding: Harness-governed language model agents tune Hyperledger Fabric settings and schedule conflict-free transactions, lifting effective throughput up to 6.0 times over default Fabric and 2.0 times over the best baseline.

title: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving
finding: A validated self-improving harness raises pass rate across four frontier models by 3.0-19.6% relative to native harnesses while cutting recorded model calls by 46.9%.

title: JoyFrontBench: Evaluating Front-End Coding Agents through Goal-Oriented Acceptance Contracts
finding: Front-end agents average 87.69% task score but only 51.52% application success under OpenHands; model rankings change across harnesses, and success varies across repeated runs.

title: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy
finding: Across six models and six harnesses, EvoX reaches 56.2% success, about 3.0 points above the average of the other harnesses; its gain reaches 10.7 points on GLM-5.3.

title: guardscope: Measuring Which Actions Runtime Controls Check in LLM Agent Systems
finding: A framework measures which of an agent's 15 action paths a runtime control can check, against kernel ground truth, so coverage claims by control products become verifiable.

title: Knowledge in the Harness, Reliability in the Weights: Teacher-Free Co-Evolution of an LLM Agent
finding: A 12B open model writing its own rules gains 12.5 points on retail and 19.5 on airline after two rounds, and beats the reference agent by 11.8 and 8.0 points.

title: Verify by Doing: Co-Evolving Agent Execution and Evaluation without External Feedback
finding: Actor and Evaluator harnesses co-evolve without external feedback, gaining 3.3, 4.1 and 2.3 points over the strongest baselines on three task suites.

title: AgentTorrent: A Dataset of Context and Harness Engineering Artifacts on GitHub
finding: Dataset of 62,374 configuration artifacts and 27,593 planning documents from 10,944 GitHub projects, linking harness configuration files to commits that credit an AI tool.

title: Bug Finding With Agentic Symbolic Execution
finding: An agentic harness drives symbolic execution over 11 Python web applications, executing 81% of contracted functions versus 4.5% without it, and finds 1,050 reproduced bugs.

title: MULTILOOP: Evolving Multi-Agent Harnesses for Complex Information-Seeking Tasks
finding: Automated harness optimization on 10 training samples raises a multi-agent harness's accuracy 4.6% over base and 3.2% over the best single agent, though orchestration failures persist.

title: BWM-Forge: Agentic World Programming for Embodied Intelligence
finding: A coding agent writes Blender scene programs that drive a video model; on 15 robot tasks it scores higher than LingBot-World Base Cam on most quality measures, except dynamic degree.

title: Shared Item-Level Error Limits the Aggregation of Small Language Models in Fermi Estimation
finding: Across 15 open-weight models of 3B-72B, teams of thirty cut one agent's error by a median 1.7%, because most error is shared per item; unbiased draws would cut it 74-79%.

title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
finding: A harness that guides language models through video generation, selection and repair releases 100K training videos and two evaluation datasets; no headline score is given.

title: ControlHarbor: A Benchmark for Control Design by Coding Agents
finding: Three frontier coding agents reach the reinforcement-learning return on every control task but only in a minority of sessions; their controllers usually fail under perturbations.

title: AnalogLayoutWorld: An Open Benchmark for Agentic Analog Layout Design
finding: Across 13 model-harness setups on 40 analog circuit layout tasks, 91.1% of attempts produce layouts, but only 23.0% meet the acceptance criteria.

title: Interpreting Coding Agents Through Their Behavioral Trajectories
finding: Across 143,209 trajectories from 125 agent configurations, agents with similar solve rates differ in how they explore, edit and test; scaffold choice shifts those behaviors systematically.

title: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs
finding: Benchmark of 48 kernels on Ascend accelerator chips, using real workload data types and shapes, plus a Speedup-Token Score that weighs speedup against token cost.

title: OCTAVE: A Capability-Resolved Benchmark for End-to-End HTML5 Game Generation
finding: Across 11 model-harness combinations, generated HTML5 games reach 33.2% Completeness and 32.5% Richness; 19.9% of generation records fail static gates or lack artifacts.

title: Vision-as-a-Tool: Visual Harness for Multimodal Agentic Coding
finding: Treating a general vision model as a callable tool improves visual fidelity and geometric accuracy for both text-only and multimodal coding agents on image-to-HTML, SVG and 3D tasks.

title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
finding: Position paper: a foundation model with an embodied harness forms the decision core of agentic robotics; it proposes an evaluation framework, with no measurements reported.

title: HerAgent: A Block-Level Checkpointing Harness for Coding-Agent Environment Setup
finding: A block-level setup harness beats six prior agents on four environment-setup datasets, rising from 52.0% to 85.0% on Installamatic-Bench and from 46.3% to 70.4% on SetupBench.

title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
finding: Learned compression and steering programs for reinforcement-learning harnesses beat a fixed harness in most settings, for models from 1.5B to 8B on CodeSearch, ALFWorld and BIRD SQL.

title: A Compositional Theory of Agent Harnesses
finding: No abstract was supplied; only the title, a compositional theory of agent harnesses, is known, so no claim can be checked here.

title: Auditable Authorization for LLM Agents: Empirical Evidence Across Model, Harness, and Workflow Layers
finding: Human approval fails at execution boundaries: the paired model panel leaves 7 of 300 approvals unfinished despite zero denied effects; CrewAI restoration omits 336 of 672 approvals.

title: One Run Is Not Enough: Reminding a small Gemma 4 coding agent of its last finding made no measurable difference in a paired test
finding: A reminder of the last finding made no measurable difference over 98 paired tasks: 47 solved with it, 48 without (-1.0 points); 19% of tasks flipped between identical runs.

title: Program Distillation: Transferring LLM Capability from System 2 to System 0
finding: Program distillation moves language model knowledge into CPU-only student programs; the strongest model scores 0.728 normalized mean, above proximal policy optimization at 0.656 on 27 tasks.

title: CRAFT: A Robot-Agent Harness with Scope-Aware Adaptation
finding: A scope-aware robot harness asks fewer questions than language model agents with persistent memory, but some of those agents succeed more often after requirements change; all results are simulated.

title: Anatomy of an Agent Harness: Decisions, Invariants and Corner Cases
finding: Of 83 invariant clauses for agent harnesses, 56 are tested, 12 believed and 15 open; the checklist passes 11 of one author's harness items, fails 14, leaves 5 untested.

title: Harness Engineering for Language Agents: The Harness Layer as Control, Agency, and Runtime
finding: Argues the harness layer deserves explicit study; audits 63 works, finds a visibility gap between papers and engineering notes, and proposes HARNESSCARD for reporting harness configuration.

title: Harness Engineering for LLM Agents: A Survey of Harness Component Taxonomy, Evaluation, and Model–Harness Coevolution
finding: Surveys harness components, proposes a two-stage evaluation logic for net benefit, and says capability support migrates into model weights while governance stays external.

title: Positioning MBSE System Architectures in the Agent Harness Towards Automated Product Development: A Scoping Review
finding: Scoping review of 329 full-text papers on agents in product development, asking whether the system architecture from model-based systems engineering serves as harness context and state.

title: Agent Harness for Large Language Model Agents: A Survey
finding: Survey defines an agent harness as six components and classifies 23 systems; production-ready systems consistently implement all six. Cites studies showing order-of-magnitude reliability gains from harness redesign alone.

title: From Harness Optimization to Recursive Self-Improvement: A Survey of Language Model Agents
finding: Survey of harness optimization across coding, reasoning, embodied and visual tasks; finds cases where added tools and context fail to help and calls for attribution and reliable evaluation.

title: Where the Harness Meets the Physical World: A Survey of the Physical Agentic Harness
finding: Surveys over 200 embodied robot harness works; reviewed benchmarks give limited evidence of individual runtime contributions, especially execution governance and persistent evolution.

title: Harness-Aware Evaluation of LLM Agents: Systems, Benchmarks, and Protocols
finding: Survey proposing a four-factor evaluation framework (model, harness, environment, evaluator) because changing the harness around a fixed model can alter performance and reverse model rankings.

title: Agent Harness Engineering: A Survey
finding: Surveys 171 public harness entries, classifies 138 with a seven-layer taxonomy, and holds that harness design and model capability jointly determine agent performance.

title: Agent Systems with Harness Engineering
finding: Review of harness components (workflows, memory, skills, orchestration) that argues harness and model should be jointly optimized; a capable model lets the harness run workflows a weaker reasoner cannot.

title: Harness Engineering Can Make Small Language Models Explore Like Large Language Models
finding: Small Gemma 4 31B in a multi-worker harness covers 51.9% of analytical moves versus 30.2% for the best single-agent harness, matching a near-frontier model with about 14 times the parameters.

title: Task-Specialized Harness Refinement Across Financial Decision Tasks
finding: Fin-Harness evolves harness skills, roles and code against stage-local finance objectives in about 10 iterations; a multi-agent refinement loop beats single-agent variants on three financial tasks.

title: Meta-Harness: Beyond-Reward Agent Improvement from Language, Traces, and Sparse Task Outcomes
finding: Outer-loop coding agent rewrites harness code from traces; the discovered harness surpasses Terminus-KIRA on Claude Opus 4.6 and ranks first among reported Claude Haiku 4.5 agents on TerminalBench-2.

title: Meta-Harness: Post-Training Reliable Agent Systems via Harness Search
finding: Preliminary version of Meta-Harness: searches harness code using execution traces; the discovered harness surpasses Terminus-KIRA on Claude Opus 4.6.

title: From Failures to Evolution: Behavioral Rubrics for Agent Harness Evolution
finding: Rubric-guided harness evolution uses behavioral specifications between evidence and harness edits; it improves agent performance on SWE-bench Verified and AppWorld across three backbone models.

title: Data Canvas: A Provenance-Guided Harness for Agentic Data Engineering
finding: Data Canvas adds a provenance graph that traces errors to steps and replays only affected parts; it beats existing systems on standard deep research benchmarks in answer quality.

title: Harness Engineering: A Governance Framework for AI-Driven Software Engineering
finding: Conceptual framework defining a harness as a governance system with context, constraint and convergence dimensions, and noting practitioners at several organizations converged on similar practices.

title: Harness Alignment and Harness Drift: Why Intent, Unlike Correctness, Resists Automation
finding: Defines harness alignment, the continuous human-gated work of keeping an agent's harness matched to operator intent, and its failure mode, harness drift; provisional, with no efficacy evidence.

title: HELM: Harness Engineering for LLM Decision-Making Agents in Emergency Operations and Management
finding: Harness for a language model dispatcher in emergency operations: it processes raw incident and unit state and turns decisions into unit dispatches. No results shown.

title: What the Rapid Adoption of the "Harness" Metaphor in Artificial Intelligence Reveals About How We Conceptualize Human-AI Relations
finding: Argues the harness metaphor for artificial intelligence infrastructure carries assumptions about control, and that harness engineering may amplify automation bias and weaken critical scrutiny.

title: The Second Half of Harness Design: From Agents to 2 Bots
finding: Perspective arguing harness design moves from agents that run around tasks to persistent Bots that accumulate experience and act on message streams; it offers three predictions testable by 2029.

title: The Agent Loop: A Survey of Control Strategies, Skills, and Harnesses for LLM Agents
finding: Survey of agent loops, skills and harnesses, giving negative results equal weight: on intrinsic self-correction, elaborate agents versus simple pipelines, and the harness confound in evaluation.

title: The Harness as Control Surface: Connecting Institutional Obligations to Deployed Agent Actions
finding: Argues governance requirements can be enforced and evidenced at the agent harness; a conditional, unbuilt example gates two tools on an approval token. Not empirical validation.

title: Enabling Agentic PCG with Harness-Controlled Local Models
finding: Harness that constrains action formats, recovers unfinished replies and checks edits raises a local model's perfect-match rate on Zelda edits from 37.5% (24/64) to 100% (64/64).

title: From Prompt Engineering to Harnessing Engineering: A Unified CDIO-V Framework for Generative AI Systems
finding: Proposes a five-phase cycle (Concept, Design, Implement, Operate, Verify) for prompt, context and harness engineering, mapping benchmarks to unit tests and agent evaluations to acceptance tests.

title: Infrastructure Cash Flow Forecasting with a Bounded Agent Harness
finding: Verifies a bounded agent harness for cash-flow forecasting: 96 tests, 200 random configurations and a scripted five-request test; no live language model planner was evaluated.

title: Harnessing LLMs for Reliable Academic Supervision: A Comparative Study A Case Study in Harness Engineering
finding: Blind ten-rater study: a small GPT-4o-mini wrapped in a harness has a pooled mean of 4.08 against 1.23 for an unscaffolded GPT-5 chatbot; a two-by-two ablation finds harness gains largely model-invariant.

title: The Governance Operating System (GOS): A Physical Constitution for Sovereign Cyber-Physical AI Part X -Harness Engineering at the Scale of a Society: Domain Industrial Systems Under Owner Sovereignty
finding: Extends harness engineering from one machine to an industry and a society, aiming to keep domain systems under owner sovereignty; the opening text gives no measurements.

title: LLMs Should Not Judge: Rule-First Harnesses as the Governing Layer for Legal AI A Working Paper on Prompt Dependence, Harness Sovereignty, and Rule-Feedback Legal Intelligence
finding: Working paper arguing legal artificial intelligence should use rule-first harnesses that own constraints, verifiers and escalation, with language models only parsing, generating candidates and explaining. No measurements are given.

title: From Language Generators to Rule Learners: Rule-First Harnesses, Self-Learning, and Legal AI A Working Paper on Harness Sovereignty, Process Supervision, Expert Systems, and Legal Rule Execution
finding: Working paper proposing a rule-first harness in which external rules own constraints, verifiers and rewards, and structured feedback can become training signals. No measurements are given.

title: The Magnum Opus: The Detektor-Safe Harness - A Computational Protocol for Non-Collusive Autonomous Orchestration and ASI Alignment in Perishable Inventory Markets
finding: Models a yield paradox in agent-to-agent pricing of perishable inventory; proposes a harness splitting probabilistic agents from a rigid computational layer. Its reliability decay figures are parameterized, not asserted empirically.

title: The Honesty Harness: expert-directed, AI-executed empirical research with criteria frozen in advance and the burden of proof on positive results
finding: Expert freezes criteria in advance, an agent runs the study; a blinded challenge detected the strongest planted pattern in 19 of 20 series and flagged 24 of 500 empty series.
